EDITOR’S NOTE: This story has been updated with Schell’s victory.

Berdasarkan laporan, in 2020, sara schell was planning to move to london to study business after graduating high school in venezuela. On Thursday (Nov. 12), she won the Latin Grammy Award for songwriter of the year, and was also nominated for best pop song as a co-writer of Kany García’s “A La Niña Que Fui. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at 23, schell was not the only woman in the songwriter of the year category, but she was the only newcomer. She appeared alongside veterans like Edgar Barrera (who boasted 82 Latin Grammy nominations and 29 wins, including songwriter of the year for the past three years), Yoel Henríquez (who had garnered 23 nominations and three victories), Iván Gámez and Jenni Mosello (with a total of four nominations each).

Berdasarkan laporan, her credits listed by the latin recording academy included “a la niña que fui” by garcía, “ahí estabas tú” and “barco de papel” by fonseca, “bendito” by rawayana, “si te vas” by j balvin and jay wheeler (which reached no. 21 on the Hot 100), “Mercedes” by Becky G and Óscar Maydon (No. She’s also been behind chart hits like “Gabriela” by KATSEYE (No. 1 on Billboard‘s Latin Airplay chart), and “Vas a Quedarte” by Diego Torres and Manuel Carrasco. 1 on Regional Mexican Airplay) and “Ojos verdes” by Nicki Nicole (No. 1 on the Billboard Argentina Hot 100).

But how did this young woman from Barquisimeto go from wanting to study business to writing for major stars?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “in 2020, i graduated high school and then the pandemic hit, so we decided to move to mexico. When we arrived, I was supposed to go to London to study business because I had always said I wanted a career, but at that moment, all the universities were shut down, so we had to do what everyone else did: stay home and find something to do,” Schell tells Billboard Español in an interview from Spain during a break from a songwriting session. “I started posting covers and other things on Instagram, and that’s how I connected with several writers online, started doing Zoom sessions and writing together. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa schell’s musical training began at the age of four at the vicente emilio sojo conservatory, a prestigious institution founded in 1936 in barquisimeto, lara state, which works closely with venezuela’s national system of youth and children’s orchestras and choirs, a. a. There, she played the cello until she was 14 — a “super magical experience” that allowed her to travel to Peru and the U. representing her country. S. k. El Sistema. She also took piano and singing lessons.

Berdasarkan laporan, at 15, she wrote her first song, “sin ti o contigo,” which she uploaded to digital platforms, though it has since been taken down. “Then my heart was broken, and that’s when you start writing — because, you know, everyone needs therapy. “I remember I was falling asleep and a melody came to me, so I got up and went to the bathroom so I wouldn’t wake anyone up. What inspired me was that I was dating this guy, and we had broken up, so I started pouring it all out,” she says. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, but schell didn’t know people in her circle who could actually make a living from music, so she considered a more conventional university education necessary to “move forward. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, it was her father who advised her not to leave and to try her luck in music — “‘try what you’ve always loved,’ he told me, ‘give it two years'” — because his own parents hadn’t encouraged him to pursue his dreams. ’ So with me, he did the complete opposite. “My dad played music, did sports, he was great at everything, and my grandfather would say: ‘No, you’re going to study this. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, her first break came in 2024 with fuerza regida after a brief trip to miami, where she went with a demo of her songs and the idea of finding someone in the industry she’d heard about but “only knew his name was ben,” schell says. “At that moment, I didn’t know who Nir was. I told him: ‘Yeah, sure, let’s meet. ’ But I had no idea what I was walking into. There, she managed to have two or three songwriting sessions a day with different colleagues, and her name reached the ears of Nir Seroussi of Interscope, who contacted her to learn more about her work. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, upon meeting seroussi, schell says he immediately made her feel “like family,” and after listening to a couple of her songs, introduced her to ben tischker of wide eyed entertainment — the very same “ben” she had originally been looking for — who is now her manager. “It was incredible!” Schell says. “Then Nir helped me place a couple of songs, including my first one, ‘PXTXS,’ for Fuerza Regida.

Sebagaimana diketahui, originally written as a bolero, “pxtxs” — part of fuerza’s album dolido pero no arrepentido — is a heartbreak song about trying to overcome a breakup through excess and self-destruction. It turned out very beautiful. “It was a song that got a lot of attention at the time because it was a bolero that wasn’t vulgar but very raw,” says Schell. “I remember they replicated what I was doing with my voice on a guitar, and then they made it more regional. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa through interscope, the hit “gabriela” by katseye also came about. ’ I didn’t even know KATSEYE was such a big group. He said, ‘This one,’ sent it, and that was it,” she recalls. “It was quite strange because it happened very fast. “Normally songs take much longer to come out, but two months later the song was released and I started receiving tons of messages: ‘Congrats, congrats. They needed me to write a bridge in Spanish, and I remember sending Nir two options. And well, obviously it came out, and with everything that happened with the song, I’m very grateful to be part of it. ”.

Since then, she mentions Rawayana’s “Bendito” (“It was super fun to write, a blast”) and Kany García’s “A La Niña Que Fui” (“It was very beautiful how we connected”) among her favorite collaborations.

Berdasarkan laporan, in her august cover story interview with billboard español, garcía praised schell as a “super-talented” songwriter while recounting how this song, now competing for a latin grammy, came to be. (Its songwriting credits also include Rafa Arcaute, Nate Campany and Richi López).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i called her to write. But when you sit with creative people who are seeing the picture from outside, they see things that you don’t. And I told myself: ‘How beautiful it is that sometimes, as a songwriter, I think I have to do it all myself, that everything has to come from my head. I had melodies in my head, but nothing concrete… And she said to me — because it wasn’t me, it was her: ‘Hey, how about writing a song to your inner child?'” García recalled. “It gave me chills, because she didn’t know that the project was heading in that direction. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “just meeting her, and how i grasped what she wanted without her telling me,” says schell, “sometimes there’s this energy in the room that’s the most important, where the most magical songs come from, and i feel like we walked in and captured it right away. ”.

Although she has released some music as a singer in the past year — mostly collaborations with Sistek, Gonza Silva and LAGOS — Schell, currently signed to MPub and Wide Eyed Publishing, says her “calling” has always been “writing for others” and that she doesn’t plan to have a career as a performer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “from the moment we met sara, we recognized an exceptional talent in her,” daniela méndez varón, head of a&r at mpub, tells billboard. “Her artistic sensitivity, versatility and vision as a songwriter set her apart, but it’s her human qualities that make her even more special. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa as for how she found out about her latin grammy nominations, the songwriter recalls going to bed exhausted after a long day’s work and not even setting her alarm to catch the announcement. “But obviously, I was nervous,” she says. ’ I was like: ‘Oh my God. “I left my phone’s sound on, and I got a call from producer Héctor Mazzarri, who’s one of my best friends — also nominated this year, by the way — telling me: ‘Congratulations. ’ And I’m like: ‘What happened?’ ‘Songwriter of the Year. '”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meanwhile, her dad couldn’t be prouder: “he’s so happy. So he’s like: ‘I knew it from the beginning. ’ It’s very sweet. I mean, of course he could believe it. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when asked who she’d like to write songs with, schell doesn’t hesitate. “Franco De Vita. You know, being from Venezuela, I grew up listening to him, and it was the music I listened to most with my grandparents,” she says with a smile.

Berdasarkan laporan, founded in 2016 by filmmaker vincente disanti, womp stomp films has built a devoted following with its ambitious series of “friday the 13th” fan films. The saga began with DiSanti’s 2017 short “Never Hike Alone,” followed by the winter-set prequel “Never Hike in the Snow” in 2020. The feature-length sequel “Never Hike Alone 2” arrived in 2023, featuring “Friday the 13th Part VI: Jason Lives” actors Thom Mathews and Vincent Guastaferro reprising their original roles as Tommy Jarvis and Sheriff Rick Cologne.

Berdasarkan laporan, the “never hike alone” films have relied on crowdfunding campaigns to help finance their increasingly elaborate productions. The fan-supported approach has allowed DiSanti and his collaborators to expand the saga while making the finished films available to watch for free online.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, although the “never hike alone” films feature copyrighted characters, settings and storylines from the official “friday the 13th” franchise, womp stomp films operates independently of the studios that own the jason voorhees property. Diungkapkan bahwa "heartland" also stars john hawkes, garrett hedlund, jennifer nettles, and ross lynch in supporting roles, but chastain is the real draw here, and whether or not you saw or loved "other mommy," you should check this pick out. Sebagaimana diketahui, if you, like me, love dark and twisted thrillers, you're probably familiar with the name karin slaughter. Sebagaimana diketahui, the premise of "the good daughter" is enticing on its own: decades after a brutal and violent incident in the quinn family, sisters samantha and charlotte (byrne and fahy) still reside in their hometown of pikeville, georgia, with charlotte working in law enforcement. Sebagaimana diketahui, "the lord of the rings: the rings of power," which has been running since 2022, takes its lore from the appendices of j. Tolkien's massive fantasy tomes (but notably not Tolkien's "The Silmarillion" due to rights issues, so that has yet to be fully adapted). Berdasarkan laporan, i truly cannot believe a movie as delightfully weird and ambitious as "the end of oak street" got made in the first place, but i sure am happy that it did. (There's also a family dog, Starbuck, and don't worry — nothing bad happens to him. That's as close to a spoiler as I'll get. David Robert Mitchell ("It Follows," "Under the Silver Lake") helmed this ode to dinosaur movies, summer blockbusters, and 1980s Steven Spielberg classics, which stars Ewan McGregor as Greg Platt, Anne Hathaway as his wife and aspiring writer Denise, Maisy Stella as the couple's eldest child Audrey, and Christian Convery as their son and youngest Brian. ) The Platts are an everyday family with everyday problems — Greg is secretly working as a pizza delivery driver after losing his job, while Denise is growing dissatisfied with their suburban life — but one night, a storm hits and traps them all in a bizarre prehistoric playground full of dinosaurs. This sounds almost magical, but here's the thing: those dinosaurs are starving.

Diungkapkan bahwa on one level, "the end of oak street" is the only movie in existence, as far as i'm aware, where you can watch anne hathaway wreak havoc on dinosaurs with a shotgun. What "The End of Oak Street" is above all else, though, is fun. On another level, it's a treatise on the importance on family, and on another level, it's an audacious science-fiction story with a little bit of time travel and a lot left unexplained. and it's streaming on HBO Max as of November 13.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the aughts, "24" innovated a new style of episodic television by using a real-time conceit as a spy tries to save the world. Decades later, "The Pitt" used that same structure to great effect for its real-time experience of working a busy 15-hour emergency room shift. Apple TV's new drama series "12 12 12," though, is even stranger. Created by creative partners Jim Keeble and Dudi Appleton, "12 12 12" stars Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan as Jack Strickland and Bobby Galvin, two men involved with a high-risk heist in Zürich.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so, how does "12 12 12" tell its story? as former fbi agent strickland and master criminal galvin circle each other in europe, the heist in zürich is where they eventually meet. and Keeble and Appleton use three timelines within each episode. First, you get the 12 months of planning the heist, followed by the 12 hours required for said heist — and finally, the 12 days' worth of heist-related aftermath. "12 12 12" also stars Jack Kesy, Kali Reis, Ólafur Darri Ólafsson, and Patrick Fabian in supporting roles, and its first two episodes are streaming on Apple TV as of November 13.

Martin McDonagh at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

Maria di Girolamo, John Malkovich and Martin McDonagh, in conversation with Rebecca Ford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on Friday, November 13, 2026.

John Malkovich at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

Diungkapkan bahwa "he's one of the best actors of his generation, if not the best," adds mcdonagh of rockwell. "He's always surprising, always dangerous, always sensitive, always smart, always coming up with new stuff. We always hope the characters will always be surprising, and with Sam's voice in the head, that really helps. And I think there's a danger to him that's lovely to write for. ".

Mariana di Girolamo at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

For rising star Mariana di Girolamo, a Chilean actress making her English language movie debut with Wild Horse Nine, she was excited and only slightly intimidated to be a part of the cast.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "it was quite a challenge to perform for the first time in english," she said. Maria di Girolamo, John Malkovich and Martin McDonagh, in conversation with Rebecca Ford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on Friday, November 13, 2026.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in 1977, disabled rights activist judy heumann helped organize the landmark section 504 sit-in, a nationwide protest aimed at compelling hew secretary joseph califano to finally sign the long-delayed regulations implementing section 504 of the rehabilitation act of 1973. Heumann and her fellow disabled activists occupied federal buildings across the country for more than three weeks until Califano finally put pen to paper.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the regulations secured civil rights protections for disabled individuals and helped direct billions of dollars toward making federally funded infrastructure more accessible, including through curb cuts, wheelchair ramps, wider public restrooms and designated parking spaces. The movement also helped pave the way for the more sweeping Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990.

Berdasarkan laporan, walsh and heder knew that if they were going to dramatize heumann’s david-versus-goliath tale, the only way to honor the late disabled pioneer was to bring her story to the screen authentically. That meant casting more than a dozen key roles with disabled actors and practicing what the movie preaches by creating an accessible, equitable set that could accommodate the ensemble’s unique needs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the rub was that no such blueprint existed, and there was only one wheelchair-accessible trailer in all of north america. Working alongside a ten-person accessibility team and a crew that included disabled artisans and technicians, Walsh, Heder and their partners customized the Being Heumann set, taking extra precautions for the cast and ensuring direct access to personal and hair/makeup trailers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we did experience a handful of califano-type people, just not from the studio side. It was more, You can’t do it this way. It’s never been done this way,” Walsh shares. Apple was great. “But we needed to ignore history and really try to recreate how people make movies. Sebagaimana diketahui, on his first day, he got into the hair and makeup trailer and started to cry. He went on to describe it to me personally and said, “You don’t understand. But I feel like I’m one of everyone here. This is Shangri-La for an actor who’s disabled. They asked him what was wrong, and he said, “In my whole career, I’ve never, ever seen the inside of a hair and makeup trailer. ” I was so floored by that story and what we had done to achieve it. Normally, I’m down the hall in a closet getting ready on my own. ” So, as a seasoned disabled actor, he could see the difference.

Was there extra crew to accommodate the disabled cast?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we had a 10-person accessibility team at all times. We provided masseuses, nutritionists and round-the-clock care. We had people transferring disabled actors from their regular wheelchairs to period wheelchairs. We’d give them time for stretches and breaks. We had a lot of disabled crew members working with us as well.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but we made a lot of mistakes throughout the process. It’s one of the reasons why I did the movie. We had to refine it and hone it and get it better and better. ” I wanted to figure out all these issues. When Sian first asked me, “Why do you want to do this?” my answer truly was, “Because the movie fucking terrifies me. It was just really important for me to learn this new skillset. But with a good team around us, we were able to achieve it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there are so many great disabled actors in this movie who had never acted before. So, for them, it was like, This is how movies must work all the time. They’d never been in a film before, much less a soundstage or a set. (Laughs. ).

When it came to casting Judy and the other 504 protestors, how large was the talent pool of disabled actors?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, you might be surprised to hear this, but there are a lot of really talented people. Our casting directors, Bernie Telsey and Adam Caldwell, really put the spotlight on that community. Had we not tried to authentically cast people with the actual disabilities of the characters they’re portraying, we wouldn’t have found that talent.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for judy, it was a bit more specific. We had to find a disabled person who has the charisma and acting chops to lead a movie, but also possess the same kind of ferociousness and tenacity that Judy had. So there aren’t a lot of Ruth Madeleys out there.

Hopefully, this movie opens more doors for everyone.

Berdasarkan laporan, yeah, my hope is that people will shine a spotlight on these actors so that they’ll be considered for other parts. We’re developing a TV show right now for an A-list TV actress, and I’ve pitched one of our disabled actors, Andrew Pilkington, to play her sibling. So I just said, “How great would it be if he were the brother of this actress? That would provide a whole other layer of complexity to this show. He plays Hale Zukas in Being Heumann, and he communicates with the antenna on the board. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa i’m also doing the team hoyt movie at netflix with producers gotham chopra and tom brady, and [directors] nat faxon and jim rash. I’m bringing Andrew Pilkington on because he’s a producer in his own right, and he’s going to help me with authenticity. We have an actor who has cerebral palsy, and he’ll oversee the way we make the movie.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so there is a lot of talent in front of the camera and behind it. It’s just a matter of redefining the norms of casting actors in movies and TV shows and learning to look at everyone all at once. Again, access.

One of the best performances of the year was given by a disabled actor named Steve Way on the series Furious, which was partially directed by Cory Finley, who you helped launch by way of Thoroughbreds.

Diungkapkan bahwa yes, steve is incredible. I just read in the trades a couple days ago that Ramy Youssef and Steve are doing a body swap comedy, which is really interesting. She chatted with him, but Steve had some conflicts regarding this movie. What Steve and Cory and [creator] Liz Meriwether did on that show is amazing. We’re actually getting ready to start prep on Cory’s next film. Sian knows Steve. It’s coming up next year with a really good cast.

Berdasarkan laporan, i admire how honestly being heumann portrays its disabled characters. In other words, the film doesn’t portray them as infallible saints simply because they’re disabled. They’re generally altruistic, but they still make mistakes and give in to their impulses, like we all do. Did the ensemble also appreciate this unvarnished take?.

Diungkapkan bahwa they totally did. One of the most amazing feats of the movie is that each person you meet has their own little 180-degree turn. Early, early on, before prep, I said, “There’s too many people to service, Sian. I’m glad you mentioned that because one of the geniuses of Sian Heder is that she’s able to create an arc for all 15 of these characters. And I will say she proved me wrong. I don’t know if you’re going to get around to all of it. ” And she did. And so the actors loved that.

Diungkapkan bahwa a lot of times, when we see disabled characters, they’re either perceived as saintly or bitter because they’re dealing with their disability, but they are like anybody else. They just happen to be in a wheelchair or unable to access certain things that non-disabled people have access to. So the actors really appreciated how layered and different all these characters were.

Diungkapkan bahwa i was also impressed by how they let their personal experiences shine through in their characters quite a bit. If you recall the testimonials in the movie, Sian wisely guided and directed them to look inward a bit as they were telling those stories about their disabilities. That infused the film with a certain credibility, but also emotion.

Mark Ruffalo and Dylan O’Brien both fit their roles so well, but the cynical viewpoint is that you needed a couple names to appease the powers that be.

Berdasarkan laporan, they just responded well to the material. Stick to this number, but go make the film. [Apple TV bosses] Zack Van Amburg, Jamie Erlicht, and Matt Dentler really got behind this movie and said, “Go make the film. Don’t get me wrong, it’s always beneficial to have movie stars help open a film and bring awareness to a film. ” So we didn’t need any real names. But Apple was supporting this film through and through, head to toe. We were just lucky to get Mark and Dylan.

Berdasarkan laporan, mark is a once-in-a-generation-level actor. He could be perceived as a cold, simple villain, but he’s really a guy who’s just trying to do his best. He is perfect in the role of Califano. I spoke to him this morning in fact. We’re working together on another project that he’s going to star in and direct. It’s a very complex, layered part. And at the end of the day, he tips his hat to Judy, nicely, by saying, “Well fought. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa dylan is another wonderful actor with a huge following, so we got lucky to have those guys help raise awareness of the film. But we didn’t really need them.

Diungkapkan bahwa the postscript says that the fight for disability rights is far from over. Do you happen to know what the outstanding issues are?.

Berdasarkan laporan, yeah, a lot of these section 504 rights and regulations are now being conflated with the argument about transgender rights. They all fall under the same umbrella. So, in 14 states right now, they’re trying to repeal funding for some of these Section 504 rights because of other rights that fall under that umbrella. There was a big article about this in Time magazine within the last couple of months.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what people don’t understand is that you’re talking about taking away curb cuts, elevators and access for disabled people in our community. If you’re against the idea of a person in a wheelchair being able to access a federal building, a post office or a place to get their passport renewed, you’re on the wrong side of history. This is why it’s super important, and it saddens me that we’re still having this conversation 50 years later. It’s just that simple. So you have to look closely at what you’re reading, what you’re voting for and who you’re supporting.

Diungkapkan bahwa i spoke to tom pelphrey and louis leterrier not too long ago, and your sci-fi action-thriller with them, liminal, came up. What else are you excited about on the Walsh Company slate?.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’m really excited about louis’ movie. Besides Tom, it has Vanessa Kirby, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Tracy Letts and Franka Potente. He’s got a murderer’s row of great actors. So we’re in post on that right now.

Diungkapkan bahwa we’ve also had a rocket-ship start to our tv business. We hired an executive named Danny Feldheim about a year and a half ago, and we’ve set up ten TV shows in that time. We have five or six shows at Apple, a show with John Mulaney and Langston Kerman at HBO and another great show called The Hawk with Dave Collard and Casey Affleck at Hulu. So we’re excited about being all over that side of the business.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we’re also prepping three or four movies for next year. We just got something in the last week that I’m most excited about. There’s a Black List script called Best Seller that was with Peter Rice until he left to take the [Netflix CCO] job. We got lucky enough to meet on it, and while it went out to 10 or 15 producers, we won that movie. So we’re really excited about putting it together and getting a director on it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we’re finally going to make adam and aaron nee’s next movie, calamity hustle, next year. We’re getting close on that deal with two actors.

Ryan Reynolds and Channing Tatum are no longer attached?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it’s no longer ryan and channing. The Nee brothers have done a really good job on the script, and they’re ready to go. It’s going to be a couple other actors, but we’re really excited about it. They’ve said no to a lot of movies to make this movie.

You mentioned it earlier, but what’s the latest on Cory Finley’s next one?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, yeah, we’re going to make cory’s upcoming film [reasonable people] with paul rudd and sam rockwell, which will probably be a fall shoot. It’s a wonderful story about revenge in modern-day America. We’re out to another actor now, and we’re closing a deal with a really exciting financier who’s going to do it. It’s kind of like a present-day Hatfields & McCoys set in the suburbs. It has that same darkly comedic tone as Thoroughbreds, with really nuanced characters and a deep dive into the relationship between two fathers and one of the fathers’ brothers in this suburban community.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, then we have a really big film at apple that we’re getting quite close on for next year. It’s a Christmas movie. So it could be a busy year next year, but I’m honestly just lucky and happy to be making movies and doing what I love. Apple has been great to us, and I’m grateful they’ve given us a platform.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “obsession and backrooms” has been the most repeated phrase this year. Everyone’s been trying to discern what the takeaway should be. Rather than simply hiring more YouTubers or adapting unusual internet properties, is the real lesson to take chances on newer, original voices, regardless of platform or genre?.

Berdasarkan laporan, you’re right about original voices. Matisse Haddad, who wrote Best Seller, is an original voice. He has a Black List script called Drudge about Matt Drudge, which is also one of the best scripts I’ve ever read. There’s another great young writer named Cody Brotter who’s writing the Bon Jovi story for us at Universal. It’s one of her early screenplays, and it’s one of the best scripts I’ve read in a long time. We’re going to try to get that made.

Diungkapkan bahwa so it’s about finding young voices and just trusting youthful filmmakers. There’s a great script we love called The Toe by a writer named Mallory Westfall. It’s harder to make those kinds of movies. It’s completely bonkers and left of center and dark, but original and great and unlike anything you’ll read. Those [tonal seesaws], like Cory’s next movie, are harder lifts, but you’re fighting for originality at the end of the day.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there are filmmakers to be found on youtube, just like there’s filmmakers to be found everywhere. The directive at our company isn’t, Go find us an action movie or a romantic comedy. It’s just about keeping an open mind to originality and setting your own pace and not trying to copy something else. It’s always, What makes you sit up straight when you read it? Do you want to make it and why? That’s really all we look for.

Berdasarkan laporan, we’ve reached the dreaded ai question. But now there’s filmmakers like Doug Liman and Darren Aronofsky who are experimenting with it rather aggressively, while directors like Ben Affleck, Danny Boyle, and Ava DuVernay have acknowledged using it for minor details, such as animating old photographs. Initially, the creative community drew a hard line in the sand against its use. But as the scope keeps creeping outward, those minor details could soon become major ones, and entire departments could be gutted or downsized in no time. Maybe I’m being an alarmist, but do you think it’s inevitable at this rate?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i don’t think you’re being alarmist, but i don’t think it’s inevitable, either. There’s always going to be human artistry that you need to harness.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, some people say, “graphic designers and previs artists and other visual artists are going to be gone. He did Boston Strangler with me. ” John P. Goldsmith, who was my production designer on Being Heumann, has a degree from Harvard — a master’s in architecture. On Being Heumann, he designed all the detailed lobby work, like the brass elevator buttons and the marbling, in the building the protestors storm. John took all of his education, his history, his experience, all of it, and made sure that it looks right. He’s a genius. All of that was constructed from scratch. People from Apple came to visit the set, and they couldn’t believe it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it hearkens back to one of my first films in my early 20s when i worked as an assistant on the hours. So, Stephen Daldry, I believe, described the [dropped] shot to the production designer and the construction team. I walked through it, and I couldn’t believe how exact a match it was. We didn’t want to go back to the hotel location. It was flawless. The next morning, I came back to the stage at Pinewood, and the hallway of this hotel had been reconstructed. We dropped a shot while filming at a hotel in the south of London, and we moved back to the stage. We put the actors in the hallway, Julianne Moore, and we had the shot.

Sebagaimana diketahui, so, yes, there’s a way to use ai quite a bit in previs, in post and with vfx, but you still need to harness that type of human creativity. You need to have a team that executes at a high level. This is a community medium. You’re going to use AI as a tool. The filmmakers you mentioned — Danny, Ava and Ben — they’re using it as a tool in a great way. But if you ask any one of them, “Can you do away with human artistry and do your job?” they’d say that you can’t. I could not make Being Heumann without my producing team of Sian, David, Kevin Cleary and John Beach.

Berdasarkan laporan, we are using ai, for sure, with certain vfx stuff. There’s definitely some AI in the previs on bigger movies. But I came up working in a lot of different departments in moviemaking, and you will always need to harness artistic creativity. Without it, you’re going to have a movie that feels devoid of spirit. It’s going to look mechanical, and audiences are going to sniff it out.

Berdasarkan laporan, screenwriting, storytelling and directing need to keep redefining. Those areas can’t be iterative. If you’re going to be iterative with AI, you’ll just be rehashing old movies and old stories. So you need human creativity to explore other areas, and that’s where you’ll find your Backrooms and Being Heumanns, movies that have not been done before.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i’ve asked this question off and on over the years, but i play rocky has given me permission to dust it off. I love narrative features about the making of beloved movies. So out of all your projects, which one warrants the I Play Rocky treatment?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, oh man, that’s such a hard question. It was an incredible movie. I actually attended an AMPAS lunch this past weekend, and coincidentally, I was seated next to Mark Ricker, my production designer, on that movie. I had such a good time on The Way, Way Back. We talked about how it was his favorite movie ever.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, everyone rented beach houses alongside each other. We would walk to work every day, shoot the movie and come home. That was a great moviemaking experience for the comedy of it, because [co-directors] Nat [Faxon] and Jim [Rash] and I would go to dinners and get cocktails with all our wonderful comedic actors each night. Toni Collette, Allison Janney, Steve Carell, Sam Rockwell, Maya Rudolph and the rest of our wonderful cast all lived on the beach together. So there’s definitely a behind-the-scenes element to that.

Berdasarkan laporan, but then there’s the scope and scale of the ridley movies and those experiences. Napoleon was jaw-dropping to film and create. Seeing the scope of it made me pinch myself quite a few times and think, How did I get here? How did I get here from making a tiny little independent film 28 years earlier?.

Would [script doctor] Paul Thomas Anderson be the second or third-act twist in the Napoleon making-of movie?.

Diungkapkan bahwa (laughs. The filmmaker was so taken with Walsh’s look that he cast him in The Master. [Writer’s Note: In the early 2010s, Walsh attended a wedding officiated by Anderson. ) Yes, the Paul part of that process was great and really rewarding to watch. I actually got to meet Paul much, much earlier than that. ].

Sebagaimana diketahui, then i would say house of gucci, just with the legendary cast and the postcard-like tour of italy. I got to watch Al Pacino, Jeremy Irons, Gaga, Adam Driver and Jared Leto. We made the movie in Rome, Milan, Lake Como and the Alps. It was a wonderful front-row seat to moviemaking with Ridley at the helm. He’s one of a kind.

***Being Heumann is now streaming on Apple TV.

#513. Seth Rogen on ‘The Invite,’ ‘Tangles,’ ‘The Studio’ Season 2, Reviving ‘Darkwing Duck’ and Why ‘Any A–hole Can Write That Joke’ Was the Best Advice He Ever Got

📅 13 Nov 2026

Seth Rogen on ‘The Invite,’ ‘Tangles,’ ‘The Studio’ Season 2, Reviving ‘Darkwing Duck’ and Why ‘Any A–hole Can Write That Joke’ Was the Best Advice He Ever Got

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://variety.com/2026/film/awards/seth-rogen-the-invite-tangles-the-studio-season-2-1236946538/

Awards Circuit Podcast: The roundtable discusses the 'I Play Rocky' screenplay debate and the new Disney movie 'Hexed'.

For years, people have told me that Seth Rogen and I are voice twins.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sitting across from him at the middleburg film festival, deep in virginia horse country, even jeremy, the person recording our conversation, can confirm that the resemblance is very close. Even so, the year Rogen is having belongs entirely to him.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, coming off the historic emmy run of “the studio,” rogen could have gone anywhere next. He chose to travel into the world of darkly comic relationship drama “The Invite” and the 2D animated world of Alzheimer’s disease with “Tangles,” a one-two punch nobody could have seen coming. Related Stories Chris Pratt to Continue 'Terminal List' Story in 'Savage Son' Series for Amazon 'Off Campus' Sets Season 2 Release Date at Amazon.

Berdasarkan laporan, in “the invite,” olivia wilde’s a24 dinner-party indie, rogen plays joe, a husband whose fraying marriage gets stress-tested over one excruciating evening with the upstairs neighbors, played by penélope cruz and edward norton. On paper, it sounds like a “another Seth Rogen” role. I think it’s his finest hour as an actor. On screen, he plays it in a way we didn’t expect and he credits Wilde for taking his and Norton’s ideas to heart.

Berdasarkan laporan, “she could have just not used any of it,” he says. “and I just would not have been as funny in it. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa on the episode of the variety awards circuit podcast, rogen discusses his one-two punch of “the invite” and “tangles,” along with the recently announced “darkwing duck” revival at disney+, the awards-season satire threaded through season 2 of “the studio” and how “steve jobs” opened a door to a part of the industry he had never been invited into. Listen below!.

Among comedians, he says, going dramatic “almost feels like a bit of a cheat code” and he recalls Jonah Hill predicting “Moneyball” (2011) would bring him the most acclaim of his career for doing the least (Hill was right, getting his first Oscar nom for supporting actor).

Berdasarkan laporan, “tangles,” on the other hand, is a different kind of gamble. The hand-drawn, black-and-white animated feature, adapted from Sarah Leavitt’s graphic memoir about her mother’s Alzheimer’s and directed by first-time feature filmmaker Leah Nelson, comes from Rogen’s Point Grey Pictures and features his voice alongside Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Abbi Jacobson, Bryan Cranston and Samira Wiley. In a category ruled by studio franchises, it is the outlier and it took 10 years to make and the Canadian multihyphenate always had his eye on what’s most important. “When we give up on it is when it doesn’t happen,” he says.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, independent film company and sapan studio open “tangles” in theaters this year for an awards-qualifying run, with a wider expansion in early 2027. “The Invite” is streaming on HBO Max.

The conversation has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Sebagaimana diketahui, you’re having quite a year, with two very different movies in “the invite” and “tangles. ” You’re coming off “The Studio,” and there’s been a lot of anticipation about what you’ll do next. This is quite a one-two punch. How does this moment in your career feel?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i feel very lucky. It’s incredibly nice and gratifying that, over the last few years, I feel like I’ve been doing work I’m very proud of and pushing myself to do things that are hopefully different from what I’ve done in the past. You only want to hope that you’re learning more in life, that you’re getting better at making choices and that once you’ve decided to do something, you get better at being the best part of the team you can be. And part of it is coincidence. We didn’t know it was going to come out now. But I also feel very lucky to have people who have wanted to work with me and have been willing to. We’ve worked on “Tangles” for 10 years. Luck has a lot to do with these things coming to life in a way that makes it seem like I planned it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, starting with “the invite,” this might be your finest hour as an actor. On paper, it sounds like a movie Seth Rogen would make. Playing Joe, did you feel you were doing something you hadn’t done before? Did you have one of those out-of-body experiences?.

Diungkapkan bahwa as we were making the movie, i felt like i was being given the opportunity, at least in a movie, to do something that was very representative of my exact comedic, tonal and dramatic taste. She allowed Edward to give dramatic monologues in places where they weren’t originally going to be. What was really amazing about what Olivia did was that she allowed us to affect the tone of the film with our performances. She allowed me to insert humor in moments where it wasn’t originally going to be, which changes the tone of the whole thing. And then she allowed me to make jokes that subverted those moments in ways that weren’t originally scripted.

Berdasarkan laporan, to me, that was an incredibly new and gratifying feeling. You could see it happening in real time. We weren’t just being invited to change the dialogue or our characters throughout the performing process. You could see that a scene was much funnier than we thought it would be. Or we thought a scene was going to be funny, but it was actually much more intense than we all thought. Olivia was allowing us to change the tone of the film itself with our performances. We were encouraged to play with that and not be too beholden to what it was originally conceived as, but instead feel it out as we were doing it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i have to give her credit for using my stuff in a way that turned out very well. I throw a lot of stuff out there, and she could have edited this movie in a way that left out some of what I think are the funniest moments I generated as we were making it. The film probably still would have been very good, but I just wouldn’t have been as funny in it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so i’m very proud that it’s a performance people seem to like, and i genuinely feel it’s one of my funnier performances. And it’s for sure the easiest thing I’ve done, because I’m just doing less than I normally do. So what’s nice is that I do feel like I was creating comedy throughout this film, and people are appreciating that. I remember Jonah Hill was making “Moneyball,” and he said, “This is going to be the thing that I get the most acclaim for. ” And I’ve done things like that. If I’m not funny, everyone leans in a little bit more. I’ve done dramatic work in the past, and I think among comedians it almost feels like a bit of a cheat code. It isn’t just because it’s not funny that people are appreciating it, which is something I think a lot of comedians have experienced.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it’s the jim carrey cheat code. He gets to do “The Truman Show” and “Eternal Sunshine,” and suddenly we’re all saying, “My God. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, yes. It’s obviously an honor to get to be in Steven Spielberg movies and things like that are certainly less comedic, and the fact that those filmmakers think I can serve their work in any way is very flattering. That’s exactly what Olivia really encouraged me to do. I’ve always been most proud of my funny work. There was a time when comedians really pursued that and wanted that, and I think it was a very deliberate thing comedians were doing for a while. I totally get it. It’s totally legitimate. It’s just that, to me, I’m very proud of my ability to generate comedy on camera. But I’m always thinking, if I could also bring my full ability to make this comedic, that would be great. So it was very gratifying to be able to bring that.

Berdasarkan laporan, i love that comedic actors can make that transition so seamlessly. I want to see the Christopher Nolan version of “Superbad. I’m also dying for directors who are known for drama to go the other way. ” I want them to take a swing like that.

Sebagaimana diketahui, apparently, “digger” is that. Comedians try to do drama, and sometimes it’s ill-fitting. I haven’t seen it. It’s harder than it looks sometimes. I’m not saying that film is that. Dramatic actors try to do comedy, and sometimes that’s ill-fitting, too. I haven’t seen it yet. It does go both ways. But it’s something I’ve seen happen.

Berdasarkan laporan, then there’s “tangles,” which is about as far from “the invite” as you can get. The animated feature category at the Oscars has been dominated by studio franchises for years, and now we have this hand-drawn, black-and-white film about Alzheimer’s. I think people need to hear the answer to this: How difficult is it to make a movie like this?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, really hard [laughs]. We’ve been working on it for 10 years, and I think maybe the last three years of that were production. So it was about seven years of us internally developing it, but also trying to find financing, putting together a cast that would be appealing to financiers, doing readings and making sure the script was really, really good.

Berdasarkan laporan, and the movie itself was made incredibly differently. You screen them, redo the third act, screen them again and redo the first act. Most animated movies, these big studio ones, are made, then made again, then made again. It had to be written and then executed, and we could change almost nothing. This movie couldn’t be made that way. It’s hand-drawn, so the process of changing things, should you want to, is incredibly labor-intensive and arduous.

Berdasarkan laporan, people like julia louis-dreyfus, bryan cranston, samira wiley and abbi jacobson, along with so many of the amazing cast members, were honestly really helpful in getting the movie made. So was having a good script and filmmakers who, when those actors got in the room with them, were willing to let them take ownership of the material. It’s so gratifying that the movie even exists. We’ve spent so long working on it.

During those first seven years, how many times did you think, “This isn’t happening?”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i thought it would happen. “Superbad” took so long to get made. Sometimes we don’t give up, and we will bring it into existence through sheer brute force. If something is good, I believe you can find a way to make it. This felt worth it because it was good. And then there were things like “Pineapple Express” and “Sausage Party,” all these movies we worked on for so long before they were made. So many things take a long time to get made. I truly believe that if we give up on it, that’s when it doesn’t happen. To me, 10 years is normal.

Berdasarkan laporan, “darkwing duck” because i’m a child of the ’80s and ’90s. Congratulations on the Emmy for “The Muppet Show,” and obviously we have “The Studio” Season 2 coming. But nothing excites me more than this cartoon classic that Mark Hamill has a role in! Did that casting fall into your lap?.

Berdasarkan laporan, the cast is really great. I’ve been watching the episodes, and they’re amazing. But it’s incredible. We’ve been working on it for a very long time. I’ll tell you after. You get caught up in these corporate restructurings, but we’ve been working on “Darkwing Duck” for years and years. We just cast a Scrooge McDuck who might be the most exciting casting I could ever imagine. They’re coming together so well, and the animation is beautiful and really inventive.

I was actually surprised you didn’t go the movie route.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’m glad we didn’t. The TV nature of it was very appealing to us, honestly. Getting to work in both those ways is nice. As nice as it is to make a hand-drawn, black-and-white animated film, it’s also nice to extract every penny Disney’s willing to put into a thing. But with something like “Darkwing Duck,” we felt that if we were going to do it, it had to be top, top-notch.

Sebagaimana diketahui, are there other disney shows from the ’80s and ’90s you’d love to bring back? i think of “talespin,” “gummi bears” and “ducktales. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i always think of “flight of the navigator. Years ago, when we were first talking about doing “Darkwing Duck” again, I rewatched all of it and thought, this is really meta. “Darkwing Duck,” though, I loved. I would never presume I’d do it, but that’s always been a movie I thought was cool. And it’s very meta. ” That was a Disney movie, I guess. It’s funny, I reread those “Calvin and Hobbes” comics recently and I realized they really formed a lot of my personality. It really breaks the fourth wall and comments on these shows I was also watching at the same time, at the same age.

If we can get “Gargoyles” back up and running ….

Sebagaimana diketahui, that would be great. I did love “Gargoyles. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, let’s talk about “the studio” season 2. There have been a lot of reports from the set: Madonna, the Venice Film Festival. Which real-life awards-season humiliation of yours is going to end up on the show?.

How much does Variety figure into the new season?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i think it comes up. I don’t want to reveal too much, but some of the stuff has made it out publicly into the world a little bit. This idea of playing the awards game as a studio is definitely a theme explored throughout the season.

Do you have a Season 2 equivalent of the Martin Scorsese moment, when viewers see who’s appearing and think, “I can’t believe they got him?” Does Christopher Nolan show up, for example?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we have several of those. We wanted to get people we were even bigger fans of and make them even bigger parts of the episodes, if we could. Some are really unbelievable, and having to direct these people has been among the most terrifying moments of my entire life. For ourselves, we really tried to be even more ambitious. We also wanted to dig deeper into our own feelings about the industry and our own internal conflicts as we go about all this.

Does the awards race feel more or less relevant to you now? Having made “The Studio,” how does it look compared with 15 years ago?.

Diungkapkan bahwa what’s interesting is that until i did the “steve jobs” movie, which was pretty deep into my career, i was never part of anything that was on that journey in any capacity. But that was the first time I went to Telluride, and then we were in the New York Film Festival. I’d been to TIFF and South by Southwest to premiere things. Honestly, it was like a door to a secret part of the industry that I’d never been invited into was suddenly opened. So it’s interesting, because I had a very lovely career before any of this was even on my radar.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but that being said, the fact that “the studio” won awards got us things in the second season that we probably wouldn’t have gotten in the first season. So there is some tangible outcome to some of this stuff. And I’ve seen people go on the journey and not get the outcome they wanted, and they had a good time and seemed to have good perspective at the end of all of it. I’ve seen people go on this journey and get the exact outcome they were hoping for, and it ultimately gave them none of the things they hoped it would. I understand why people get invested in it, and I understand the lure and the draw. It is a fascinating part of our industry to me.

Berdasarkan laporan, i think especially for smaller things, it is incredibly helpful. But what’s interesting is those people are at these events right next to the people whose lives it will change. If you’ve already made many billion-dollar movies, winning best picture is a feather in your cap. It could make or break people’s careers. It could make or break a film. It could change the course of people’s lives. For some people, they’re at the point of their career where awards have very personal stakes, but there are many other people here for whom the awards have real-life stakes. It’s not going to change the course of your life, per se. To me, that is really interesting to see in real life and really cool. Will they get to do the thing they’ve always wanted to do, or will it not happen the way they hoped?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that is really interesting and scary and cool to see play out. There are those moments where your heart is pounding and you’re like, we’re doing it. This is what we asked for: to put ourselves out there and subject ourselves to reality in terms of how our work is being perceived. It can be very gratifying and incredibly scary and stressful.

Can you tell me something about “The Studio” Season 2? Is there a oner episode again?.

Diungkapkan bahwa we actually try to do much more of that. There are more episodes in a much more condensed timeline. I think there are technically several episodes this season that have no cuts in them, basically, throughout the entire thing. They’re real-time, half-hour moments in time that the episode is chronicling.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s a weird time in the industry. Depending on who you ask, the future looks very grim. Others say it’s an evolution and we’re just going through some changes. One of the biggest conversations here at Middleburg was Peter Rice going to Netflix. Someone like him, who’s been such a theatrical guy, making that move feels like a signal: Theatrical’s back! How do you feel about this moment? Do you get nervous, or do you think we’re going to be OK?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s a mixture of everything. The fact that so many people are going to theaters, compared to the last few years, is so encouraging. It reminds me of when I was a kid, honestly, a little bit more. As someone who loves going to the movies, it’s really fun to see. I think we are finally getting over that hump of the pandemic and the strikes and all that. It is everything at once. It seems like things are returning to a time when there are a lot of good movies and people are willing to go see them, and that’s really exciting. From my own personal lens, I can go to the theater on a Tuesday night and it’s packed and it wasn’t like that for a long time. I’m very optimistic about some things. And I think other things are terrifying.

Berdasarkan laporan, “sethical. ” Friends from growing up still call me that when I see them. They don’t even think about it. It just comes out.

Something you loved as a kid but can’t believe you were into when you think about it now?.

Diungkapkan bahwa i get why people like “magic: the gathering,” but i spent every penny i had on “magic: the gathering” cards. That’s the thing I look back on, and I’m like, I should have bought other stuff.

Berdasarkan laporan, i don’t karaoke as a rule. Now you’re in a little room with just your friends in it, screaming your ass off like an idiot. If karaoke went away altogether, I’d never need to be in a room with some drunk person screaming a song ever again. That said, “All for Love” by Bryan Adams. I hate it. The rooms are getting smaller and smaller. It used to be the bar was higher because you were subjecting yourself to a real big room full of people. Now I’m three feet away from this person. It’s so loud. If you have two other raspy-voiced friends, it’s a really good song.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i was going to say “the apartment. ” I would take “The Apartment. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i’m pretty flexible. I can almost get my leg behind my head.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i just like vanilla. I did that movie with Barbra Streisand [”The Guilt Trip”], and she was obsessed with McConnell’s ice cream, which is from Santa Barbara. Every scene we shot, she’s like, “Wouldn’t we be eating ice cream in this scene?” So yes, it’s become McConnell’s.

Sebagaimana diketahui, my glasses come to mind. My shoes. Things like that.

What TV show or film in all of history do you wish you were a cast member of?.

Maybe it would have been cool to be in “Ghostbusters” or something like that.

Which fictional character do you most relate to or admire?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i always liked homer simpson. Not that I relate to or admire him, but I always just liked him.

Your favorite piece of advice, either given or received?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i was told at a very young age to write what only i could write, which meant writing things based on my own experience, things that were happening to me. Don’t talk about fucking crazy glue. Talk about that. I was writing jokes that were observational, like, “What’s the deal with crazy glue?” Those kinds of jokes. No one else can talk about that. I was maybe 15, maybe 14 and he pulled me aside and said, “Dude, you’re out there trying to get hand jobs and trying to buy beer and trying to sneak into parties and shit. I was doing OK. ” It was honestly the best creative advice I’ve ever gotten. Any asshole can write that joke. A stand-up comedian named Darryl Lenox, who’s passed away, unfortunately, told me that and he was really nice to me. I try to adhere to it to this day.

#516. Ghost Soldier Ending Explained: How Jim Caviezel's New Action Hero Destroys Brownstone

Ghost Soldier Ending Explained: How Jim Caviezel's New Action Hero Destroys Brownstone

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/ghost-soldier-ending-explained-how-jim-caviezels-fitz-destroys-blackstone/

Sebagaimana diketahui, in 2023, actor jim caviezel (best known for playing jesus christ in mel gibson’s the passion of the christ) starred in angel studios’ sound of freedom. Sound of Freedom earned over $250 million on a meager $15 million production budget, proving to be one of the most profitable films of the year. The film was a surprise smash hit at the box office and with audiences, putting Angel Studios on the map. Now, he's back with another movie — Ghost Soldier, which premiered this week for a Veteran's Day release.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sound of freedom may have had just a 57% score critics score on rotten tomatoes, but it was still a huge hit with audiences. That’s in spite of the political controversy and general divisiveness that the movie generated too. The Alejandro Monteverde-directed action epic earned a whopping 99% audience score on the site, highlighting just how much viewers connected with the film. As a result, many have high expectations for Ghost Soldier.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s no surprise, then, that jim caviezel is back in another action film that embraces many of the same themes and values as sound of freedom. In the new film, Caviezel plays a former special operatives soldier who is forced to protect his town from a villainous corporation seeking to displace residents from their homes in order to build a cooling plant for AI data centers.

Diungkapkan bahwa ghost soldier is described as a faith-based action film, and one that is being released on veterans day because of the military themes present throughout. Caviezel’s Henry Fitzgerald isn’t the only character to have served in the military, and the film shows how the action follows Fitz even after he departed the service. All of this builds up to a jam-packed finale, and one that puts Fitz in grave danger as he pushes back against the company and its third party mercenaries.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at the heart of this story is a villainous company called the brownstone corporation. The fictional company is deeply involved in artificial intelligence and is led by foreign investors based in the Middle East. Blackstone is said to have invested significant amounts of money in new artificial intelligence data centers and are intent on ensuring their long-term success.

Berdasarkan laporan, fitz defeats brownstone with a meticulous plan, and one that begins long before the grand finale. For starters, he goes to the home of the Brownstone lawyer that accompanied their mercenaries to the Hernandez residence and uses threats of torture to coerce useful information out of her. What's more, he lays the groundwork for the company's downfall by convincing her to take what she knows to the press.

Berdasarkan laporan, however, a lot more is needed in order to take down brownstone. Fitz recognizes this, and opts to use his many advanced weapons in battle against the company’s mercenaries. One of these weapons is a cloak of invisibility, something that feels as if it’s been pulled straight from the wizarding world of Harry Potter.

Berdasarkan laporan, fitz uses this cloak, along with his many other weapons, as he infiltrates a brownstone party, held to celebrate their recent successes and the launch of their plans. Fitz poses as a waiter initially, but quickly attracts the attention of security, and it’s at this moment that the fighting begins. Fitz fends off countless soldiers, and eventually uses explosives to destroy the cooling center that Browstone had been building, thus crushing the company’s plans in the region. He also uses missiles to destroy the entire event space, with only Brownstone operatives left in the space at this point.

Berdasarkan laporan, his actions culminate in a one-on-one showdown with the leader of a group of bosnian mercenaries contracted by brownstone. Initially, his choice comes across as a mistake, as the mercenary gets the upper hand and seemingly has Fitz on the ropes. Despite displaying ruthless tactics against his other opponents, Fitz makes the interesting decision to fight the villain honorably, rather than shooting him dead right away. But unbeknownst to him, Fitz had attached two parts of an explosive device on his back and chest, allowing him to blow an explosive hole in the man's torso.

It was a finishing move that had somewhat of a sci-fi edge to it, but still felt consistent with the technologically advanced arsenal of weapons Fitz had at his disposal throughout the movie.

Sebagaimana diketahui, fitz also had a small helping hand from the recently fired sheriff of the community, olivia thirlby's parker. Having infiltrated the party as well, Parker was able to take on a minor role in the action, including a chance to kill Garret Dillahunt's character when he had Fitz in his sights. Although less skilled than his foreign counterparts, Dillahunt's character made it surprisingly far, but ultimately, none of the villains went unpunished - and that extended to the one power player who managed to keep his distance from the entire conflict.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the closing minutes of the movie, fitz travels to the middle east, where he targets the company’s founder and leader. Fitz uses a sniper rifle to shoot him in the head, thus bringing Brownstone’s reign of terror to a complete end, tying up the last remaining loose end.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it was the methods of the aforementioned villain who made all of this necessary. Desire for full control over the region's water, which would lead to the construction of AI data centers and in turn, a vast increase in the company's wealth, was the driving force of his decision making.

Berdasarkan laporan, as is the case with every ai data center, a significant amount of water is needed in order to keep them going. Brownstone recognizes this and, as such, is actively working to build cooling centers that would help keep the technology at a healthy temperature. For this, the company needs a sizable amount of land, and they had identified the town of Valentine in the countryside of Wyoming as a prime place for their cooling centers.

Diungkapkan bahwa in its efforts to make sense of the lengths they were willing to go to get what they wanted, ghost soldier addressed the matter of imminent domain, a law that enables property to be seized if it serves the good of the community. As characters in the story pointed out, the villains would have had to wait longer than they preferred for imminent domain to kick in, and expectations placed on them to get results spurred them to take matters into their own hands.

Sebagaimana diketahui, brownstone is no more, but fitz still has more to do. Fitz has thus far been lying low in his lab at Wyoming, even when he knows the government could use him elsewhere. His handler in the government, played by Shea Whigham, threatened to pull him out of Wyoming, prompting Fitz to tempt him with a compelling offer. Taking advantage of this, Fitz promised to help deal with international threats if he was allowed to finish the Brownstone fight.

Diungkapkan bahwa presumably, that's what will define fitz's next chapter. It's likely that in the immediate aftermath of Ghost Soldier, Fitz will have his hands full with field work overseas. The United States has all sorts of problems to concern itself with, from Russia to China, which were both brought up in their conversation. That setup could create room for a sequel if the new Jim Caviezel-led action film performs well at the box office.

A reclusive government asset and former Green Beret veteran uses his weapon prototypes to defend rural communities in Wyoming.

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.tmz.com/2026/11/13/tom-winter-saying-no-microsoft-faa-connection/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the nationwide federal aviation administration shutdown is not connected to microsoft's widespread outage. despite the timing of the two major disruptions raising questions about whether a cyberattack or technical failure could be behind both incidents, according to reports.

NBC News correspondent Tom Winter reports he's been speaking with top law enforcement and cybersecurity officials throughout Friday, and as of 5 PM ET, there's no indication the Microsoft outage has any connection to the FAA problems.

Diungkapkan bahwa winter says officials have found no evidence linking the two incidents, pushing back on speculation that microsoft's technical issues may have played a role in the aviation disruption. The FAA has not publicly confirmed or denied whether the two incidents are related.

The clarification comes amid a chaotic day for travelers, with the FAA's nationwide shutdown raising concerns about flight operations across the country.

As we previously reported, the FAA ordered the unprecedented ground stop Friday afternoon, instructing departing flights at airports nationwide to remain on the ground because of what officials described as an extraordinary circumstance.

Berdasarkan laporan, planes already in the air were allowed to land, while international arrivals were being handled on a case-by-case basis. The order sent airlines and airports scrambling as passengers faced delays and uncertainty about when normal operations would resume.

Diungkapkan bahwa transportation secretary sean duffy said faa technicians were investigating the communications failure. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin also said there was no evidence of a cyberattack or other national security threat, describing the incident as a telecommunications outage.

Berdasarkan laporan, meanwhile, microsoft has been dealing with its own massive outage, which began thursday and affected millions of users worldwide. Outlook, Teams, Copilot, SharePoint and other Microsoft 365 services experienced disruptions, impacting businesses, government agencies and other organizations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, microsoft has attributed its problems to a technical issue involving a network capacity upgrade and subsequent network changes, saying it found no evidence of malicious or cyber activity. The company had begun restoring services Friday, although some users continued experiencing issues.

Despite the overlap, Winter's reporting suggests the two major outages are separate incidents, with officials not finding evidence that Microsoft's technical problems contributed to the FAA's nationwide shutdown.

The FAA's investigation into the communications failure remains ongoing.

#521. Why Jordan Brand Is Using a ‘Space Jam’ Docuseries to Launch “Jordan TV”

📅 13 Nov 2026

Why Jordan Brand Is Using a ‘Space Jam’ Docuseries to Launch “Jordan TV”

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/digital/beyond-the-jam-space-jam-youtube-docuseries-jordan-brand-1236755122/

The Nike-owned brand is planning to use its Jordan TV platforms to roll out content built around its products, and Michael Jordan himself.

This Sunday, Jordan TV will launch with a buzzy docuseries that takes fans behind the scenes of Space Jam, the live action-cartoon hybrid that debuted in theaters 30 years ago.

The docuseries, Beyond the Jam, features a star-studded cast of characters, from Michael Jordan himself (making a rare on-camera appearance) to stars like Teyana Taylor, J Balvin, and Jayson Tatum, as well as the late Eric Bauza, the voice of Bugs Bunny, who passed away unexpectedly last month.

Berdasarkan laporan, the first episode debuts on the jordan tv youtube channel sunday, with new episodes dropping each week. Warner Bros. worked with Jordan Brand on the docuseries.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “space jam really was more than a movie, it was a cultural movement and really changed the face of the entertainment industry, with an athlete like michael coming in,” says jordan brand cmo caitlin sargent, in an interview with the hollywood reporter. “The last thing you would have expected of an athlete like that would be going and filming a movie. So it was quite unconventional, and I think we always take that as inspiration. He’s our blueprint to say how can we do things a little bit differently?”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “what we decided was to leverage this moment and the story of space jam 30 years, really inspiring the next generation to find their own greatness,” sargent added. “We wanted to use that as a moment to reposition this channel with the six-part mini doc, and the goal here was no doubt to to make sure that we were telling the untold stories of the making of Space Jam, but also the cultural impact it had. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, but it is jordan tv that may be the more intriguing part of the launch. Jordan Brand, the Nike-owned athletics brand known for its iconic “Jumpman” logo, is rethinking content, betting that high-quality original programming, delivered directly to consumers via YouTube, is the future of how it engages with that audience.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i think we know how important storytelling is with the next generation, and we know how important youtube and that channel is,” sargent says. “And so we are working on repositioning our Jordan YouTube channel to Jordan TV, which is really what we’re calling inside access. It’s a one-stop shop destination for never been seen storytelling around product stories and experiences, really allowing our community and our consumer to come inside the walls of the Jordan brand.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “this is our first step out to really reposition the channel, and what you’re going to see is an intersection of sport culture and sneaker culture,” she adds. “But the main piece is that we want to make sure that it does feel like it’s that inside access. I always say, when we’re doing our storytelling, our branded content is always really amazing. But what really our young consumer wants to see is the making of, what was it like to be on set as we’re shooting? What was it like bringing that brand experience to life? And so this will really feel like you’re getting that through several stories that we’ve got coming and that we’re really excited about. ”.

As The Hollywood Reporter reported in an August cover story, brands are becoming more ambitious in their storytelling, looking beyond traditional commercials and campaigns to become more full-funnel storytellers, funding original content, and bringing consumers inside their worlds.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that’s true for nike, which was featured in the story, but also for jordan brand. Sargent describes the move as being an imperative.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we know our consumer has changed, and what creates an emotional connection with youth today is different than what it what it has been over the last 40 years,” she says. “So what we’re doing right now is trying to make sure that we’re shifting into, less branded content. If it feels like an ad, smells like an ad, it starts to fall a bit flat. What we really want to do is shift into a space where we’re creating core memories with our young consumer through the products, through the stories, and through the experiences that we’re putting forth. ”.

The launch of The Sopranos in 1999 paved the way for the 2002 premiere of The Wire, which focused on drug dealers in Baltimore and the police officers trying to disrupt their operations. The series is still one of the best shows of all time, and provided breakout roles for huge stars like Idris Elba and Michael B. Jordan. But while it was compelling from the beginning, The Wire truly achieved perfection in season 4 when the scope expanded beyond the drug trade to examine the cycle of institutional failure.

Sebagaimana diketahui, season 1 of the wire was tightly focused on the drug empire of avon barksdale (wood harris) and his business-savvy second-in-command stringer bell (elba). Season 2 shifted the focus to the city’s port system, a jarring change as many characters faded into the background to make room for the tragic tale of the Sobotka family. The show could find comedy in something as simple as cops struggling to get new furniture into their office, and then gut audiences with the death of a relatable drug dealer. Showrunner David Simon quickly established a brilliant mix of humor and pathos. Season 3 was the most tightly linked to the show’s first season, largely completing the story of the Barksdale gang.

Berdasarkan laporan, that made season 4 perfect for a soft reboot, a shift that was defined by star dominic west all but disappearing after his relentless detective, jimmy mcnulty, was demoted for pissing off his bosses too many times. criminals beats are familiar, they become just one part of a far more ambitious season that fully capitalized on Simon’s knowledge of the city. (Simon worked as a journalist at The Baltimore Sun for 12 years before creating The Wire. Lester Freamon (Clarke Peters) effectively steps into the McNulty role of pursuing the truth, even when his supervisors would love for him to be a little less dogged, bringing a new methodical nature to the investigations instead of McNulty’s brash confidence. But while the cops vs. The detectives he previously worked with in the major crimes unit continue their work, investigating a vicious new gang that’s filling the void Barksdale left behind. ).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the season’s largest secondary plot involves the students at a baltimore middle school where former cop roland pryzbylewski (jim true-frost) begins teaching. By the end of season 4, the system has profoundly failed almost all of these kids, driving them to lives of addiction and violence. You want to root for all of them, from the ambitious Randy Wagstaff (Maestro Harrell) to the fiercely protective Michael Lee (Tristan Wilds). The young actors do a phenomenal job establishing likable characters in terrible circumstances. The Wire was always good at making most of its characters sympathetic, but seeing children trapped in such a brutal cycle really drives home the show’s themes of how crime thrives when institutions fail.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that theme also plays out in the mayoral campaign of tommy carcetti (aidan gillen). Gillen’s oily performance as a political survivor who would doom his city to satisfy his own ambitions was what landed him the role of Littlefinger in Game of Thrones. Carcetti was introduced in season 3 as an ambitious city council member, but he really shines in season 4 as he runs on reforming the Baltimore Police Department — and then quickly breaks his promises. Carcetti is even more compelling a character because he feels like a man who could have done good if he’d been willing to make sacrifices rather than feed his own ego.

Diungkapkan bahwa the wire season 4 is able to build so many new arcs because of the strong foundation established in the previous three seasons. The show is dense with rich characters who have grown significantly over the years even as they continue to struggle with many of the same problems. The cops and drug dealers alike feel world-weary as they deal with a more violent new generation represented by Marlo Stanfield (Jamie Hector) and his vicious enforcers Snoop (Felicia Pearson) and Chris Partlow (Gbenga Akinnagbe). Combined with the dark fate of most of the kids and Carcetti’s broken promises, the season creates the bleak feeling that everyone is trapped in a cycle of misery and decay.

Sebagaimana diketahui, season 5 gave most of the wire’s characters satisfying ends to their arcs and delivered a scathing critique of the downfall of american newspapers, commentary that has only become more profound 20 years later. But overall, it’s a big step down from season 4, spending too much time on a goofy fake serial killer plot and not enough on the nuanced character-driven stories that made season 4 feel so authentic. There are no bad seasons of The Wire, but season 4 perfectly achieved the show’s goals. It’s an alternately funny, tragic, and profound look at the complex ways that people are betrayed by systems that never really give them a chance to succeed.

Berdasarkan laporan, we want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

We held off on season 4 until I was sure I could survive. Although there was an article in the Times a week before the COVID shutdown that explicated how vital the NYC DOE was as a social safety net, and that made me feel both great and depressed.
