#629. The 10 Best Sci-Fi Shows With Less Than 20 Episodes, Ranked

📅 14 Nov 2026

The 10 Best Sci-Fi Shows With Less Than 20 Episodes, Ranked

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/best-sci-fi-shows-shorter-than-20-episodes/

Sebagaimana diketahui, nineteen episodes or fewer. That's all it has taken several of the greatest sci-fi TV shows in history to join the ranks of the best the genre has ever delivered on the small screen. Though this is a genre that lends itself perfectly to long-running shows that deliver hundreds of incredible episodes of hyper-creative television, there's something magical about a tight, concise sci-fi show that doesn't even need 20 episodes to deliver a masterclass in genre storytelling.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, whether we're talking about a miniseries like garth marenghi's darkplace or a full-length show like arcane, these remarkable shows proved beyond a shadow of a doubt that sci-fi doesn't need to run for decades in order to be incredible. For the purposes of this list, only shows that have already delivered their series finale will be counted, seeing as there are some other sci-fi masterpieces which are less than 20 episodes long only because they're still ongoing.

Diungkapkan bahwa it was with wandavision that the mcu made its first true, fully interconnected foray onto the small screen. To this day, however, the highest-rated MCU show from Disney+ on IMDb is Loki, and that's for good reason. We're talking about one of the most perfect superhero shows of the last five years, focused on one of the most universally beloved MCU characters out there.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a solo loki project was long overdue, and fans couldn't have possibly asked for a better final result. With only two seasons and 12 episodes in total, the show delivered some incredible visuals and production values, a delectable high-concept premise that all fans of multiversal sci-fi should love, and a surprisingly emotional climax for Loki's years-long character arc.

Diungkapkan bahwa pitched by creators josé rivera and karl schaefer as a sort of "twin peaks for kids," eerie, indiana is one of the strangest, most fascinatingly surreal children's series in the history of television. It's an absolute tragedy that low ratings and high production costs led NBC to cancel it after only one season and 19 episodes in total, because it really did have the potential to grow into something even better.

Diungkapkan bahwa nonetheless, eerie, indiana has remained one of the biggest cult classic shows of its era as the years since its untimely cancellation have passed, with fans hailing it as one of the few true sci-fi show masterpieces of the '90s. Strongly reminiscent of future classics like Gravity Falls and Stranger Things, it's an exquisitely weird, creative, and at times downright scary little gem of children's television.

Sebagaimana diketahui, screenwriters matthew graham and ashley pharoah originally came up with the idea that would eventually turn into life on mars back in 1998, envisioning a time travel series satirizing '70s society. At the time, broadcasters rejected the concept. It wouldn't be until 2006 that the show would finally see the light of day, and today, many remember it as one of those mystery shows that are perfect from start to finish.

Berdasarkan laporan, blending elements of the police procedural, supernatural drama, and sci-fi historical drama genres, life on mars is one of the greatest british genre shows of the 21st century. With its 16 episodes across a two-season run, it delivered a mind-bending existential mystery that doesn't lose any of its magic even after several revisits. It's creative, it's emotionally moving, and it's philosophically sharp.

Sebagaimana diketahui, seeing as alan moore and dave gibbons' watchmen is universally recognized as one of the most important and influential works of art in the history of comic books, it's unsurprising that the announcement of an hbo television sequel created by lost's damon lindelof had fans feeling skeptical. In the end, divisive though it was (and remains), it would by no means be exaggerated to say that Lindelof's Watchmen went so far as to surpass those expectations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of the most thoroughly perfect must-watch miniseries of the last decade, a nine-episode masterpiece pitched by lindelof as a sort of remix of the original comic series. The show takes the source material's uniquely punchy thematic and philosophical core and masterfully turns it into a sharply 21st-century tale, scathingly talking about themes like systemic racism and historical trauma.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the channel 4 british conspiracy thriller series utopia is one of the greatest cult classics of 2010s television, one of those sci-fi shows with absolutely no filler episodes. Over the course of two seasons and 12 episodes in total, the show delivered a masterfully dark and complex study of themes of deep-state paranoia and utilitarian morality.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, due to its extremely graphic violence and the way it holds back no punches in depicting sensitive topics like school shootings and political assassinations, the show was hugely polarizing and controversial back when it was on air. Though low ratings led Channel 4 to cancel the series, it has remained a taboo-breaking cult classic in the years since, a must-see for people who love transgressive science fiction.

Sebagaimana diketahui, based on their stage show garth marenghi's fright knight, richard ayoade and matthew holness created the channel 4 miniseries garth marenghi's darkplace. Delightfully meta in every way imaginable, this cult classic is both a loving tribute to cheap '80s sci-fi and horror shows and a parody of the pretentious "auteurs" who created them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with an irresistible sense of humor and a cast at the top of their comedic game, garth marenghi's darkplace is one of those miniseries that are absolutely perfect masterpieces, and six episodes were all it took for it to achieve that status. It's campy, it's absurd, it's deceivingly intelligent, and it's endlessly rewatchable in a uniquely (and very intentional) so-bad-it's-good way.

Diungkapkan bahwa fans have been clamoring for a second season of the unfairly-canceled scavengers reign for years, and creators joe bennett and charles huettner have admitted that there certainly are some ideas for a potential revival. Nonetheless, the series was originally pitched as a perfectly self-contained miniseries; and as such, it's an airtight sci-fi story with a perfectly satisfying conclusion, which all those who love the genre should watch at least once.

Diungkapkan bahwa people who think that animation is somehow lesser than live-action science fiction have clearly not watched scavengers reign, one of the best adult animated shows where every episode's a masterpiece. Highly experimental and avant-garde in its approach throughout 12 episodes, it's far more focused on complex character development and incredibly intricate world-building than it is on any traditional sense of plot.

Berdasarkan laporan, as if any more proof were needed that animated science fiction deserves every bit as much respect as live-action science fiction, there's also arcane, netflix's adaptation of the legendary multiplayer online battle arena game league of legends. It happens to be one of the best animated sci-fi shows in history, an absolute masterpiece that requires no prior knowledge of the source material in order to be thoroughly enjoyed.

Diungkapkan bahwa full of richly layered and deeply moving character arcs, simple yet enrapturing world-building, gripping storylines and subplots, and compelling sociopolitical commentary, arcane is science fantasy at its very best. On top of being visually jaw-dropping and full of phenomenal music, it's one of the most engrossingly dramatic and incredibly action-packed adult animated shows that the small screen has seen in quite some time, and 18 episodes across two seasons were all it took for it to achieve that.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, yet another british cult classic that has kept aging like fine wine, patrick mcgoohan's the prisoner (starring mcgoohan himself) is one of those near-perfect sci-fi shows that nobody seems to remember. It follows an unnamed British secret agent who, after resigning from his job, is abducted and taken to a surreal coastal prison known as "The Village," where authorities try to get him to reveal why he quit.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one season, 17 episodes. The show grows more psychedelic, surreal, intellectually challenging, and downright Kafkaesque as it goes on, challenging the norms of episodic television from its time. That's all it took for The Prisoner to see an evolution more dramatic than what many other sci-fi shows see over the course of several seasons. As such, it feels surprisingly modern even today.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there is arguably no single-season sci-fi show more legendary or iconic than firefly, whose untimely cancellation remains one of the biggest tragedies in the modern history of network sci-fi television. Before the arrival of its upcoming animated continuation, now should be as perfect a time as any for those who haven't experienced this essential cult classic to finally give it a go.

Berdasarkan laporan, it's one of the most perfect sci-fi shows of the last 25 years, a space western with some of the most engaging characters and genre-cliché-defying stories that sci-fi has seen on television in a while. It delivers a timeless masterclass in ensemble writing, in delivering futuristic sci-fi grounded in realism, and in balancing episodic and serialized storytelling. It's a cult classic that anyone who loves the genre is pretty much guaranteed to thoroughly enjoy.

#632. Nicholas Hoult Filmed 2 Different Endings for His ‘How to Rob a Bank’ Character

Starring Nicholas Hoult, Pete Davidson, John C. Reilly, Zoë Kravitz, Anna Sawai, and Rhenzy Feliz, the movie takes audiences on a high-octane ride using 35mm film intertwined with attention-grabbing YouTube footage for a final cut even the cast didn’t see coming.

Sebagaimana diketahui, how to rob a bank follows an anonymous youtuber, “the wolf” (hoult), and a group of bank robbers — davidson, sawai, and feliz — who post their capers on the internet. As they continue to see success online, an FBI agent (Reilly) hires a hacker on house arrest (Kravitz) to help put an end to their escapades.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in this interview, collider’s steve weintraub talks with hoult, reilly, sawai, and feliz to discuss their approach to the material, working with leitch on different versions of their scenes, and how the film’s surprising perspectives came together in the end. Check out the full conversation in the video above, with a transcript provided below.

COLLIDER: John, I'm going to start with you.

Yeah, I was just curious how you feel when someone is wearing a bootleg T-shirt of your face during an interview for your new movie.

Diungkapkan bahwa reilly: i'm still getting used to it. Yeah. I'll let you know at the end of the interview.

Diungkapkan bahwa i wore this for something i did with will ferrell, and i handed him a dollar to give him a residual payment. I would do the same for you, but we are virtual.

Sebagaimana diketahui, reilly: you know, i would have done that movie for free. It was a joyful experience. But how about How to Rob a Bank?.

Berdasarkan laporan, i really want to start with congrats on the movie. I think the film does a great job of capturing the anger that so many of us feel about what's going on. But before I get into the film, I'm doing a supercut of everyone I'm interviewing right now, and I'm asking everyone where they like to sit in a movie theater.

Berdasarkan laporan, reilly: i like to sit on the aisle. First seat on the aisle, usually a little bit over to the right, about halfway down.

NICHOLAS HOULT: That’s pretty close to where I like to sit.

HOULT: I'm not necessarily right on the aisle, but close enough that if I have to get up, I don't have to go right past everyone.

Sebagaimana diketahui, feliz: i try to do everything possible to never have to get up through the movie, so i will do whatever i gotta do. Middle, but close-ish. I like to go middle. Not too close, but not middle-middle. Closer than middle, but not all the way forward.

Berdasarkan laporan, feliz: normally, it’s g. It’s right in the middle of G. At the Lincoln Center, it's G. So that’s, like, six, or something.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, anna sawai: [laughs] i'm in the middle but towards the back. But I like to be in the center.

HOULT: Does anybody ever say, like, front left?.

Berdasarkan laporan, i've had people say they actually like being the first or second row. I think they're insane, but by all means. That's the great thing about this question is you get all sorts of answers.

REILLY: Well, there's always a seat available if it gets crowded, because most people don't pick that front row.

Sebagaimana diketahui, from 'talladega nights' to 'step brothers,' these are some of john c. Reilly's funniest performances to date.

Jumping into why I get to talk to you guys, like I said, I really do think that this captures a lot of the anger that so many of us feel, and I'm just curious, how did the finished film actually compare to the script you read and what David [Leitch] told you about it going in?.

Berdasarkan laporan, sawai: i feel like when i read it, i was reading with emmy in mind, and so everything kind of felt really heavy. But I was surprised at how entertaining and fun it was, because I forgot that it was more of that in the film.

Berdasarkan laporan, feliz: i guess maybe, yeah, a similar thing where the perspective was from the robbers’ side, and then when i watched the final version of it, it felt like so much more of the perspective was sort of looking at us instead of it coming from us. I felt the audience would maybe know more about us, and when I watched, I was like, “Oh, we're a little bit out of reach, just slightly. And I think I also felt more mysterious in the edit when I watched the movie than I felt when I was making it. ” Like, it's the chase, which I think actually, it's better than what I had thought up in my head when I was reading the script.

Berdasarkan laporan, hoult: seeing the film was exciting because, like rhenzy was saying, all of john and zoë [kravitz]’s part of the movie we weren't present for. So, to see how they developed those characters and that side of the story was really exciting and fun to watch.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, then these robberies, because they're so different, the film parts of this are so grounded and lived in and very beautifully shot, and then this content that they create is so fast. The way that that was shot with these POV cameras and lenses attached to us and the stunt team itself, it was so frantic. So to see how those things combined, I just think David did a really creative, wonderful job mixing those mediums in many ways.

Diungkapkan bahwa but also, he's so open to ideas and trying things that even whether my character died or didn't die wasn't decided fully. So we shot both versions of that towards the end of the movie, and it was only when he was done editing and stuff that he made the final decision on those things. So, it's kind of a nice surprise seeing the movie for me because there were lots of undecided things. [Laughs].

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, reilly: i think playing a character in a movie is similar to life, in that everyone walks through life like they're the lead character. And then you see all this is social media content that's part of the movie and what's actually happening in the heist and everything. And so I thought the movie was about a guy trying to catch some bank robbers. You know, your experiences, the way you're seeing your life. So yeah, like Nick was just saying, it’s always a delight to see the parts of the movie that you were not present for when it was being filmed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nick, i really think that the youtube stuff that's in this is just so well done. I’m curious if, as you were filming it, did you gain a newfound respect for content creators being able to talk to the camera and pull you in?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this team is obviously really great at it and has tapped into a nerve. And like you were saying, people are angry about many different things, so there's this element of creating a voice for people that feel like they aren't being heard is a special thing. But yeah, it gave me a whole new level of respect because it's not something I could do — particularly while I was robbing banks.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, 100%. One of the things I love learning about is the behind-the-scenes, the making of a movie, and I love learning shit that you cannot find on Wikipedia or in the press notes. For soon-to-be fans of the film, is there anything that you think would be cool to learn or exciting or unique about actually making this film?.

Berdasarkan laporan, reilly: the guns had blanks in them. They weren't actual, real bullets.

Berdasarkan laporan, hoult: every sixth one was a real bullet, and they wouldn't tell us. [Laughs].

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the things i'm so curious about is when you guys are making a movie like this, the four of you are never working together. This is like your first day, when you're doing press, that you're with each other. What have you learned about each other through a day of doing press?.

Berdasarkan laporan, reilly: i've learned if there's a pause, i'll start talking. I’ve learned that about myself.

Berdasarkan laporan, hoult: i've learned to pause so that john will start talking. We went to go to dinner together. No, actually, when we all got to Pittsburgh, us four were the first four people to hang out. So, this is like the reunion of the OG core group.

REILLY: Yeah, and my first day was the interrogations, so I actually spent the day with everybody the very first day of shooting.

Sebagaimana diketahui, feliz: we’re all great friends. We've done it all. We've done roller coaster rides. We've done pickle rides. We're a tight-knit unit.

That’s only if you still have a text chain going.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, feliz: well, actually, for a while there, we did, and it was one of the highlights of my day, actually. We gotta fire that back up again.

I love learning about how actors get ready for a role or a big scene, so when you're making a film like this or filming in general, and you have a big scene coming up on a Monday, how are you getting ready for that? Is it in the days leading up to it, or are you always thinking about it weeks in advance? I'm just fascinated by how actors get ready for a role or a big scene, because it's something that I could never do myself.

Sebagaimana diketahui, reilly: well, there’s the learning of dialogue, of course, memorizing your lines and all that stuff, but i find myself really making sure that i understand the emotional shifts in the scene — when things change, when does the temperature in the room change when someone says this or that — and then you kind of compare notes with the director when you get there. You know, you give your take on it.

I think every actor has their own process, actually, very individually, but my thing is I always try to leave enough space so that in case my interpretation is not what the director wants, that I can pivot, that I'm not set in something so much that I can't do what they want me to do.

Diungkapkan bahwa hoult: i try not to think of it as a big scene if it's a big scene. Does that make sense? Because if you're like, “Oh, this is a big scene,” then you're probably going to intimidate yourself into not being loose and free with it. So I try and prepare as much as possible, but then also remember that it's a culmination of all the scenes and all the work that make the difference, not necessarily this one pivotal thing, so you can go in there and approach it with a sense of ease and have fun with it, I guess.

Sebagaimana diketahui, feliz: that's something i still got to learn. I feel like I try not to think of it as such a big thing, but I find myself….

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, hoult: well, i still do it. I’m still like, “It's a big one!”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, feliz: yeah, i know the day it’s coming up. You guys actually both said it. But I think what you said was crucial. You prepare, and you try to figure out exactly what the heck's going on with your character in the moment, and all the lines, and you know everything, hopefully, so well that you can sort of feel the freedom to go in and try to find something natural and fun and spontaneous amidst all the preparation.

Diungkapkan bahwa i think the only times i've ever felt comfortable going into big days is when i feel like i know so much about what's going on in the moment with the character, with the scene and the movie in that moment that i'm open to so many different kinds of things happening on the day. But I've been guilty of maybe not being prepared as much as I should have on some days, and that's when I go into it the most nervous and the most in my head about things.

Berdasarkan laporan, sawai: also, sometimes they can change the script the day before. So, you do as much preparation as you can, like they said, but yeah, you just have to go in and do what you can.

How to Rob a Bank opens in theaters on November 13.

Diungkapkan bahwa looking ahead to the future of animation, knight sees little has changed since laika began. Both Coraline and Wildwood were a fight to get made.

Diungkapkan bahwa “it’s getting harder and harder to make anything with consolidation,” knight said. We’re one voice. We have to. “Art needs advocacy. It needs champions. Others will join us. That’s what we’re trying to do at the studio. ”.

Deschanel also added hope for a broader approach to animation for all ages.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “animation doesn’t just have to be for small children,” deschanel said. “The possibility for creating wonderful, deep stories are there. ”.

#639. Is ‘Club Kid’ a ‘Conservative’ Movie? Only If You’re Still Living in the ’60s

📅 14 Nov 2026

Is ‘Club Kid’ a ‘Conservative’ Movie? Only If You’re Still Living in the ’60s

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://variety.com/2026/film/columns/is-club-kid-a-conservative-movie-jordan-firstman-1236947691/

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the things i love about movies is how layered they are. Chasing down a movie’s inner meaning can lead you into the mystery of things. When a film connects on a deep level, saying what it’s truly “about” may not be as simple as it sounds. A great movie can be “about” more than it seems.

Diungkapkan bahwa take “club kid. Firstman, who gives a fantastic performance, plays Peter, a queer New York party promoter (a few decades ago we would have called him “downtown,” now he’s Brooklyn) who learns that he has a 9-year-old son, whom he fathered in a random three-way sexual encounter at one of his 4:00 a. club bacchanals. m. But as he and the kid start to hang out, a tentative relationship forms, and the two begin to figure out what they might mean to each other. It’s something he doesn’t want and, for the time being, doesn’t have much choice about. ” Jordan Firstman’s ebullient and moving first feature tells a story that couldn’t be more straightforward — or, in a way, more traditional. The responsibility to take care of Arlo has suddenly dropped on Peter like a load of bricks. The kid, Arlo (Reggie Absolom), is sweet and curly-haired and British (he arrives with a chaperone from London); his mother, who raised him, recently committed suicide. Related Stories 'Hold Onto Me' Director Myrsini Aristidou Kicks Off Historic Oscar Campaign for Sundance Audience Award Winner: 'I Really Feel Like We're Underdogs'.

Diungkapkan bahwa what “club kid” is “about” is how peter, a charming dissolute man-child, living an existence of unhinged hedonism, discovers that he wants to grow up and take care of someone besides himself. In outline, though, it’s something we’ve seen many times before, in films from “About a Boy” to “Big Daddy. On that score, the drama is authentic and fully felt. ” Yet what makes “Club Kid” singular is that it’s about something larger than that.

Berdasarkan laporan, as a filmmaker, firstman plunges you into the world of queer club culture with a fervor and tumult and personality and lived-in detail that takes your breath away. He plunks the audience down in the middle of the shade-throwing nightbloom revels, the cocaine and ketamine binges, so that we experience the cathartic rush of drugged-out insolence, of heightened erotic excitement, of gender-flipping transgression. From the earliest days of gay liberation, the party scene was a core expression of queer freedom, and still is. The staging of these scenes, and the acting in them, is extraordinary. What we call disco started in the underground gay clubs of the early ’70s, and part of Peter’s cachet as a promoter is that what’s he organizing is now a business, but it’s still underground. Jordan Firstman makes us feel the life of the party.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and yet…he’s not merely celebrating it. Far from it. As authentic and scene-specific as they are, the party sequences in “Club Kid” signify as more than just a portrayal of the New York queer club scene. They’re also a larger snapshot of what party culture, out there in the world, has become: an arena of liberation that’s rooted in a place of physical and spiritual abandon that contains the seeds of destruction.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you wanted to encapsulate the history of the last six decades in one sentence, you could do worse than this: ever since the late ’60s, the party has never stopped. It might have been the punk mosh pits, or the revels of Studio 54, or the back-to-the-underground scene of Basement. There are countless versions of the party, and we’ve all been to our own preferred versions. It might have been the suburban saturnalia of “Jersey Shore,” or the more contempo versions of that. It might have been the industrial dance clubs of the ’80s or the raves of the ’90s. It might have been the singles bars of the disco age, or the frat-house benders that came to rule in the late ’70s — and have only grown more frenzied and predatory ever since. The music, the drugs, the alcohol, the hooking up, the vibe of orgiastic excess — for 60 years now, we’ve been a culture on the prowl.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in “club kid,” it’s not just peter who starts to question the party culture that has fueled him. It’s asking, “Is this how we should be living?” And yet, because the movie dares to pose that question, there has been a backlash against it, with a chorus of voices damning the movie by branding it “conservative. The film itself is questioning it. ” A certain number of people are looking at “Club Kid,” with its tale of a queer man who turns his back on his own personal decadence to embrace the call of family, as if it were a movie Nancy Reagan could love.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what i think the “conservative” slur misses is that jordan firstman, who came out of this scene, is not questioning it in a puritanical or moralistic way. He captures the honest vibrance of party culture. The party doesn’t need to stop. That’s the hidden seduction of party culture, the thrill and the beauty of it, and maybe the lie of it. Yet he also captures — and this is what I think is brilliant about “Club Kid” — that whatever version of it floats your boat, the party that never stops, while rooted in a certain vibe of community, may be rooted even more deeply in the enticement we feel from getting high on ourselves. But it might be time that we stopped seeing it as an uncut salvation without ever pausing to ask, as “Club Kid” does, what it’s doing to us.

It’s amazing to me that people know you’re playing a character and you’re still able to get the kinds of reactions you do from them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, morgan it started in little two-minute sections [on weekly wipe]. It’s a nice way to test out a character. Sebagaimana diketahui, morgan it was complete ripoff of physicist brian cox’s documentary that had just gone out. It’s always good to spoof something. You’ve got a template for something; now just take the piss out of the whole thing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, brooker i think we pitched a weekly show that was just philomena [to the bbc], and they were like, we can’t quite commit to that yet. But we’ve got a season of shows coming up because it was the anniversary of Shakespeare’s [death]. They said why don’t you try doing Cunk on Shakespeare as a one-off? Sebagaimana diketahui, morgan it’s sort of me if i had no social skills, but also, i can use all those tropes that other documentary makers use. They all go on a journey. They all do the same things. Berdasarkan laporan, brooker in cunk on britain, we had a running joke where it was [cutaways to] brush strokes, a british sitcom from the 1980s which had a theme song by kevin rowland of dexy’s midnight runners. We would show the opening sequence of Brush Strokes almost in full.

#658. Battle Royale Told A More Brutal Version Of The Hunger Games 12 Years Earlier

📅 14 Nov 2026

Battle Royale Told A More Brutal Version Of The Hunger Games 12 Years Earlier

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/hunger-games-battle-royale-japanese-movie-comparison/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, japanese cinema offered a rendition of the hunger games 12 years earlier, and it’s so much more intense. Young adult dystopian fiction has produced some of the most successful entertainment franchises of the 21st century. Few have made a bigger impression than The Hunger Games, Suzanne Collins' bestselling book series and its hugely successful film adaptations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the hunger games franchise established a distinctive formula for dystopian blockbuster filmmaking, combining political commentary with high-stakes survival drama. However, the idea of forcing young people to fight one another to the death in a government-controlled competition wasn't new when Collins introduced Panem. In fact, a Japanese filmmaker had already explored a remarkably similar premise, taking it in a considerably more violent and disturbing direction.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, released more than a decade before the first hunger games movie, battle royale is one of the most provocative dystopian movies ever made. Its influence and similarities to Collins' franchise continue to invite comparisons, particularly among those who want something considerably more brutal after finishing Katniss Everdeen's story.

Sebagaimana diketahui, directed by kinji fukasaku in 2000, battle royale adapted koushun takami's 1999 novel of the same name. The premise will sound immediately familiar to anyone who has watched The Hunger Games: a totalitarian government selects a group of teenagers, transports them to an isolated location, and forces them to fight until only one remains alive. However, while Katniss Everdeen enters the arena as part of a televised competition, the students in Battle Royale are victims of a government program intended to terrorize an increasingly rebellious younger generation.

Berdasarkan laporan, battle royale centers on a class of 42 junior high school students who are abducted during a school trip and transported to an island. Their former teacher, Kitano, explains that they have been selected under the Battle Royale Act, a government policy that forces one school class to participate in a three-day fight to the death. Each student receives supplies and a randomly assigned weapon, while explosive collars ensure nobody can simply refuse to participate or escape.

Diungkapkan bahwa the basic mechanics are remarkably similar to the hunger games, but fukasaku's film makes the experience considerably less like a sporting event. There are no elaborate opening ceremonies, celebrity stylists, or opportunities to cultivate public affection. The teenagers are simply abandoned with instructions to kill their classmates, and the government expects them to comply.

Rather than turning violence into an elaborate national spectacle, it presents the competition as a bleak institutional punishment designed to demonstrate the consequences of challenging authority.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the most obvious differences between battle royale and the hunger games is their respective approaches to violence. The Hunger Games certainly contains disturbing material, particularly considering its teenage characters, but its PG-13 classification required fairly restrained bloodshed. Fukasaku, meanwhile, makes little effort to soften the brutality.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, students are shot, stabbed, beaten, and blown apart, with battle royale frequently emphasizing the physical consequences of each confrontation. Fukasaku gives several students individual personalities and relationships before subjecting them to sudden, shocking deaths. Its violence isn't restricted to the anonymous background deaths of characters audiences barely know, either. The contrast between their ordinary teenage lives and the savagery of the competition is precisely what makes it so uncomfortable.

Diungkapkan bahwa the sudden deaths reinforce how little control the students have over their circumstances. Even characters who initially appear confident or capable of surviving can be killed within moments, often by people they previously considered friends. The arbitrary distribution of weapons makes matters worse, ensuring that some students begin with a significant advantage over others.

Berdasarkan laporan, there is also a particularly nasty sense of unpredictability to the film's violence. The Hunger Games establishes a more conventional progression of alliances, confrontations, and strategic eliminations, whereas Battle Royale frequently allows paranoia and panic to dictate what happens next.

Sebagaimana diketahui, despite their obvious similarities, battle royale and the hunger games approach their dystopian settings from different political perspectives. Both examine authoritarian governments that maintain control through fear, using young people as instruments of state power. However, The Hunger Games focuses particularly on class inequality, propaganda, and the exploitation of poverty.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, panem's hunger games are an annual reminder of the capitol's victory over the rebellious districts. The wealthy citizens are encouraged to treat the deaths of teenagers as entertainment, while the impoverished districts are forced to sacrifice their children.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, battle royale, by contrast, focuses more on generational conflict and the breakdown of trust between adults and children. Its fictional government responds to fears about juvenile delinquency by introducing a policy that effectively declares an entire generation expendable. The students are punished collectively, regardless of whether they have actually committed any wrongdoing.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, battle royale doesn’t present a conventional heroic rebellion but rather examines what happens when a society teaches its children to distrust one another. Its characters are frequently frightened, selfish, impulsive, and emotionally overwhelmed, which makes them seem considerably closer to ordinary teenagers than the increasingly strategic competitors of Panem.

Diungkapkan bahwa for anyone who loves the hunger games, battle royale is a perfect next watch because it offers the deadly survival premise in a much less sanitized form. Both put teenagers in situations where survival means confronting people they know, but Battle Royale’s approach makes the psychological and physical consequences much more immediate. There is no glamorous preparation for the competition, no carefully managed public image, and no expectation that the contestants will become celebrities.

Diungkapkan bahwa the hunger games examines how an authoritarian government uses spectacle and propaganda to maintain power, whereas battle royale spotlights the destruction of trust between ordinary people. The films also make an interesting double feature because their protagonists respond to institutional cruelty in different ways.

Sebagaimana diketahui, katniss gradually becomes a symbol of rebellion, while shuya and noriko are primarily concerned with surviving. As a result, Battle Royale is particularly valuable for anyone interested in dystopian narratives that don’t adhere to classic Hollywood blockbuster storytelling.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, battle royale is particularly effective at exploring the emotional consequences of its premise without turning every character into a perfectly calculated survivalist. The friendships, romances, jealousies, and petty disagreements that define school life don't suddenly disappear when the students are given weapons. Instead, those familiar relationships become the foundation for some of the film's most upsetting moments.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ultimately, battle royale deserves to be watched on its own merits rather than simply as the japanese predecessor to the hunger games. Its examination of institutional cruelty, teenage alienation, and the destructive consequences of authoritarianism gives it considerably more substance than its notorious reputation for violence might suggest. Fans of The Hunger Games adventures will recognize plenty of familiar ideas, but Fukasaku's film takes them somewhere much darker.

Diungkapkan bahwa the hunger games is the first of four in the action-drama movie series based on the novels by suzanne collins. Set in a dystopian world where people are separated into twelve districts to maintain order, this first film in the franchise focuses on Katniss Everdeen as she is forced to participate in The Hunger Games: a draconian gladiatorial survival event where there can be only one winner.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the dystopian action movie battle royale takes place in a future japan, where a group of high school students fight to the death in a deserted island until only one survivor remains. Directed by Kinji Fukasaku, the 2000 film gave rise to a whole genre of similar stories such as the Hunger Games books and movies, as well as the video game Fortnite.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the amount of times i’ve been called a fire hazard, it’s going to be the name of my autobiography. I’m telling you, it’s the perfect title,” Madeley said at Deadline’s Contenders Film Los Angeles.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, madeley was joined on the panel by casting directors bernard telsey and adam caldwell to discuss the apple original films drama being heumann. S. Co-written and directed by Oscar-winning CODA filmmaker Siân Heder, the film adapts Heumann’s memoir, following the disability rights advocate as more than 100 disabled protesters occupied the San Francisco Federal Building in 1977. Their 28-day sit-in became the longest occupation of a federal building in U. history.

Madeley read extensively and scoured footage of Heumann, looking for the details that would bring her personality into the performance.

Diungkapkan bahwa “but also from a craft perspective, all of the other things that i wanted to show of her, like her humor, her joy — she was really cheeky, and i loved that charm that she had even when she was forgetting her pleases and her thank yous sometimes. “And the tiny things about her, how her accent shifts as well when she’s with her friends rather than when she’s in front of the press, and you can see in performance the tone shifts, she uses bigger words. Everyone’s rooting for her because she’s so damn charming,” Madeley said. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, she also studied how heumann moved. “It was important for me to honor her physicality and the differences between her disability and my own. I wanted to make sure they were truthful as well as all her characteristics,” Madeley said.

Diungkapkan bahwa telsey and caldwell had previously auditioned madeley for wicked. Her audition for Judy quickly got them excited. “We knew that she had the chutzpah, I like to say, that Judy had, even though she’s not from Brooklyn,” Telsey said.

Diungkapkan bahwa casting the wider ensemble meant reaching beyond familiar audition channels, given the film’s inclusive nature and the real-life movement. And in most projects, you might have one character that needs that, maybe two, maybe,” Caldwell said. “But seeing this, we had to be really methodical about, OK, so we’re going to start with Judy, we’re going to start with women in wheelchairs, and we’re going to do something as comprehensive as possible, doing open calls for anyone with a disability that wants to be considered, to see thousands of people that way, however we can. “I think as casting directors, we love a good search. We love when we get to go deep, find people, and do it expansively. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, those open calls were one part of the work. So to do a targeted search for a young Black blind man, to do a targeted search for people with cerebral palsy, to do the deaf community, do it one at a time on a rolling basis and try to keep them all organized and straight and moving forward simultaneously. Caldwell explained: “But then we had to start being targeted and actually making sure that the people we needed for these historical characters knew we wanted them. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the takeaway, he said, was simple: “the lesson learned is that they’re out there. If you’re given the time to go look for them, you can find them. ”.

#674. The 10 Most Hopeless Christmas Movies, Ranked

📅 14 Nov 2026

The 10 Most Hopeless Christmas Movies, Ranked

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/most-hopeless-christmas-movies-ranked/

Sebagaimana diketahui, there’s no shortage of feel-good christmas movies. Some will have dramatic moments, sure, but you can’t really call It’s a Wonderful Life downbeat or hopeless when it ends up feeling life-affirming and hopeful by the end. So, it’s not a movie that you'll see mentioned below, nor will you see other movies that have a lot of drama but wholly inspiring endings (see also most adaptations of A Christmas Carol).

Diungkapkan bahwa instead, what you'll see below are the most hopeless christmas movies of all time. They generally work as good anti-Christmas movies, telling darker stories that just so happen to play out during the holiday season. They're not all 100% heavy, because some are more cynical than tragic, though in one way or another, they do ultimately stand out against the more conventional Christmas movies out there that you’ve probably seen discussed (and recommended) to death.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the ref is a well-made comedic crime film that just so happens to take place on christmas eve, and mostly concerns a bunch of generally unlikable characters clashing, and then it’s kind of funny because no one’s sympathetic. If you take a step back, or try to imagine yourself stuck in this film, then it would be miserable, and that sense of it all being cynical is what makes it clash with most Christmas movies and the sentiments found within them.

There is certainly a time and place for anti-Christmas movies, especially if you're not someone who feels like engaging with the season this year, for whatever reason.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the antagonist here is a burglar who takes a family hostage, but the family is a dysfunctional one, and everyone ends up making everyone feel worse. There is certainly a time and place for anti-Christmas movies, especially if you're not someone who feels like engaging with the season this year, for whatever reason, and so something pessimistic like The Ref has got your back, in that instance.

Diungkapkan bahwa what do you want, or what were you expecting? it’s a movie called bad santa. Okay, Bad Santa is good, but it’s not really feel-good; that’s the unsurprising part. It’s one of the better R-rated Christmas movies out there, and it might also be one of the “most R-rated” Christmas movies, too, because it's about a miserable conman who robs department stores while dressed up as a mall Santa, and then things change for him to some extent when he meets a young kid who’s struggling socially.

Diungkapkan bahwa only “to some extent,” since it’s not really warm and fuzzy, by any means. There is a tiny bit of heart here that stops this from being utterly depressing and nihilistic, yet a lot of the humor comes from that, and Billy Bob Thornton is very much the right person to cast if you want that kind of energy, too. It might not be the kind of dark Christmas movie that'll appeal to everyone, for obvious reasons, but it will likely appeal to you if you're after a Christmas-themed dark comedy.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there were a ton of great movies released in 1984, including gremlins. This is also an all-timer if you're looking at subversive and possibly "edgy" Christmas movies, and sure, while it’s not as dark or twisted as some other films here, it’s a pretty wild one for something that’s kind of family-friendly. It’s grisly for something that older kids could probably still watch, and the way it goes from being very jolly and cozy to violent and chaotic is great.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the plot… you know the plot, right? it’s gremlins. It’s a creature feature, and one of the best ever made. And it memorably ruins the magic of Christmas for potential younger viewers, thanks to having a character monologue about the awful event in her life that made her realize Santa wasn’t real. It's a dark and very funny film that's willing to strip away some of the typical magic of Christmas, in turn crafting something wilder and weirder than most Christmas movies. Merry Christmas!.

Diungkapkan bahwa this one is only slightly a christmas movie, lacking the iconography and warmth you'd associate with such a film, but still, the lion in winter is worthy of getting a shout-out here. The premise does ultimately concern a dysfunctional family coming together for the holiday season and arguing a great deal, since they're not just any family, but the royal one, and the King, Henry II, has a few heirs who are power-hungry.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s like succession but set a bit over eight centuries ago, though it doesn’t really feel like your average period drama, because there’s a lot of energy here and an incredible script that feels more modern (but not in a distracting way). The Lion in Winter is excellent as a film on its own, and so maybe the Christmas stuff kind of comes second, but the quality of it overall makes it feel hard to overlook. And, once more, it’s a good anti-Christmas movie, especially if you don’t particularly love the yearly requirement to come together as a family.

Berdasarkan laporan, there’s one other christmas-themed slasher movie that’ll be mentioned further down, because it is admittedly more intense and harrowing than black christmas. To some extent, Black Christmas is slightly cozy, but it is also tense for its time, not to mention important in the overall history of the slasher genre, since Black Christmas pre-dated other slashers like the original Halloween and Friday the 13th movies by a few years.

Sebagaimana diketahui, pretty wild to consider there was an essential christmas slasher movie before there was a true “halloween” slasher movie; not the holiday you'd expect to be prioritized. Anyway, it’s about the members of a sorority house getting tormented and eventually hunted down by a mysterious killer. Simple stuff, but it’s a slasher movie, so of course it’s not going to be complicated. Black Christmas does what it needs to, and it also did so before a good many other slasher films. Much of it holds up, too (don’t bother with the more recent remakes/updates).

Diungkapkan bahwa batman returns confirms that gotham city celebrates christmas. The film plays out when things are snowy and festive, and then it’s notably also quite dark for a superhero movie of its era. 1989’s Batman was already more intense than much of what came before, but Batman Returns is next-level in that regard, pushing things about as far as they can go while (just) retaining a PG-13 rating.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it’s almost a bit much. And sure, other movies here have more violence and profanity, but all this unpleasantness feels a little different in a film like this. So, Batman Returns is more of a cult thing, but the people who do feel this is a cult classic are passionate about Batman Returns; make no mistake. And even if you don’t love it, or enjoy it, it’s not hard to admire how gutsy this one was, and how effectively anti-Christmas it feels among Christmas movies.

Berdasarkan laporan, eyes wide shut was the final film stanley kubrick ever directed, and it came out posthumously. It is kind of a Christmas movie, taking place at the end of the year and having some of the iconography you'd expect to see, but thematically, it’s not very Christmassy. Nor does it really scream Christmas narratively, since it’s about a man putting himself in great danger psychologically and physically when he spirals after learning his wife once thought about cheating on him.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what happens around the middle of eyes wide shut is absolutely horrifying, and then the final act is about the aftermath of all that, and unsettling in more subdued ways. It’s one of the more anxiety-provoking movies of its era for sure, but it is great, both for its direction and for how well-acted it is (Tom Cruise especially seems willing to do just about anything Kubrick asked of him, so he gives one of his most committed performances here).

Diungkapkan bahwa with terrifier 3, you get more terrifier, for better or worse. Art tortures people. You know the drill. Art torments people. It’s Terrifier set around Christmastime, so Art the Clown does some of his rampage while being dressed like Santa Claus, and after doing something (expectedly) horrifying to another person dressed up as Santa. Art (eventually) kills people, after they’ve experienced the most pain possible.

Sebagaimana diketahui, beyond the bloodshed, there are a few things going on narratively, at least more so than the first movie, and as a continuation of the second movie (also better than the first), terrifier 3 works pretty well. You shouldn’t watch it if you're even a tiny bit squeamish, and there is a whole lot of gore and stress here, but these are all extreme horror movies, so if you’ve been fooled by Terrifier three times now, hoping for something different each time a new one comes out… like, come on.

Berdasarkan laporan, the main reason to watch spencer is kristen stewart’s performance as princess diana, though you could also watch it if you like christmas movies but don’t want to watch a nice/happy christmas movie. It takes place during the holiday season, and is focused on Diana struggling with her marriage and being wrapped up in the royal family, with no one in the institution coming away from things looking particularly good (other than Princess Diana and maybe her two songs).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it's an unrelenting historical drama, but it gets heavy and feels intensely solemn for a good reason, demystifying things and being empathetic toward diana. Spencer is no ordinary biopic, both because it’s quite dark and also because the timeframe here is rather narrow, but it’s pretty great for what it does and how intense it ends up being. And, once more, Stewart hasn’t even been better than she is here in the lead role.

Berdasarkan laporan, you have to squint more than usual to see this as a christmas movie, even compared to some of the other films here, but brazil takes place at the year’s end, and there’s some christmas-like imagery. It’s easier to describe as an essential cult classic sci-fi film, and also a very dark comedy, being about a bureaucrat whose life absolutely spirals out of control, largely due to his world being terrible and his luck being even worse.

Diungkapkan bahwa the line between reality and fantasy breaks down, though not to the extent that you ever entirely forget just how horrible the dystopian world brazil takes place in truly is. The way it wraps up is especially soul-crushing, and though before that point, much of Brazil is comedic, it’s also an exhausting sort of comedy. If you don’t like feeling more stressed than usual around Christmas, maybe it’s better to wait and watch this one at a different point in the year.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fall is always rubber soul season. The Beatles’ 1965 masterpiece has always been autumn-coded, with its bristling guitars, wistful vocals, pensive lyrics. Their most emotional album. Their wittiest. Their moodiest. But this fall, Rubber Soul has been in the air even more than usual, because of the phenomenal new Special Edition, which gets you up close with John, Paul, George, and Ringo like never before. Their best.

Sebagaimana diketahui, so what is it that makes rubber soul the beatles’ best album? it’s a loaded question, but for some of us, there’s a correct answer, and it’s simple: it all comes down to the singing. In addition to everything else it is, Rubber Soul is the best place to hear John, Paul, George, and Ringo sing together. It’s four boys telling their stories out loud—you can hear them puzzling out the tales as they sing, bouncing ideas off each other, daring each other to dig a little deeper.

Diungkapkan bahwa over the decades, each era chooses its own beatles album to deify as the ultimate fabs masterpiece. Pepper; the CD era chose Revolver; the streaming era has anointed Abbey Road. Mustard to pretend you don’t have a favorite, and for me, that’s always been Rubber Soul.

Berdasarkan laporan, the beatles had to bash out this album in a hurry, in october 1965, to rush some product into the shops in time for christmas. But they had a phenomenal hot streak. They wrote seven of the songs in a week, pushing the deadline right down to the final hours. (Or should we say, it once had them?) Even the quickies have soul — like “Michelle,” a trifle Paul wrote in his teens for the specific purpose of wooing Liverpool art-student girls by pretending to be French.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but the thing that makes rubber soul stand out, head and moptops above the rest, is the singing, with these four boys mingling their voices, each sha-la-la and each na-na-na, each in-my-life and no-i-wouldn’t so charged with raw emotion. Their voices were changing from boys to men — Ringo and John were 25, Paul 23, George 22 — and you can hear their irresistible excitement that they can now emote as the world-weary men they always aspired to be. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the lads were cranking around the clock to get rubber soul finished. #685. ‘The Good Daughter’ Stars Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy on Playing Sisters With Secrets and That Twisty Killer Ending

📅 14 Nov 2026

‘The Good Daughter’ Stars Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy on Playing Sisters With Secrets and That Twisty Killer Ending

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/the-good-daughter-spoilers-rose-byrne-meghann-fahy-season-finale-1236945641/

SPOILER ALERT: This interview contains major spoilers from “The Good Daughter,” now streaming on Peacock.

For Sam and Charlie Quinn, the estranged sisters played by Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy in “The Good Daughter,” the truth was always going to set them free.

Sebagaimana diketahui, adapted by author karin slaughter from her own bestselling novel of the same name, the six-episode peacock series gradually unravels a southern gothic family mystery. More than 20 years earlier, two masked gunmen broke into the Quinns’ rural Georgia home, murdering their mother, Gamma (Olivia Williams), and leaving both sisters with life-altering injuries. Rather than bonding them, the tragedy and a subsequent web of secrets drove the girls apart, culminating in a bitter falling-out a decade ago despite their shared career path. While Sam built a lucrative career in patent law in New York City, Charlie followed in her father Rusty’s (Brendan Gleeson) footsteps to practice criminal defense law in their shady fictional hometown of Pikeville.

Berdasarkan laporan, but when charlie witnesses a tragic school shooting that leaves principal douglas pinkman (kovar mcclure) and a young student dead, sam is pulled back to her old stomping grounds after rusty is badly injured taking the suspect’s case. Forced to step in for her father despite not having very much experience as a defense attorney, Sam reluctantly agrees to represent Kelly Wilson (Shayna Benardo), the pregnant teen who allegedly confessed to killing her principal and a much younger student.

Sebagaimana diketahui, over the course of the season, with the help of charlie and her estranged husband ben (michael dorman), sam discovers that kelly was merely a pawn used by judith (paula malcomson), the kind teacher who looked after charlie following gamma’s death. Upon discovering her husband Douglas had abused and impregnated Kelly — and expected them all to raise the child together — Judith manipulated the unstable teen into bringing a gun to school, planning to kill Douglas and blame Kelly. But when Kelly hesitated to shoot, Judith seized the weapon, executing Douglas and accidentally killing another kid in the ensuing struggle.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at the same time, the shooting resurfaces old memories for both quinn sisters. As Sam digs deeper into the past, the truth of that tragic day finally comes to light: Charlie had been sexually assaulted by Zach Culpepper — one of Rusty’s most dangerous clients who owed him thousands in legal bills — and the brutal home invasion that resulted in Gamma’s murder had been orchestrated by Mason “Huck” Huckabee (Jake McDorman), a man with whom Charlie had a one-night stand right before the school shooting in the first episode.

Sebagaimana diketahui, though charlie had forced rusty to keep her assault a secret for decades, confronting these buried traumas finally breaks down the walls threatening charlie’s relationship with sam — and her marriage to ben. “It’s always really hard when we have things that we don’t like about ourselves, or things that we haven’t confronted about ourselves,” Fahy tells Variety. “That can be a really hard thing to communicate to someone else because when you operate out of a place of hurt, you do close yourself off from the people that you actually want to be closest to. I think that is true for the sisters and the beginning of the series, and then you have the payoff of watching them come through the other side of that and come back together. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the conversation below, conducted separately, byrne (also an executive producer) and fahy discuss the “corrosive” nature of family secrets, why they believe sam and charlie are ultimately more alike than different — and whether that cathartic finale is truly the last we’ve seen of the quinn sisters onscreen together. Related Stories 'Hold Onto Me' Director Myrsini Aristidou Kicks Off Historic Oscar Campaign for Sundance Audience Award Winner: 'I Really Feel Like We're Underdogs'.

Diungkapkan bahwa rose byrne: the estrangement and the origin story of sam returning home to face her personal truths was really intriguing. I thought the nature of truth was also really interesting — [with] one person’s perspective then shifting to another and the tension of that, and the great suspenseful nature of the story. She had such fury and anger, which she speaks about in the show and in the book a lot, but [I was interested in] her coming to terms with her anger toward her father and his decisions that led them to this tragedy they find themselves in. That genre has always been really fun to me, and something I hadn’t done for a long time, so it was fun to revisit those tropes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meghann fahy: ultimately, the thing that really attracted me to the show is that, when you zoom out, it really is the story of confronting your grief and your trauma and the things that keep us at an arm’s length from the people that we love. It tells a story of coming out on the other side of that stronger and living more of a connected existence, and then drawing the people that you love closer to you as a result of having really faced yourself.

Berdasarkan laporan, byrne: sam’s driven very much by her mother and her mother’s words of, “you have to leave. ” Her sense of really pushing the daughters to leave to a bigger world, to a better place, to more opportunities, particularly as young women — I think that is her drive. She’s extremely bright; she’s very ambitious. This town is corrupt. It’s run by these people and you’ve got to get out. It’s rigged. The voice in her head is her mother’s voice, and she’s very much like her mother. I think the only way through life is to leave and to go somewhere where she can see like-minded people and be less oppressed and repressed in this town, which can be pretty challenging and pretty backward.

Diungkapkan bahwa fahy: i don’t think charlie wanted to leave her dad. I think that she wanted to follow in his footsteps in terms of doing the work that she had seen him do for their whole lives, and there’s something really interesting about that because Charlie and Sam obviously suffered in a big way as a result of what he did for a living and how that affected the family. There was something about Charlie that wanted to stay to rewrite the story or to take control of elements of the story that she didn’t feel that she had. And for her, the path to doing that was staying where it all happened.

Sebagaimana diketahui, fahy: karin did a really good job of weaving that in. A lot of Charlie’s behavior, especially as it applies to her husband, Ben — at the beginning of the show, they’re not really together, but you sort of want them to be. But you understand why he is taking a step back, because the fact that she hasn’t processed any of this trauma that he doesn’t even know about is keeping him from really being with her, and it’s keeping her from really letting him in. That undercurrent is there the whole time, so I didn’t feel like I had to do anything special or extra to lace that in, because Karin did such a good job of building it in the relationships. You see Charlie suffering in her relationships, and you find out why much later, but I think if you watched the show from the beginning and you knew that, you would really be able to see that throughline in her and her behavior throughout the series.

Berdasarkan laporan, byrne: i think it’s her disappointment in her sister after what she sacrificed for her. To your point, this secret is so corrosive to their relationship because Sam doesn’t know the truth. Her sister’s behavior is so triggering for Sam and so disappointing and so crushing when their mother had set this example of leaving and escaping, and I think her lack of compassion for her sister really is a great flaw in the character. Obviously, once she finds out the truth, she understands the whole perspective and also her anger. But that is another very specific trait in Sam that is really roadblocking her ability to have compassion and accept that her sister is not her.

Berdasarkan laporan, fahy: the girls were raised in a house that was very intellectually driven. The scenes where you see Gamma teaching them, the way that she spoke to them — I always think it’s so funny when they’re in the store, and she’s giving Sam a lesson on how to really land saying “Fuck!,” and using her breath and stuff like that. That part of how they were raised is something that they both actually really like.

Sebagaimana diketahui, byrne: sam’s law is patent law, so it’s so dry; it’s so unemotional, and it is so specific. Whereas Charlie’s character, she feels so tied to her father. I think she adores how benign it can be, and she thrives in the specificity of it, in the numbers of it. I think the trauma bond she has with her father and the secret they share — it’s very, very hard for her to leave that, and to leave what they’ve shared together in that sense.

Diungkapkan bahwa fahy: for all of her father’s faults, he protected her when she needed him to. He kept the secret that she asked him to. I think she respected him, and Sam doesn’t in the same way, but then ultimately comes to feel that way about him towards the end.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, byrne: it’s like that great ram dass saying: “if you think you’re enlightened, then go and spend a weekend with your parents. You can think all the things you want about yourself until you’re back in front of whoever consists of your family. There’s just no relationship on Earth like it, and it is so powerful. ” I feel like that speaks really truth to everybody who’s alive and has parents who are alive. I feel like this is a really great examination of that, particularly with Samantha.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fahy: sam and charlie both wanting to go into the field of law is rooted ultimately in their respect for what they saw their father achieve, regardless of how it ultimately negatively affected everyone in the family and caused their mother to be killed. I know that’s true for Charlie at least. And that’s so awful, but I do think that, ultimately, they really love feeling like they’re helping people. That’s the thing she loves the most about what she does: helping kids that she feels like don’t have anybody else who wants to in the same way that she does.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fahy: our director, steph green, had found a version of the song that she really, really liked, and she knew that i sang, and she asked if i would be open to covering it. She wanted it to come after Episode 5 because she feels like some of the words, especially in the first verse, could be Charlie singing to Sam. I, of course, was very excited by the idea. I think the way that the episode ends where Charlie’s in the doorway and she’s calling for her sister the way that she did in the first episode — it’s like this callback to her being a child and standing in that same spot right before the worst thing happened. I like that the version that we did is a little bit haunting, a little bit stripped down.

Sebagaimana diketahui, byrne: karin slaughter is so interesting, because she’s so ahead of the reader. She’s so ahead of her audience with her plots, but I do feel like Sam is that role too, and she’s a little bit ahead of the audience in her mind about what’s happening and she’s piecing it all together faster than everybody else. That was something I talked about a lot with Karin, so I tried to remember that in those scenes. I think she intuitively already knows all of this, and it’s catching up in real time as we’re watching it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fahy: what’s so interesting about the show is it’s so nuanced in terms of who did what, who is guilty of what, and who was wrong, because charlie did accuse the wrong person [daniel] of assaulting her — and that person was killed. But also, she was a kid, and she was confused, and she only had the information that was in front of her. So in the moment that she realizes that, she feels incredibly guilty for having essentially been responsible for someone losing their life. I think that really speaks to the way that we process trauma. Sometimes, it’s really hard to zoom out and look at things from a different point of view when all you can feel is the trauma that your body is still in fight or flight.

Berdasarkan laporan, she’s unraveling all of that, feeling the guilt of that, feeling the anger of having been intimate with huck, who is now a part of the worst day of her life. Ultimately, I think that Charlie finding out all of this is the thing that breaks her open, that ultimately allows her to come face to face with her truth. That is part of the catalyst to her being able to share that with Ben, which is what she needed to do so that they could really be together in a real way.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, byrne: they say in the birth order, the eldest daughter is such a huge responsibility in a family, especially for a young girl. So to see her sister go through this trauma again and relive it again in front of her is really harrowing and makes her so wildly furious that I feel like that is another very specific thing she’s going through.

Sebagaimana diketahui, fahy: judith was there the day that charlie was assaulted in the woods. For Charlie, feeling safe with anybody is a tall order. Charlie shows up to her door, and Judith takes her in. After that, Judith continues to take care of her in school. She sticks up for Charlie when she’s being bullied. So for her to come to the realization that a person that she really trusted and felt looked after by could have done something so horrible — I think she was a cocktail of emotions, but there was a real, real sadness and heartbreak in there when Charlie realized that Judith really was the one who orchestrated the killings.

Berdasarkan laporan, byrne: that’s so cool. I didn’t know that.

Diungkapkan bahwa fahy: because the novel is so beautifully written, it felt complete to me — and the show felt complete to me, too. I don’t think I ever really pictured it as being ongoing. But that being said, Charlie is one of my most cherished characters that I’ve ever been able to play, so she’ll stay with me for a long time. I would be very curious to know what she would be getting up to and what her life would be like after having gone through everything that she goes through.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, byrne: we felt it was pretty contained within the pages of what we were doing, but i’ve also been around so long that now i don’t know what anywhere will lead to anywhere anymore. So “anything can happen” is really my motto now in this business, because you just never know how things will shake out. I always try to keep an open mind, but it feels like the story we were meant to tell was the one we’ve told.

Diungkapkan bahwa byrne: maybe they go to a private island and have a mojito. They deserve a drink! They should talk about the weather for a few weeks, and keep it really light. Not the news — just the weather, what they’re going to have for dinner. I’m being silly, but I’m kind of not. That’s what I would like: for them to be a little bored, a little quiet, just relaxed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, fahy: i hope that charlie finds real comfort and peace. I think we don’t show a lot of relationships like Charlie and Ben where the person is given space to figure themselves out, and Ben’s not punishing her for it. Another thing that I really, really love about the character of Ben, played by Michael Dorman — we were so lucky to have him because his energy is so unique and loving and understanding. He’s loving her through it while also having his own boundary.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to see them come back together after having given each other that space, and for him to really hold all of charlie’s truth and say, “i’m still here,” is so hopeful and nice. We should show more of that because if you’re lucky enough to be in a really healthy relationship, that’s what you would hope would be true for anybody. It was just the work Charlie had to do, and he allowed her to do that. So I loved that the conflict was never really between the two of them. So I hope that after “The Good Daughter,” Charlie and Ben are super happy in Atlanta and that they’re just finally really enjoying each other.

This interview has been edited and condensed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, with the novel being compared most consistently to the reacher franchise, kill current has echoes of the lee child series in its larger story, and has also been compared to john le carré's work, as well. Diungkapkan bahwa as someone who's known to take his work seriously, knowing that reeves is behind the adaptation of kill current is an exciting step in the right direction. While it was only announced in September 2026, Kill Current's adaptation has already been pushed into development, which means there's a great chance it comes to fruition. Sebagaimana diketahui, for readers looking for a new thriller series to dive into on the ground floor, kill current should be a viable option, especially considering that there's already movement on a film adaptation. Sebagaimana diketahui, there are few things star trek fans love more than a good crossover. Bringing together characters from different eras of the franchise is practically guaranteed to generate excitement, particularly when those characters happen to be two of Starfleet's most legendary captains. But what happens when the movie designed to unite them doesn't quite live up to expectations?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, released in 1994 and now streaming free on pluto tv, star trek: generations brought captain james t. The result was a movie that divided fans, delivered one of the franchise's most controversial deaths, and destroyed one of television's most beloved starships. Kirk (William Shatner) and Captain Jean-Luc Picard (Patrick Stewart) together on the big screen for the first and only time. Yet more than three decades later, Generations deserves another look, particularly for what it has to say about growing older, accepting loss, and knowing when it's time to move on.

Berdasarkan laporan, the film opens with kirk, montgomery scott (james doohan), and pavel chekov (walter koenig) attending the maiden voyage of the enterprise-b. Kirk is retired, although it's obvious he hasn't entirely adjusted to life outside the captain's chair.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when kirk discovers that the ship's helmsman is demora sulu (jacqueline kim), daughter of his former crewmate hikaru sulu (george takei), he's surprised his old friend found time to start a family. Scotty reminds him of something Kirk himself has always said: If something is important, you make the time.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it's a seemingly insignificant exchange that establishes one of the movie's central themes. Kirk has spent his life exploring the galaxy, but what has he missed along the way? He's saved countless lives and made history, yet he's struggling to find purpose without the Enterprise.

Berdasarkan laporan, decades later, picard faces his own reckoning with mortality after learning that his brother robert and nephew rené have died in a fire. The tragedy leaves him confronting the possibility that his family line will end with him, along with the realization that the life he chose came at the expense of another he might have had.

Sebagaimana diketahui, both captains eventually find themselves inside the nexus, a mysterious energy ribbon that offers its inhabitants a seemingly perfect existence. For Picard, that means experiencing the family life he never had. Kirk finds himself back in a peaceful home, with the opportunity to reconnect with a woman from his past. Perhaps Edith Keeler?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the temptation is understandable. Who wouldn't want the chance to revisit a happier moment or correct a regret? But Generations makes the case that a meaningful life isn't necessarily a perfect one. Sometimes it's the choices we make, and the sacrifices that come with them, that give our lives purpose.

Diungkapkan bahwa none of this means generations is without problems. Tolian Soran (Malcolm McDowell), wants to return to the Nexus so badly he's willing to destroy entire star systems to make it happen. The movie's villain, Dr. Far from it. While McDowell brings considerable menace to the role, Soran never quite becomes the memorable antagonist the story needs.

Diungkapkan bahwa then there's kirk's death, which remains one of the most debated moments in star trek history. After surviving Klingons, Romulans, Khan, and countless other threats, the legendary captain meets his end beneath a collapsing bridge. For a character who spent decades boldly going where no one had gone before, it's not exactly the grand farewell many fans imagined. And yet there's plenty here to appreciate.

Sebagaimana diketahui, stewart delivers some of his finest work as picard struggles with grief, particularly during a quiet conversation with counselor deanna troi (marina sirtis). The destruction of the Enterprise-D is also genuinely shocking, especially for viewers who spent seven seasons watching the ship become almost as much a character as the people aboard it.

There's also the introduction of Data's (Brent Spiner) emotion chip, which provides some welcome humor, even if the movie occasionally leans a little too heavily into the android's newfound feelings.

Diungkapkan bahwa most importantly, shatner and stewart make the film's long-awaited meeting worthwhile. Instead, they feature two captains reflecting on what it means to make a difference. Their scenes together aren't built around elaborate action sequences or clever one-liners. It's a quieter approach than some viewers might have expected, but one that feels appropriate for these characters.

Berdasarkan laporan, beyond its story, generations occupies a unique place in star trek history. It was the franchise's first theatrical film built around the cast of Star Trek: The Next Generation, arriving just months after the television series concluded its seven-season run.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for years, kirk and his crew had been the faces of star trek on the big screen. Kirk begins the film as a celebrated former captain watching a new Enterprise depart without him. Now it was Picard's turn. The movie makes that transition literal. By the conclusion, he's helping Picard save millions of lives and making one final sacrifice before leaving the future in another captain's hands.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the destruction of the enterprise-d reinforces that transition. The ship that carried Picard and his crew through seven seasons of television adventures is gone, clearing the way for a new chapter. The Next Generation cast would return in three more films, beginning with 1996's Star Trek: First Contact.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there's something fitting about a movie so concerned with the passage of time serving as the bridge between two eras of star trek. The franchise was changing, just as its characters were learning to accept change in their own lives.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, generations may not be the best star trek movie, but beneath the spectacle, questionable decisions, and collapsing bridges is a thoughtful story about two men who devoted their lives to making a difference. When Kirk gets one last opportunity to do exactly that, he doesn't hesitate. For all the movie's imperfections, it's hard to imagine a more appropriate final choice for the captain of the Enterprise.

#696. The 8 Greatest Vampire Books Released Since 'Dracula', Ranked
