#767. 10 Movies To Watch if You Loved ‘You Can See Everything’

📅 14 Nov 2026

10 Movies To Watch if You Loved ‘You Can See Everything’

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/movies-like-you-can-see-everything/

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s cool to see how much you can see everything has been resonating and achieving popularity-wise, since it doesn’t really scream “hit movie. ” It’s a nearly three-hour-long documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, at least at first. It does more beyond that, but in ways that shouldn’t be spoiled. Anyway, it’s long, patiently paced, and not a blockbuster by any means, but it’s been making a ton of money and proving very thought-provoking.

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s nathan fielder at his most nathan fielder, which helps (and he does have a following that meant you can see everything was always going to get some attention), and then lance oppenheim also brings a lot to the film, since he’s also become quite accomplished as a documentarian/filmmaker. You Can See Everything is a documentary of sorts, but a mind-bending one that defies genre in some regards, and similar things can be said about the following films. Some are documentaries, or part-documentaries, while others are films that feel heavily meta and effortlessly thought-provoking, with all being worthwhile watches for anyone who loved and/or can’t stop thinking about You Can See Everything.

Sebagaimana diketahui, you hear “orson welles,” and you probably think citizen kane, first and foremost, and honestly, fair enough. That is about as legendary as movies get, and so it’s the artistic peak of everything Welles did, but it’s far from the only worthwhile project he tackled, and you can venture outside of cinema to see the also-famous radio adaptation of The War of the Worlds, which has a certain legend around it as being convincing enough to make people think it was real, but that's more likely a myth/urban legend.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that sense of it possibly fooling people, though, and welles’s reputation for being something of a trickster… that feels relevant when looking at f for fake. It’s Orson Welles making some sort of weird arthouse documentary that isn't wholly a documentary, and maybe more of a feature-length magic trick, and then that’s fitting when it’s also about fakery and deception. Just how deep or layered it is doesn’t feel clear, and that enhances F for Fake, honestly, rather than making it feel frustrating.

Diungkapkan bahwa close-up feels odd and proves hard to describe, but largely in a good way. It comes down to it not really committing to being a documentary or a non-documentary, and then it’s all presented in a way that makes it feel hard to tell what might be what. It’s probably safe to say that it blends fact and fiction, and also, it features people playing themselves in a story about a man who was arrested for impersonating a filmmaker.

Diungkapkan bahwa if that sounds mind-bending, it’s because close-up is, since it feels a little like a documentary, except instead of actors re-enacting certain scenes, the subjects themselves do. And then it gets strange in some other regards, but all in service of exploring various interesting subjects surrounding the art of filmmaking and the idea of identity. It’s not a hugely well-known movie, but it is the kind where just about everyone who’s seen it seems willing to praise it, so that makes it a worthy watch for those after something (very, very) different.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there are layers here, just like there are layers in you can see everything and a bunch of the other movies here. Basically, Jim & Andy: The Great Beyond is a documentary about a movie that came out almost two decades earlier called Man on the Moon. And Man on the Moon was a movie starring Jim Carrey, where he played Andy Kaufman, and a good chunk of Man on the Moon was set decades earlier, since Kaufman was active as a very unusual comedian/entertainer in the 1970s and some of the 1980s (before his death in 1984).

Diungkapkan bahwa jim carrey famously disappeared into the role, going full method actor for it, and then kaufman himself was also someone who always seemed like he was playing a character, but it was hard to work out where the character ended and kaufman began (also, whether he was actually playing multiple characters). So, a documentary about a movie starring an unusual actor (Carrey) that was about an unusual entertainer (Kaufman) is going to be a little different from your average documentary. Go figure.

Berdasarkan laporan, like with a fair few movies here, it’s hard to say what exactly my winnipeg is. There’s a real blurring of the lines between documentary and feature film here, and regarding the “feature film” side of things, who even knows what genre it belongs to. Parts of the movie are kind of funny, some are sad, and then other parts even get a little haunting, feeling ghostly and fantastical by documentary standards.

So, maybe it’s a fantasy/documentary hybrid, if that’s even possible? Speaking of things maybe not being possible, is there anything that’s really “documentary” here? Again, what is My Winnipeg? There’s nothing else like this, for better or worse, and it’s just about guaranteed to feel unfamiliar no matter how many other movies and/or documentaries you’ve watched throughout your life.

Diungkapkan bahwa pretty much anything directed by lars von trier counts as an arthouse film, so it shouldn’t be too surprising that a documentary co-directed by him gets kind of odd, though this does stand in contrast to most of lars von trier’s other movies in the sense that it’s not super depressing. Truth be told, The Five Obstructions is quite funny and decently light-hearted for much of its runtime. It was also directed by Jørgen Leth, and the premise is pretty much Lars von Trier giving Leth a series of increasingly strange and difficult rules he has to stick to while continually remaking a short film he made decades earlier.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there are five challenges all up, and those obstructions do indeed get more obstructive. Von Trier often tortures his audience, so to speak, or puts you, as a viewer, through the wringer, but here, it’s more about seeing him do it to a fellow filmmaker. And because it’s about making short films, and because you get to see the short films, The Five Obstructions does ultimately blur the line between documentary and feature film, all the while being an interesting look at a certain kind of unusual creative process.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, more of a folk horror movie than a documentary, probably, häxan is cool, whatever it is, especially when you consider its age. The fact it’s more than a century old makes it feel eerier, and the way it doesn’t purport to be wholly a documentary means that you can kind of roll with some of the more outlandish claims it makes in the service of “informing” you about the history of witchcraft and some other supernatural-related topics.

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s all very fascinating, above all else, and there is a timeless kind of unease to some of the visuals on offer here as well. Häxan is intense for a silent film, and a good one to show people who might be skeptical that films of this age can still get some sort of emotional reaction out of people. It’s definitely easier to recommend as a work of horror than a documentary, though the fact it’s even part-documentary is interesting, and also a big reason why it’s ultimately worth highlighting for present purposes.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s hard to know where to start when it comes to summarizing synecdoche, new york, if a summary is even possible with a movie this ambitious. You can talk about the extent to which it lingers in the mind long after it’s over, being a difficult movie to shake. And then also obvious is the quality of the acting here, with it containing what’s easily one of the best lead performances Philip Seymour Hoffman ever gave, and that’s saying a lot.

Diungkapkan bahwa in terms of the filmmaking, it’s charlie kaufman doing his thing to a particularly overwhelming extent, writing and directing this one while not holding back from making things layered, existentially troubling, and overall despair-filled. It’s a movie about art and existence and struggling to find a meaning in life, and then a whole bunch of other things. You might well only ever scratch the surface of this one, but even so, that’s okay, since there is oh so very much surface to scratch.

Diungkapkan bahwa nathan for you ran for a consistently hilarious four seasons, and is understandably considered one of the funniest shows in relatively recent memory, even if nathan fielder has pushed himself further artistically and creatively since it wrapped up. The final episode of the show is also kind of a movie, and so it’s going here, with it also being relevant since it suggested where Fielder was going to go post-Nathan for You.

Diungkapkan bahwa namely, he went into slightly more serious territory in the rehearsal and you can see everything, and you get a little more heaviness and tension with nathan for you: finding frances than in the other episodes of the show. It’s about Fielder assisting an unusual old man named William Heath to track down an old love. It’s funny, uncomfortable, sad, and thought-provoking in equal measure, so it made for a great feature-length finale for the whole of Nathan for You, to say the least.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if the title looks intimidating, split it like "symbio-psycho-taxi-plasm," and then you might be able to say it, should you ever find yourself in a conversation where symbiopsychotaxiplasm comes up. Fittingly for a movie with such a title, it’s hard to describe what Symbiopsychotaxiplasm: Take One is even about. It does feel in line with some of the stuff Nathan Fielder would go on to do, but with more density, possibly more layers, and also less humor, too.

If you want some kind of description, it’s about making a movie, and then it’s also about the making of the making-of, and maybe some other things.

Berdasarkan laporan, so, it came earlier, and might've influenced some of fielder’s work, but it’s a good deal more challenging. If you want some kind of description, it’s about making a movie, and then it’s also about the making of the making-of, and maybe some other things, with people acting and being watched, and those watchers being watched, and maybe those watchers being watched, too. It’s wild. And it’s hard to recommend, but it is at least very interesting… whatever it is.

Berdasarkan laporan, real life is an easy movie to enjoy, so if you’ve gotten through some of the more intense and intricate films here, then treat yourself with this, as a breather. It’s still layered and remarkably clever, though, not to mention ahead of its time it feels, even while being a parody of a show called An American Family. That show and Real Life pre-dated reality TV as it’s now understood, but reality TV has become unstoppable.

Sebagaimana diketahui, so, what this has to say about human nature, people being curious about others, and people wanting to be in control… yeah, all that can’t help but feel more relevant nowadays. It scratches a similar itch to The Truman Show, though the premises are fairly different, and the mockumentary style of Real Life makes it feel a little more worthy of being considered here than The Truman Show (consider that one honorably mentioned now, though, in any event).

Diungkapkan bahwa i actually think this was a cathartic episode for them and that they got to say things that have been lingering that, had they not said it, it wouldn’t have been real. #771. 12 Classic Wii Games That Nintendo Should Add to Switch Online

📅 14 Nov 2026

12 Classic Wii Games That Nintendo Should Add to Switch Online

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/switch-online-missing-wii-games/

Sebagaimana diketahui, with gamecube games now available to play on nintendo switch online with the expansion pack upgrade, it’s fun to think about other hardware that might benefit from similar treatment. The Wii springs most readily to mind, with a lineup of amazing games many players will remember from the system’s heyday.

Diungkapkan bahwa there’s no shortage of gems in the wii library, and they didn’t all come from nintendo itself. Thinking back on some of the games that people missed at the time, it’s easy to argue that Nintendo should add Wii to Switch Online sometime soon, if only so we have another chance to play classic games like the 12 on this list.

Diungkapkan bahwa you’ve heard of excitebike, but have you heard of excite truck? it was the start of a short-lived offshoot series of arcade-style racers from monster games (nascar heat 4), which was a frequent nintendo collaborator around that time. Players controlled pickup trucks as they raced around beautiful environments around the world and beyond, using nitrous to launch from small hills and catch air. It would be nice to see it return in remastered form, possibly even with a new sequel. The island’s topography changed around them, keeping the action fast and furious for both players. Then the franchise disappeared. A sequel, Excitebots: Trick Racing followed in 2009, and leaned more heavily into airborne stunts. But if that can’t happen, an appearance on Switch Online would be just lovely.

Diungkapkan bahwa known as anno: create a new world outside north america, dawn of discovery for wii was an accessible city builder published by ubisoft. There was also a DS version, which is similar, but the Wii version handled the necessary scale more effortlessly. The lesser known Wii version, ported by Keen Games, simplified numerous elements (including the interface and visuals) for a console audience. Despite the more manageable approach, the gameplay loop remained compelling enough that, as with previous titles like SimCity, a person didn’t want to quit playing once they started. On the PC platform outside North America, it was released as Anno 1404, which is still regarded as a classic in the genre. Ubisoft didn’t follow it up with any sequels, which suggests it didn’t sell well enough to justify the effort, but it would still make a welcome addition to the Switch Online library.

Diungkapkan bahwa cing, a developer known for its adventure titles, had one of its most acclaimed games with little king’s story. Along the way, he battles monsters and completes tasks for the populace, which allows him to gain additional resources while his kingdom grows. Co-developed with Town Factory, the real-time strategy game lets players assume the role of a cartoon king who explores his kingdom in a quest to gain wealth and territory. A port is available on Steam, once again from publisher Xseed Games, but the title remains underrepresented on consoles. It would make a compelling addition to Switch Online libraries.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the dog island is an astonishingly cute game from developer yuke’s, which has mostly built a reputation as a developer of fine wrestling and fighting games. It features big-eyed puppies of various breeds. You choose your breed of pooch at the start and follow their adventures through cozy environments populated by minor threats, which they scare away with their pipsqueak barks. The art style is very soothing, and the challenges are the sort that might appeal to players of all ages (though younger players are the ones most likely to respond favorably). The adventure itself is also surprisingly robust, with mild peril and excitement to keep everyone engaged. The canine-focused title was the third in the series, but the first published outside Japan. Anyone looking for a game about pets that isn’t a basic sim would do well to look up this overlooked gem, which deserves a new leash on life.

Berdasarkan laporan, the fortune street franchise, known as itadaki street in japan, has been around since the famicom days. But the lively presentation, featuring so many familiar characters, made it something special. The game resembles the classic Monopoly board game in some respects, since landing on a rival player’s space can really ruin your day. I remember seeing a stack of the game available for years on a local store shelf, suggesting its sales fell short of what Nintendo hoped. Unfortunately, it must have been difficult to market and western consumers didn’t respond with widespread enthusiasm. It combined Nintendo and Dragon Quest characters, placing them on boards where they competed to amass a fortune. But that’s no reason the game shouldn’t return for a second round. Fortune Street on Wii was the first chance many North American players got to experience the series in English. A newer audience might be more receptive, especially if the game is one more entry in a software library they’re already paying for.

Berdasarkan laporan, before the fan campaign known as operation rainfall made so much noise on behalf of players, it looked like three exciting jrpgs might never reach north america. Even its biggest supporters found minor flaws that prevented it from living up to its full potential. One of the titles at risk was The Last Story, which was developed by Mistwalker (Lost Odyssey and Blue Dragon). An action-RPG, it finally arrived courtesy of Xseed Games, after Nintendo passed on the opportunity. The critical response was positive overall but far from unanimous. However, innovative combat, stirring music, and a deep story kept players coming back for more. The title is still remembered fondly by many who experienced it at the time, and a new generation would likely find plenty to enjoy in one of the great works of director and co-writer Hironobu Sakaguchi, best known as the creator of the Final Fantasy series.

Berdasarkan laporan, developed by vanillaware (unicorn overlord), muramasa: the demon blade was exclusive to the wii at launch, although a remastered version arrived on the vita a few years later as muramasa rebirth. Some players find it a bit shallow and repetitive after a while, but there’s no denying its artistry. The game is an action RPG set in a beautifully rendered fantasy world, with simple controls but challenging combat. Muramasa: Revenant Blades will retell the familiar story in February 2027. Perhaps someone will see the wisdom in making the original version more available for an eager audience of Nintendo fans, who might not be ready to buy the deluxe new one.

Diungkapkan bahwa aside from letting little mac exchange blows with other mascots in games like 2018’s super smash bros. The action was fast, furious, and beautiful, a satisfying trip down memory lane for those of us who grew up playing Mike Tyson’s Punch-Out!! on the NES. Ultimate, Nintendo hasn’t paid much attention to its scrappy little hero. As usual, it pitted him against an assortment of cartoon opponents, including Glass Joe, King Hippo, and Super Macho Man, among others. The last time he got a proper game of his own was Punch-Out!! in 2009. Another run at the circuit would be most welcome.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i’ve lost track of how many hours i spent playing dokapon kingdom with my friends. The appeal comes from the interaction, which unfolds in a lighthearted fantasy world that feels like it was ripped directly from Dragon Quest. The loser might wind up with a new hairstyle, or worse. We have never completed a longer run together, but conquered many shorter ones over the course of multiple game nights. Sometimes, they run into each other and have a duel. Players move around a sprawling board, battling monsters to build levels and capture cities from monsters. It’s zany multiplayer fun with a healthy dose of humor that publisher Atlus warned might ruin a few friendships. Dokapon Kingdom: Connect brought a remastered version of the experience back on PC and Switch in 2023, but Switch Online is where it really might thrive.

Sebagaimana diketahui, released very early in the wii’s life cycle, elebits (known as eledees in australia and europe) was one of the most interesting games of its generation. The more energy they absorb on their hunt, the more options they have for manipulating the environment and reaching the end of a stage. The first-person perspective resembled a shooter, but the game wasn’t particularly violent. It had players search a house and other intimate environments for miniature creatures known as elebits, which resemble the mischievous critters in Pikmin. Players could get so absorbed by the process that they might forget to blink, until suddenly their eyes were watering and stinging (ask me how I know). Most of the fun came from rearranging furniture to find the pesky little critters. The game was quietly awesome, and it might easily find a second life on Switch Online.

Candace Cameron Bure is preparing to spread even more holiday cheer thanks to Great American Media’s expansion of the Sweet Christmas franchise.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the sweet christmas franchise is going to continue, and sam and sophie are turning marlow maple meadows into an inn,” cameron bure, 50, exclusively tells us. “It’s actually going to turn into a weekly series during Christmastime. ”.

The actress — who has played Sophie Marlow in three Sweet Christmas movies, including 2026’s A Sweet Christmas Anniversary — teases that the TV show won’t just focus on her character’s love story with Cameron Mathison’s Sam Stackhouse.

“Lots of people will come in and out of the inn and will focus on their love stories,” Cameron Bure says.

Cameron Bure announced during the Friday, November 13, episode of The View that the Sweet Christmas franchise will return in 2027 “during the holidays” as a weekly show, as different people “come and stay at the inn” as a way to explore their relationships.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the extraordinary connection viewers have with candace cameron bure, cameron mathison and the sweet christmas movies makes it an easy decision to create additional stories in the form of a series,” great american media president and ceo bill abbott said in a statement shared with us. “We’re reinventing the Christmas movie genre with richer storytelling, memorable characters and original series that allow audiences to spend more time with the people and stories they love. ”.

Cameron Bure and her production company, CandyRock Entertainment, will produce the upcoming TV series.

While fans have to wait until next year to see how Cameron Bure and Mathison, 57, bring their iconic characters to television, their third rom-com together, A Sweet Christmas Anniversary, premieres later this month.

“We go to Budapest on our anniversary, but there’s a little mystery in this Christmas movie,” Cameron Bure tells Us of the latest holiday film, which will make its world premiere on Great American Pure Flix Tuesday, November 24.

Cameron Bure reveals that there is an original song by “a good friend” of hers, Matthew West, that plays a central role in the movie.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “he has honestly, hands down, my favorite christmas albums of all time,” the full house alum says. And it’s part of the mystery within the movie. “I just love his Christmas music, so we incorporated his song into this movie. ”.

“It’s just another sweet song, and it does inspire romance and the couple who has a special attachment to this song,” she concludes.

A Sweet Christmas Anniversary focuses on Sam and Sophie as they travel to Budapest to celebrate their first wedding anniversary and toast to his directorial debut.

Berdasarkan laporan, “what begins as a romantic first-year getaway quickly transforms into a lavish royal mystery when a charismatic hotelier draws the couple into a world of festive surprises,” the logline reads. “As Sophie uncovers a hidden connection to a beloved Christmas song, she and Sam must navigate the host’s surprising twists and turns to safeguard their love — and to rediscover the true spirit of Christmas. ”.

While Cameron Bure tells Us that it’s not easy to “have to reinvent the story every year of what’s going to make a good Christmas movie,” she has no plans to stop churning out holiday films.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i love making these christmas movies, and they’re running all the time on great american pure flix. You don’t have to wait till Christmastime to watch them,” she shares. “You can watch them all year long, but hopefully I’ll never stop making them. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the first despicable me movie premiered back in 2010, and ever since then gru and (perhaps more importantly) the minions have become mainstays of popular culture. Still, when Minions & Monsters arrived on streaming with a Peacock subscription, I tuned in at the behest of my fiancé. I have to admit that I haven't really been a fan of the Illumination franchise, although I do love what the studio did with the Super Mario Bros. movies. And I was shocked by how much I truly enjoyed this latest installment of the animated franchise.

Sebagaimana diketahui, minions & monsters reviews were rather positive upon the movie's release, and it's currently sitting at an impressive 89% on rotten tomatoes. I had to judge for myself, and I'll admit that those little yellow guys and their lines in Minionese did crack me up. Although I was even more impressed by how the animated family film was connected to the greater moviemaking industry.

Diungkapkan bahwa rather than showing the minions serving gru, the new movie provide provided them with an origin story. The audience learns that a tribe of the yellow creatures dated back thousands of years ago. We watch as they accidentally kill various evil bosses they have through the years, until eventually the stumble on a bank robbery.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after trying to pledge their loyalty to the robber, both the minions (and myself) are shocked to learn that they were actually on a film set and the bank heist was nothing but a scene. The studio ends up hiring the Minions (particularly James) when two execs find them amusing, starting an entire career in both silent and talkie films. This is when I really fell in love with Minions & Monsters, which ended up being a love letter to Hollywood.

Berdasarkan laporan, some movie lovers wish they had minions & monsters as a kid, thanks to how surprisingly rich it was regarding movie history. The Extra Terrestrial. First we're shown a movie museum, where there are nods to The Matrix and E. George Lucas himself even gets a cameo, although I was waiting for some Star Wars jokes that never happened. T. Indeed, the movie's brisk 90-minute runtime had plenty of great references to classic films. Throughout the story we also get references to silent films like like 1878's The Horse in Motion (which was also included in Jordan Peele's Nope), as well as 1896's Train Pulling Into a Station.

Diungkapkan bahwa when the minions are working for a wizard he clearly resembles a similar character from disney's fantasia. There are even nods to modern movies like Damien Chazelle's 2022 flick Babylon. And once we go from silent films to talkies, one can't help but think about Singin' in the Rain. There's also a shot for shot remake of a scene from Citizen Kane, as well as a hilarious "play it again" reference from Casablanca. That's just a handful of the movie references packed into Minions & Monsters.

Berdasarkan laporan, minions & monsters is streaming now on peacock as part of the 2026 movie release list. It's more than possible that the next movie in the Despicable Me franchise won't thrill me like this title did, but I'm definitely more invested in the property than ever before.

#775. 12 Most Universally Loved Sitcom Episodes Of All Time

📅 14 Nov 2026

12 Most Universally Loved Sitcom Episodes Of All Time

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/most-beloved-sitcom-tv-episodes-everyone-loves/

Berdasarkan laporan, from seinfeld’s “the contest” to the it crowd’s “the work outing,” there’s nothing like a really great sitcom episode. A tight half-hour full of absurd situations, hilarious one-liners, and well-observed character comedy truly never gets old. Even when it tackles timely subject matter, like Fawlty Towers’ season 1 finale “The Germans,” the underlying satire is timeless.

Berdasarkan laporan, every great sitcom has a few standout episodes, like when sammy davis jr. stopped by the Bunkers’ living room in All in the Family, or when Ross found out about Monica and Chandler’s relationship in Friends. So, without further ado or the distraction of a laugh track, here are the most universally adored sitcom episodes ever made.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, very few sitcoms have captured the zeitgeist quite as aggressively as friends, so there are a handful of episodes from its 10-season run that could claim a spot on this list. Everyone remembers Ross’ fateful slipup at the altar, and Joey wearing all of Chandler’s clothes, and of course, the finale.

Berdasarkan laporan, but “the one where everybody finds out” has huge dramatic payoffs without sacrificing the laughs. As the other friends learn about Monica and Chandler’s torrid affair, they all agree to keep it a secret from Ross. But in the episode’s final moments, as Ross enjoys a rare victory, he sees his sister and his best friend hooking up across the street. “Get off my sister!” is one of the best one-liner deliveries in all of Friends.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s always sunny in philadelphia took a couple of seasons to find its feet, but it really hit its stride in the season 4 finale, “the nightman cometh. ” Charlie puts on a musical with an ulterior motive, and everyone in the Gang tries to make it about themselves.

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s a classic sunny premise, with plenty of opportunities for the gang to be selfish, vapid, attention-hungry, and otherwise despicable. And on top of all that, the musical numbers are genuinely catchy.

Diungkapkan bahwa sammy davis jr. ’s turn in All in the Family is one of the most iconic celebrity guest spots in sitcom history. Sammy leaves his briefcase in Archie’s cab, and stops by the Bunker house to pick it up.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the episode addressed america’s racial tensions head-on, with a wry smile. The final kiss between Archie and Sammy was a hilarious subversion of the groundbreaking interracial kiss on Star Trek a few years earlier.

Diungkapkan bahwa the whole point of a sitcom — a situation comedy — is to derive comedy out of situations. Very few sitcom episodes have come up with a comedic situation as juicy as “Chuckles Bites the Dust. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the oft-mentioned but seldom-seen tv clown’s death paved the way for an ingenious satirical exercise in comic juxtaposition and ironic hypocrisy. Mary spends the whole episode scolding her co-workers for turning Chuckles’ death into a joke, all building to the perfect punchline: Mary ruining the funeral with uncontrollable laughter.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the it crowd’s season 2 premiere is one of the greatest farces ever created. It’s word-perfect on the page, and every twist and turn is pulled off spectacularly by the cast.

Berdasarkan laporan, jen seeing roy in a wheelchair, then turning to see moss working as a uniformed bartender, is one of the funniest visual payoffs in sitcom history. And really, sitcoms are all about those visual payoffs: Lucy and Ethel on the factory line, George Costanza pulling out the golf ball, Laura Petrie on a bed of walnuts.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there isn’t a single weak link in fawlty towers’ 12-episode run, but the season 1 finale stands out as the most iconic installment. “The Germans” sees Basil hosting some guests from Germany, and struggling not to mention World War II.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we’ve long since moved past that post-wwii sensitivity, but the satire of the episode still holds up because it’s analogous to more recent sensitivities. In the early 21st century, if Basil was hosting Muslim guests, he’d worry about mentioning 9/11. Today, if Basil was hosting Russian guests, he’d worry about mentioning Ukraine.

Berdasarkan laporan, whenever frasier crane set his mind to a creative project, like opening a restaurant with niles or composing a grand, orchestral theme tune for his show, it was a recipe for comedy gold. Frasier’s ambitions get the better of him, and his diva direction turns all his friends and family against him.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in season 4’s “ham radio,” frasier decides to mount a lavish radio drama. But he pushes his cast so far during rehearsals that they decide to sabotage the show live on the air. The cast are all giving performances within performances, and it’s incredible.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the candy factory sequence alone earns this episode a spot on the list. In I Love Lucy’s season 2 premiere, Lucy and Ethel decide to go toe-to-toe with their husbands in the workplace, and get a couple of jobs working the factory line.

Diungkapkan bahwa it was way ahead of its time in tackling the taboo surrounding women joining the workforce in the 1950s. But it also led to one of the greatest slapstick scenes ever captured on film.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when the office got out of the office, it delivered its all-time greatest episode. “Dinner Party” is a masterpiece of cringe comedy; Michael and Jan finally get their couple friends over for dinner, and proceed to put every last toxic trait of their relationship on blast for all their guests.

Berdasarkan laporan, some office episodes pushed the cringe humor so far that people have to skip it on rewatches — i love “scott’s tots,” but it may have overegged the cringe omelet — but “dinner party” strikes the right balance. You wouldn’t want to be a guest at this dinner party from hell, but you can enjoy watching it from the safety of the other side of the screen.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the golden age of the simpsons gave us dozens of iconic episodes, with dozens of iconic premises. Those premises range from grounded, relatable scenarios, like Homer going on strike and Lisa being inspired by a substitute teacher, to absurd, far-fetched comic situations, like the Simpsons moving across the country so Homer can take a job working for a Bond villain.

Diungkapkan bahwa but “marge vs. the Monorail” remains the pinnacle of The Simpsons. It combines the relatable scenario of Homer starting a new job with the comic absurdity of The Music Man meets The Towering Inferno.

#777. 'Alien' Meets 'Interstellar' in Netflix's 20-Episode Sci-Fi Series Made for Your Next Binge

📅 14 Nov 2026

'Alien' Meets 'Interstellar' in Netflix's 20-Episode Sci-Fi Series Made for Your Next Binge

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/alien-interstellar-replacement-another-life-netflix/

Diungkapkan bahwa netflix has created many iconic original shows in the past. House of Cards, Daredevil, Narcos, all shows with complex storytelling, compelling writing, and long-lasting support from audiences. Some slip through the cracks or fail to find the right audiences. But some Netflix originals aren't so lucky. These shows have built up a legacy of high quality television that resonated with audiences even after the last episode. Another Life is one of those shows that could have been great, but might just need to be revisited with fresh eyes.

Diungkapkan bahwa upon its release, another life was met with mixed reviews. While imperfect, the show tackles similar themes from sci-fi goliaths like Alien and Interstellar. With two seasons, the show concluded its story, falling back into the mass of Netflix's catalog. But the sci-fi show deserves another chance from viewers. Critics disliked the series while audiences were conflicted. Audiences might be surprised how similar Another Life is with other iconic science fiction stories if they give the series one more go.

Diungkapkan bahwa when an alien artifact lands on earth, niko breckinridge (katee sachhoff) is tasked with leading a space crew to find the alien's home and bring back answers. Leaving her husband Eric (Justin Chatwin) and her daughter Jana behind, Niko and her crew experience the many challenges space offers. On Earth, her husband Eric tests the artifact to discover its purpose on the planet, risking his and Jana's life in the process. From contaminated food, mutinous crew mates, and strange planets, every day brings a new obstacle for Niko to overcome. When the alien threat proves to be more dangerous than they could have expected, Niko finds that the return back to Earth is just as challenging as leaving it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, another life feels like a creative mix of alien and interstellar in a way that fully utilizes the sci-fi genre. Like Alien, the threat of an unknown extraterrestrial creature looms on the horizon, presenting a physical challenge for the crew to face. The show doesn't shy away from major character deaths, just as Alien embraced it. Niko and her crew find themselves in horrific fights for their lives as they explore the depths of space. On another note, Another Life balances the emotional stakes of choosing to leave family for the greater good. Niko's decision to leave Eric and Jana demonstrates the severity of the situation and her willingness to put humanity before her own desires.

Diungkapkan bahwa another life is far from perfect, but at its core, it tells a story about sacrifice. Like Interstellar, humanity's fate is in the hands of one crew who leave behind loved ones. Their fate is uncertain, and the risk is high, but they are willing to sacrifice their futures for Earth's. Many characters meet terrible ends along the journey, not only shocking audiences but proving how dangerous the mission is. Survival is not guaranteed, and each character finds themselves in life-threatening situations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, like alien's ripley or interstellar's cooper, niko carries the weight of the story. Her role as leader is one she takes seriously, and her mission drives her to keep going. Niko knows firsthand what sacrifice means, not just for her family and current crew, but with her complicated past. When her crew gets antsy or discontent, Niko remains level-headed. Katee Sackhoff's Niko is a complicated character, but one that puts duty above everything. With a wide array of personalities in the crew, viewers get the strongest understanding of Niko's resilience and dedication to the mission.

Sebagaimana diketahui, another life had all the makings of a great sci-fi show — alien threats against humanity, a ragtag space crew, new intense conflicts each episode. With fresh eyes, viewers might find some hidden treasure in the show that gives it its own charm. No story is ever perfect, and at the heart of the show, Another Life focuses on family, duty, and sacrifice that can speak to any audience member. While there are issues with the story, Another Life is judged too harshly for its weak spots. It's not perfect, but it takes risks to tell a compelling story that audiences should give another shot.

Alcon Entertainment confirmed it has had discussions about creating a AAA game based on Blade Runner.

Sebagaimana diketahui, alcon entertainment, which owns the blade runner franchise, confirmed in a recent interview that it has discussed making a aaa game based on the beloved sci-fi series. It's an exciting development for Blade Runner, which has never quite found its footing in gaming despite how influential its visual style and narrative themes have been.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we learned about the aaa game plans for blade runner in a recent ign interview about the upcoming prime video series blade runner 2099. Andrew Kosove, co-CEO of Alcon Entertainment and executive producer of the show, was asked whether Alcon has spoken with game studios about making a Cyberpunk 2077-like AAA game based on the Blade Runner IP. Kosove apparently said "yes" before adding that they'd want the game to be AAA and prioritize player interaction with the world.

Diungkapkan bahwa kosove didn't reveal much else, and no such project has been officially announced as of nov. 2026. As such, we can't help but wonder whether a known AAA game studio is already working on a Blade Runner game or if the project is still in the discussion and negotiation stages. It would be amazing to finally see a game like this, though, since Blade Runner hasn't had much luck with video games in the 2020s.

Diungkapkan bahwa the most notable blade runner game was a 1997 3d point-and-click adventure game from wildwood studios. While people liked that game, a 2022 Enhanced Edition remaster from Nightdive Studios had a rocky launch rife with graphical issues uncommon in the studio's usual remasters. In 2023, Annapurna Interactive announced Blade Runner 2033: Labyrinth, but most of its development team resigned and left the company in 2024. The game is believed to be canceled, as it is no longer listed on Steam or Annapurna's website.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it seems that alcon entertainment has moved on from that rough remaster and blade runner 2033 and now has aaa gaming ambitions for the franchise. All we can do is wait and see if those plans come to fruition, as any newly greenlit Blade Runner game would likely still be years out from release.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the short term, fans of the series can look forward to blade runner 2099, which will be released on prime video on nov. 25.

Virgin River has officially been renewed for season 9 but what does that mean for the show’s future after cast changes?.

During an exclusive interview with Us before news broke on Friday, November 13, about the show being renewed for season 9, Ben Hollingsworth hinted how long he could see Virgin River running on Netflix.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i would like to see it go for a long time. “I think it could go that long. I don’t want to compare it to a show like Grey’s Anatomy but it does have a feeling because Grey’s Anatomy is about that space and that place, where you do see doctors come and go,” Hollingsworth, 42, said. We could be here in 10 years still talking about Virgin River. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa hollingsworth, who plays brady, teased “so much story potential. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “there are so many books in the virgin river series. “And I think the fan base is still fairly hungry for more. We’ll see. There’s a lot of content to be drawn from it,” he noted. ”.

Based on Robyn Carr’s book series, Virgin River follows the lives of residents living in a small town in Northern California, including Mel (Alexandra Breckenridge) and Jack (Martin Henderson).

The hit series, which premiered in 2019, also stars Hollingsworth, Colin Lawrence, Annette O’Toole, Tim Matheson, Sarah Dugdale, Zibby Allen and Kai Bradbury.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after seven seasons, there have been some major departures from the netflix show. Grayson Gurnsey left as Ricky after season 4 in 2022, and Mark Ghanimé, who played Cameron, had a surprising exit once season 6 was released in December 2024.

Diungkapkan bahwa in march, virgin river returned for season 7, and it was later confirmed that marco grazzini will not reprise his role as mike. In another twist, Lauren Hammersley, who has played Charmaine since the show premiered, is also not expected to come back for season 8.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it’s always bittersweet,” hollingsworth told us. “We never know if and when someone might show back up on the show. One thing we’ve been really great at as a cast is welcoming in when new people do come along. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he added: “our show very much opens its arms to people. Just like on the show. Everyone’s super kind to everyone. It’s bittersweet to see someone go but also when someone new comes in, they do bring something new to the show and they bring a new texture to the show, which is also important. It’s a great set to be a part of. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hollingsworth’s insight came as fans remain concerned about his future on the show. The season 7 finale ended with Brady injured in a motorcycle accident and Hollingsworth has remained tight-lipped about whether Brady “will be a part of” Virgin River going forward.

Diungkapkan bahwa “honestly, i wasn’t expecting [the fan reaction] to be so loud. Does he make mistakes all the time? Is he trying to be a better version of himself? Yes and he does have a lot of unfortunate things happen to him. I really take that as a compliment that people are like, ‘This show can’t happen without Brady,'” he added. He’s always trying to do what he thinks is right and he may do the wrong thing but it’s usually for the right reason. And that type of character is really relatable. “I’m right there with them. People have some opinions about it, which is a nice compliment. We’re all trying to be a better version of ourselves and Brady’s been working on that since season 1. It’s special to see people really do gravitate towards Brady and I think some of that is just he is very human. ”.

Virgin River has been renewed for seasons 8 and 9 on Netflix.

Diungkapkan bahwa i know friends is one of the best sitcoms of all time because i’ve returned to it time and time again throughout my life. Like, I couldn’t count on both hands how many times I’ve seen many of the episodes, and I’ve definitely watched it all the way through a few times. It’s been a long time since I went back to the iconic series, but when I got my wisdom teeth out last week, I ended up throwing on the show for some brainless entertainment, and something new came up. Rachel really had me fuming!.

Diungkapkan bahwa now, i know there are rachel haters out there, but in the past i’ve thought of ross as the worst and monica as my second least favorite. I've got to talk about it. This time I found myself practically yelling at my TV screen over what Rachel does more than anyone, and remembering a bunch of other instances where she was super questionable. (But remember, I’m talking about TV characters here, so it’s really not that serious).

Berdasarkan laporan, the first instance that really got my blood boiling was in season 2, episode 4. Rachel gets super jealous about Ross being with her. When they don't end up together in Season 1, Ross meets a nice gal named Julie. At this point, we know that Ross had a long-time crush on Rachel – he even told her earlier as I had recalled. When she hears that Ross and Julie are about to have sex for the first time, she sabotages the whole thing by making Julie talk all night while everyone is hanging out together.

Berdasarkan laporan, sure, it hurts to see someone you like get into a relationship with someone else, but talk about an incredibly passive-aggressive way to deal with it. She’s not only being a horrible friend to Ross, but to all her other friends who she drags down with her. Ross has just gone through a divorce at this point and communicated his interest to her multiple times before he got with Julie, so it feels super unfair. But this is just one of many things Rachel does.

Berdasarkan laporan, a few episodes later, friends has a two-part super bowl episode where they cross paths with jean-claude van damme (yes, the actor as himself). When she protests, she decides to confront him for her (which Monica doesn’t want). Upon seeing the action star, Monica confesses her big crush on him, and Rachel suggests he go up to talk to him. Van Damme starts flirting with Rachel because she’s beautiful, of course. Before she knows it, she’s going on a date with the guy. Rather than shutting it down, she totally goes for it. The nerve of Rachel! I don’t have to tell most of y’all how many girl codes this breaks, but it’s a lot.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fast forward to the end of season 3, when ross is dating bonnie. To her surprise, she’s got a full head of hair. Phoebe sets them up, but only after asking Rachel if it’d be OK if she does. Rachel only says yes because she believes Bonnie to be bald, and knows Ross won’t like it. So, Rachel decides to convince Bonnie to shave her head because she liked it that way, and she listens. Yes, once again we see Rachel being passive-aggressive toward someone whom she apparently loves, and probably once thought of as the love of her life, AND is actually friends with. This behavior feels more like bullying than friendship to me.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the same episode, ross and rachel decide to get back together after her sabotage and manipulation tactics apparently work. Instead, she gives him an 18-page letter that she wrote to read through, and she wants him to read it at 5:30 a. m. We don’t know the exact contents of the letter, but apparently it asks Ross to take all the blame for their failed relationship. But after all that, she doesn’t want to talk things out with her ex before taking him back, for some reason. While I totally agree that Ross made some big mistakes, especially with the cheating, I find this to be a pretty ridiculous way to try to repair a relationship. But, hey, sometimes Friends episodes can be ridiculous.

Berdasarkan laporan, then there’s the season 7 premiere when monica gets engaged. Not too long after Chandler pops the question, Rachel comes on to Ross (who are no longer together, again), and they end up making out in the hallway. Soon all the friends are chatting about what this means for Ross and Rachel rather than focusing on Chandler and Monica’s big milestone.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i think it understandably bothers monica and brings up some past instances where she “stole her thunder. " While you can argue Rachel didn’t know she would cause Monica so much stress, I think Rachel’s actions toward Ross were driven by her own insecurities that came up when she saw her friend engaged. Just be happy for your bestie and don’t kiss your ex and her brother for one day, girl! It’s not that hard.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the last one i’ll bring up is something from the latter part of the show that still breaks my heart. I think it’s super obvious from Season 8 on that Joey has a crush on Rachel, and yet, I feel like she ignores his feelings and manufactures her own in order to feel better about herself. Remember when Rachel decided to date Joey in order to get back at Ross? This is when Ross gets with Charlie, and Rachel essentially decides to get back at him by going out with Joey. Ugh, I'll never unsee all of this.

Berdasarkan laporan, i have one more point to make here. The show just wouldn’t be entertaining if everyone reacted well to every situation. I think one of the reasons why I’m always returning to Friends with my HBO Max subscription is because all the friends feel human and flawed. But, wow I can't believe I did not realize before all the wild choices Rachel made on the show before!.

"It shouldn't be possible to feel nostalgic for a memory that isn't yours," Jen wrote. It turns out the familiar, emotive connection everyone is feeling with the remake isn't just nostalgia. In Zelda, "you know exactly where you are, even if you've technically never been there before. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, jen points out that this feeling of knowing the game even if it's new to you stems from the elemental, fairytale simplicity of the storytelling in zelda games. I'd add that Zelda games share a deep humanity, too, more so than most Nintendo games, which tend to be quite abstract. In Zelda, this isn't expressed through strong emotions and high drama so much as it is through humor, caricature, pathos, and telling details. And no Zelda game is more poignant, funny, or scary than Ocarina of Time — not even the complex clockwork soap opera of its sequel, Majora's Mask.

Diungkapkan bahwa one thing that brought me up short this week was the revelation — by no means new, but new to me, and many others — that ocarina of time contains a sly reference to louisa may alcott's classic novel little women. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but maybe it's not out of character for ocarina of time, a game with a time-travel plot that puts the worlds of children and adults in conversation with one another. Small wonder that it made Corey think about his grandmother, and his grandmother think about her child. Maybe the Nintendo developer or translator that slipped the Little Women reference in was instinctively reminded of another classic work of art about childhood. Because that's what Ocarina of Time is.

In a series that’s (almost) all classics, which of Link’s adventures is best?.

The studio was founded by Journey art director Matt Nava, and you can certainly see its influence on this similarly sandy, wordless, and meditative (if also more conventionally exciting) game about surfing around on a sword in a dying world.

Giant Squid's latest asks you to save the world, and chill with some turtles along the way.

Sebagaimana diketahui, once upon a time, shigeru miyamoto was mr. The torch was passed, and now Aonuma is clearly lining up a successor of his own: Hidemaro Fujibayashi, director of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, who has now ascended to a producer credit on Ocarina of Time. Zelda and Eiji Aonuma was his heir apparent. In anticipation of Fujibayashi's future as the king of Zelda games, travel back to the start of his journey with the series: this excellent Game Boy Color diptych, featuring some of the best puzzles in Zelda history.

You'll never believe how much bigger the Switch 2 game is than the Nintendo 64 original.

Senior Music Writer and Chief Music Critic.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, is it possible to plan for magic, serendipity, peak-level proficiency and finally sublimity by… really not planning at all? that is the question. On Brandi Carlile‘s current “Burn the Setlist!” tour, the answer is clear: Sometimes Shangri-La really is best reached with a lost roadmap.

Berdasarkan laporan, the shortish 19-date outing carlile is undertaking at the moment is the first all-requests tour in memory by any artist significant enough to have it show up on our radar. It might even be a historic first, as far as a proven headliner opting to play nothing but spontaneously generated live audience picks. But at the opposite end of the scale from bar bands and tip jars, doing solely requests sounds like as much of a nightmare to most performers as it does a dream to hardcore fans. Which is odd when you think about it, because doesn’t anyone who’s been to a lot of shows over the years have a favorite moment when a star got loose and succumbed to someone shouting out a favorite (though they usually don’t want to encourage that kind of behavior?). There are perfectly good reasons not to throw the song selections completely open to stans for roughly 2 hours and 40 minutes — as Carlile and her two bandmates, Phil and Tim Hanseroth, are doing now — when you have a recorded catalog of close to a hundred original songs, plus a repertoire of proven live cover choices.

Who among even the greats of music has anything close to 100% recall? When the recent and distant pasts are both being dredged up, a good corollary to “Never let ’em see you sweat” might be: Never let ’em see you forget.

Fortunately, Brandi Carlile and the Hanseroth twins are freaking elephants.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but making a point out of not planning is different from not being prepared. Tim Hanseroth posted an IG video of himself running through their studio albums and strumming along to stir the old juices. Carlile said in a video livestream for fans on the tour’s eve that she would have a monitor for lyrics if she needed it. And Carlile and the brothers are prepared for this, first of all, by having brain chemistry that is clearly a little bit different from mine or probably yours, with the power not just to generate constant creative sparks but to put those sparks in an easily accessible lockbox. You’re either genetically predisposed to that kind of recall or you’re not, and at least a little part of why Carlile and the Hanseroths have been ideal partners since the turn of the millennium is that shared gift. Not that they came into the “Burn the Setlist!” tour relying completely on muscle memory. But at the show I caught, I barely noticed Carlile looking down at it… which I can’t say for most big tours I attend where the show is locked in for months straight.

Berdasarkan laporan, all of this risks making the tour seem like a stunt, which it kind of is. But the bigger reason for why it’s such a rousing success — and a reason why fans may remember these shows almost as well as Carlile and company remember their songs — is how many deeply moving moments are stirred up up in the shows, in the quietest bits that come between the outbreaks of hysterical shouting and sign-waving. Leaving the setlists up to fans, chance or God results in obscure picks and ironic juxtapositions that sometimes aren’t anything more than fun or curious, but are sometimes unexpectedly touching in a way that one of Carlile’s perfectly laid-out arena shows probably couldn’t be. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the last stretch of the oakland concert lifted the show from delightful travelogue to a something heavier on some of the trio’s most emotionally incisive songs, although it was difficult to know whether they were making these selections intentionally or those requests were providentially just arriving right on time. Tim Hanseroth did say he’d been waiting all night to pick on the guy in the front rows holding a sign asking for “The Things I Regret,” and subsequently showed up on Instagram thanking the fan again. It raised one of those questions that can only arise at a rarities-filled show like this: Why was this not a bigger hit — even amongst the band itself? Berdasarkan laporan, but the most touching highlights were “most of all,” a song about seeing your family in yourself (there are few lines more evocative than “his heavy hands swing at the end of my arms”)… and “that year,” an alternately chilling and warm ballad about looking to make peace with a high school friend who committed suicide, from across the veil that separates the living and the dead. And the recent “No One Knows Us,” about how each friendship bond formed among young people is precious, irreplaceable and worth the upkeep in a more depressed middle age. And the penultimate number, “That Wasn’t Me,” a neo-gospel ballad so healing and cathartic, it would have become Carlile’s signature song in some other lifetime, instead of a deep cut.

Berdasarkan laporan, the actual climax? a rare cover of led zeppelin’s “going to california,” because carlile can hit the golden-god notes. And then California surrendered the combo to the next stop in Tucson. (Where they did not get the Led out, of course, and where the next stop involved only repeating four of the 22 numbers heard in Oakland. ).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as a cherry on top, anyone leaving the show each night finds that there was a bonus offered earlier, not to them, but to anyone suffering at home with fomo. Right before she takes the stage, when the local audience is already seated, Carlile does a livestream of a single song while she’s having her makeup applied, just for everyone who doesn’t have the privilege of the live show (though, of course, the concert crowd can catch up with it later). It’s a hell of a miniature grace note.

Diungkapkan bahwa saying this was the best show i’ve ever seen by carlile and company probably without saying, after saying all of that; at times, i got to thinking it was one of the best shows i’ve ever seen from anyone, out of untold thousands. Maybe that’s because I have a worse memory than Carlile and the Hanseroths, but more likely because this really is as good as it gets, if you have a taste for the rare intersection where hair-trigger meets tear-jerk. Concert hyperbole is a dangerous thing, but I found myself hard-pressed to recall comparable instances in which I’d seen rock ‘n’ roll performers so throughly committed to the moment, not just for a moment but for close to three hours of them. #801. Inside the First AI Music Awards, a Chaotic Evening Attempting to Normalize Tech-Assisted Tunes

📅 14 Nov 2026

Inside the First AI Music Awards, a Chaotic Evening Attempting to Normalize Tech-Assisted Tunes

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://variety.com/2026/music/features/inside-first-ai-music-awards-sonic-intelligence-academy-1236947847/

I knew things were a little off when the first thing I heard on my walk to the AI Music Awards was “the winner…” followed by the sweet voice of Kelly Clarkson.

Berdasarkan laporan, no, miss american idol did not abandon her feud with the brooklyn bird to capitalize on her newfound appreciation for ai. Alas, not so: It was Clarkson’s Christmas classic “Underneath the Tree,” playing from speakers at a local YWCA event across the street. But as I approached the Mayan Theater in Downtown Los Angeles on a sunny afternoon to check in for Friday’s inaugural “AI Music Awards,” powered by the “Sonic Intelligence Academy” or “SIQA,” I wondered if her voice was so strong as to echo through the nearly century-old theater-turned-nightclub’s walls. Related Stories Tubi Partners With TikTok to Create 10 Original Long-Form Series (EXCLUSIVE).

To qualify for the awards, artists needed to register their tracks to SIQA’s “Verified Registry,” which denotes whether the song was fully AI-generated, made with the assistance of AI or featured a cloned human voice to lead the tune (what the group calls a “human + AI hybrid”).

Diungkapkan bahwa registered artists then nominate their peers in the 25 categories up for consideration — everything from “ai song of the year” to “best ai pop song” to “best ai comedic song” — and then vote on the winners. One of those nominees was Xania Monet, the AI persona of Telisha “Nikki” Jones, who a day earlier won the AI Album of the Year category at SIQA’s inaugural summit and who would eventually go on to win both artist and song of the year, three out of four of the awards’ top categories. (The fourth, producer of the year, went to “DJ Shawn Q. ”).

Berdasarkan laporan, the sonic intelligence academy is the brainchild of software engineer timirah “tj” james and her sister mia james. Since its January launch, it has worked to establish an awards program to counter the mainstream music industry’s aversion to AI. The group believes there needs to be infrastructure that supports those using AI to create music, rather than dismissing its existence, and it hopes to be an AI counterpart to the longstanding Recording Academy that governs the Grammy Awards. It advocates for artists to publicly associate themselves with their AI-powered work, eager to highlight the humans who helped create the product.

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s a noble, if surprising, decision to embrace its role as counterculture when ai artists continue to pursue a billboard charting position. Some of its methods are a little overt, perhaps intentionally: After some in the industry spurned the idea of AI-generated music charting on Billboard’s industry-standard charts, the group used a week in January ahead of the Grammys to launch its own charts exclusively for AI music. The Mayan is a 12-minute walk from the Crypto. com Arena, the Grammys’ longtime home.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the moves are not subtle, but subtlety is not the organization’s goal. The group and awards’ existence alone reflects those in the AI music space trying to move past the thorny legal questions surrounding AI music, which have led to lawsuits by artists and record labels against generators like Suno and Udio over copyright infringement, and into a realm of relevance within the genres they’re trying to embody.

It is, in a word, new, and new things mean kinks to work out.

Berdasarkan laporan, the first kink i noticed was when, as i arrived 30 minutes before the red carpet was set to begin, the doors to the venue were locked. I had to pull on each door before someone opened one, which led me to the check-in stand (bypassing any form of security, which didn’t seem to exist). I entered the foyer and arrived at the makeshift red carpet, where about 12, mostly independent media ventures set up cameras to interview the various nominees, presenters, and VIPs who’d grace the roughly 7-foot-long red carpet in front of one of the two step-and-repeat backdrops. PT. A spokesperson told me 29 media outlets had signed up to cover the event, but that some couldn’t make it because of the sudden flight ground-stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration around 12:30 p. m. Whether human or AI, aviation afflictions come for us all.

Diungkapkan bahwa the guests gracing the red carpet were not screens rolled out displaying ai avatars, contrary to a reasonable assumption. Sequined dresses and colorful blazers strolled through, stopping to speak with outlets like Reuters to the fiery red mohawk-sporting, sequin-wearing host of “The Iconic Punk Oz” Oz Powers to, tucked against a wall and steps from the red carpet, an effective AI red carpet correspondent housed inside a tall, white faux-stone vessel. Instead, the human creators behind the digital faces strutted the carpet in their Sunday best, treating the night less as music’s biggest night and more as the biggest night for their music. The contraption was developed by the event’s top sponsor, Deepgram, an AI startup specializing in text-to-speech agents.

Berdasarkan laporan, the device, which knew the artists and pressed them about the event, struck in me a slight fear about whether people might opt for robot reporters instead of humans, though that fear subsided when i realized this device could not appear on the red carpet because it could not move. The creators seemed more eager to speak to the physical reporters anyway, with some of them emphasizing the human elements of their AI work. Fredro Starr, one half of the rap group Onyx, spent much of the carpet touting the human vocals that made up his AI-beat-laden record “It All Started in Brooklyn,” which he claimed was the first AI album on vinyl.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “you can’t replace [humans],” starr told me, using the carpet to debut his new moniker, “mad ai. So vocally, you can hear that, but the AI just took it to another level. ” “The feeling that you get was what we bring with the spirit of hip-hop. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, inside the theater, siqa tried to bring a party-like feel to the function. A bar at the back of the venue —at a charge — kept well drinks flowing, and the bar top was littered with copies of a sponsored version of the newspaper “Rolling Out” featuring interviews with many of the nominees and James, the SIQA founder. One of those featured, Xania Monet founder Jones, sparked a wave of controversy last year when some of her Monet songs hit some of Billboard’s genre charts, leading to an interview with CBS’s Gayle King and to Kehlani slamming a $3 million record deal Jones received. As she waited for a drink by the bar ahead of the event’s start, Jones told me she wasn’t worried about the AI of it all overshadowing the pursuit of legitimacy within the greater music industry.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “ai is just a tool,” she said. “It just emphasizes what we do. I just feel like we should all be one. ”.

But despite that lofty goal, the kinks kept rearing their heads.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the event started about 30 minutes past its 6:15 p. m. start time, skipping a planned opening video montage for a dance break performed and choreographed by actor Giovanni Wilson with eight dancers to a seemingly AI-produced song that described — in literal terms — how we were at the inaugural AI music awards. The delay forced the show to skip introducing the nominees for the first half of the awards and instead have presenters just state the winner, robbing some attendees of hearing their names called for what felt like one of their biggest achievements.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the event was hosted by wilson and podcast host lana hout, one half of the podcasting duo the “ai chicks,” with a three-member house band of real people playing guitar, bass, keys and drums, soundtracking much of the night. The two hosts shared the only two microphones apparently available throughout the night, with a teleprompter loaded with the Claude-generated run-of-show, but they often seemed lost about what category, presenter, performance or commercial break was next.

Diungkapkan bahwa at one point, hout and wilson were confused over whether they would cut to commercial or bring out the two presenters for best ai country artist. They then brought out the two country award presenters, only for Hout to walk back out mid-introduction to interrupt and say that, actually, they would go to commercial break. The award was eventually presented 13 minutes later with a different presenter.

Diungkapkan bahwa oftentimes, the use of ai seemed to hover over some of the technical hiccups. Deepgram also had a commercial that played throughout the evening, but it would sometimes play at random moments even when a commercial break wasn’t called. Deepgram was meant to power an AI voice that introduced the night’s presenters and nominees, but it often didn’t work and, when it did, talked over many of the presenters. The Deepgram team sat on the couch to my left, and when I looked over to see their reaction to the madness, one member had her head in her hands.

Berdasarkan laporan, early in the night, wilson tried to introduce a trailer for his latest acting gig, the terrance howard-led film “a good hand wasted” that he said used ai to help finish the project, but none of wilson’s cues seemed to get it to play. Once it finally did, the screen only played a portion of the trailer before Howard’s face even appeared.

“So, ugh,” he said, before raising his hand to summon the audience’s applause.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the teleprompter was not much help, often shifting rapidly as presenters were speaking. The chaos led Wilson, who spent much of the night trying to maintain some decorum throughout the frustration, to joke they were “dealing with a prompter that has Tourette’s. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the commercials for the event featured deepgram and a new social network called “trinity social,” with the latter’s ai-generated ad featuring a persona wearing a necklace of the rockstar games logo encouraging a stadium full of generated people to sign up for the app. A Rockstar spokesperson did not respond to an immediate request for comment on whether it authorized the logo, though if it did not, the ad would represent the latest in AI content lifting copyrighted material without permission, all at an event celebrating a use of AI that has rankled the music industry over similar concerns.

Some of the greatest energy came from the evening’s nearly 10 performances, all of which made the cut despite the event running nearly 40 minutes behind schedule the entire night.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there had been some speculation over how, exactly, songs produced with ai and presented by ai avatars would play on stage. Some acts, like country artist Ava Bentley and R&B artist EJ Rogers, lip-synced their entire performance, while others relied on hired performers who did even that for them. For “Chaisen Hale,” a project that features a video of an AI-generated boy with AI-generated vocals, a human lookalike singer named John Victor, 14, was brought out to lip-sync to the track. It turns out, through the power of lip-syncing and acting. Attendees — including one duo, for some reason, dressed as Frankenstein and his bride — were generally riveted.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nearly all of the performances were backed by the live band and dancers, who were provided to the artists for free by siqa. Many who produce music with AI say they did so because they could not afford the studio musicians and resources required to bring their tracks to life, which made the reliance on the house band feel more like an opportunity to live out their dreams without the cost often paid by traditional artists who hire such musicians to produce their work.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, some of the only actual live vocals came from a rapper named godfellow and grammy-winning singers eric bellinger and candace wakefield, the latter of whom made a point to note the “hiccups” throughout the night and that she was singing live as she performed a song by ai artist “aria blue. ” The performances captured much of what remained in the crowd, which grew smaller and smaller as the night progressed.

James, the SIQA founder, acknowledged the “technical difficulties” ahead of presenting Jones with her awards, but she promised those would be resolved ahead of next year’s ceremony.

Berdasarkan laporan, “because there will be a next year because this is the new music industry,” she told the crowd around 9:45 p. , just as it was hitting its hard end time. ”SIQA has created the infrastructure for that industry and for all the artists coming up in that industry. m. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and for many of the people in the room, that’s all they wanted. (When I addressed her by her given name, she snapped at me. Another artist named Ramona Höffel, a 56-year-old woman who spends her days helping disabled people, flew in from Switzerland to represent her AI persona “Vireya” on her first-ever red carpet. One artist, Sheena Taylor, accepted her award for best AI gospel song for a track called “I Denounce You, Satan,” by acknowledging the intense traumas she endured that led to a religious discovery. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i have a lot of ideas and wishes, and for a long time i paint, then i write, and that’s not enough,” she said, visibly nervous to be the first person to walk the red carpet. “The music gives me room to all this bring outside of my brain. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, i thought about höffel’s words as i left the venue just after 10 p. , well past the event’s scheduled 9:30 end, and into the downtown rain. m. It’s unclear whether AI music will generate an enduring monoculture in the way the music from the 2010s has, particularly as the larger music industry has mostly ostracized it. To my right was a line forming to get into the venue for “Club 2010s” night, now delayed due to the prolonged awards show. But it’s left people like Höffel feeling stronger, which is all someone like 2011 chart-topper Kelly Clarkson could ask for.

#802. Forget Black Mirror & Severance, This 16-Episode Masterpiece Nails Existential Sci-Fi

📅 15 Nov 2026

Forget Black Mirror & Severance, This 16-Episode Masterpiece Nails Existential Sci-Fi

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/forget-black-mirror-severance-pantheon-existential-sci-fi/

Sebagaimana diketahui, when it comes to delivering pure existential sci-fi, black mirror and severance would probably be considered the top shows from recent years. Given how both sci-fi series are packed with unsettling explorations of reality, identity, and free will, it is hard not to consider them masterpieces. However, there is one relatively obscure but brilliant sci-fi show that takes existentialism to a whole different level.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, created by craig silverstein and based on a series of short stories by ken liu, pantheon, on the surface, is a cyberpunk conspiracy thriller. Although it is not as well-known as shows like Black Mirror and Severance, it has a solid cult following and boasts a perfect 100% critical score on Rotten Tomatoes. Its acclaim can partly be attributed to its creative animation style and voice acting.

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, the show's true appeal lies in its portrayal of singularity. In its early moments, it sets up a rather simple story where it unfolds in a world where mind-uploading technology is about to be adopted by the masses. With this story setup, though, the show turns into a mind-bending story about the large existential implications of achieving technological singularity and how it challenges our understanding of everything.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, driven by the "ship of theseus" paradox, pantheon initially explores the horrors of uploading one's consciousness. It shows how even after a person awakens in the cloud with the same memories and quirks as their physical self, they are seemingly nothing like their biological original. With this, it prompts one to question whether human evolution is worth it if it strips away one's humanity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, almost reminiscent of severance's innies and outies, pantheon also explores how a cloned character is completely raised in a simulation to be able to replicate the genius of his original counterpart. This becomes an existential exploration of free will, walking through the character's journey of defining his own moral compass despite being coded to be someone else.

Berdasarkan laporan, similar to one of the most harrowing episodes from black mirror, "be right back," pantheon also walks through the story of a grieving daughter and wife. They struggle to process the demise of David Kim. However, when he returns as uploaded intelligence, they are forced to wonder whether he is merely a digital echo of their inability to process their grief.

Sebagaimana diketahui, pantheon originally premiered on amc+, but it is now available for streaming on netflix in the u. S.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in its two-season runtime, pantheon also does not shy away from expanding its vision to an international geopolitical scale before going completely cosmic with its stakes. It highlights how Uploaded Intelligence is ultimately weaponized by nations, leading to a chilling Cold War. In its final arc, the show takes an existential look at the Simulation hypothesis by exploring the long-term implications of its central ideas.

Before Pantheon's ending credits start rolling, the sci-fi series leaves viewers with many questions surrounding the importance of having a finite life span and the existence of true meaning in the face of uncertainty.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, pantheon's narrative eventually spirals into wildly fantastical developments focusing on everything from god-like entitites to dyson spheres. Surprisingly, though, even in these moments, the show feels incredibly grounded and relatable. Even when it expands its vision to cosmic scales, it never forgets the sociological and existential roots of its drama.

Diungkapkan bahwa even its portrayal of imaginative and bizarre technology is made to look familiar through recognizable interfaces. Meanwhile, even its 2-D dimensional animation style ensures that when its sci-fi ideas become a little too extreme, its visuals remain tangible. Without explicitly naming certain characters, Pantheon cleverly parallels them with real tech billionaires.

With this, the sci-fi show even becomes a critique of Silicon Valley's transhumanist culture.

Diungkapkan bahwa it also features real-world pop culture references and even features nods to other popular sci-fi works like frank herbert’s dune and william gibson’s neuromancer. It is unfortunate that Pantheon never got to last as long as shows like Severance and Black Mirror. Even with two seasons, however, the sci-fi show is undoubtedly a masterpiece.
