#909. I Ain't Got No Body: The Various Non-Corporeal Aliens In Star Trek Explained

📅 15 Nov 2026

I Ain't Got No Body: The Various Non-Corporeal Aliens In Star Trek Explained

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2311655/star-trek-non-corporeal-aliens-explained/

Welcome to Trekspertise, a series where we break down the technology, history, details, and decisions that make the Star Trek universe so complex — and so fun.

Berdasarkan laporan, one of the primary features of "star trek" is theoretical biology. Given the wide panoply of alien species on display throughout the franchise, audiences have been invited to ponder alternate evolutionary paths besides the one that happened to bring us into being on Earth. What kind of planetary conditions would be required to form, say, a hyper-intelligent crystalline being? How did a horta evolve? What will we evolve into in the future? Will our brains adapt to become psychic over time? According to the "Star Trek: Voyager" episode "Threshold" (one of the show's most outraging to fans), it was revealed that humans will eventually evolve into giant salamanders.

Berdasarkan laporan, this leads to a few logical evolutionary extremes, like the fact that some species on "star trek" have evolved into beings of pure energy. To cite a notable example: In the original series episode "Is There In Truth No Beauty?," audiences were introduced to the Medusans, a highly intelligent, telepathic, and empathic species whose light-constructed bodies are so wildly complex that any human looking at them would instantly go mad. "Star Trek" has many examples of non-corporeal aliens who can only be perceived as light, as a psychic presence, as a sound, or as a vision beamed directly into our inferior, corporeal brains. Only a mentally disciplined species like the Vulcans could look at a Medusan, and even then required a special filtered visor (pictured above).

These kinds of aliens expand the audience's mind as to what can be considered life.

Diungkapkan bahwa in looking at fictional non-corporeal species, "star trek" expands our horizons. We're invited to ponder new perspectives about basic concepts like evolution, time, the nature of consciousness, and, perhaps, our own relationship to the cosmos. Non-corporeal entities are one of the coolest ideas "Star Trek" has to offer, and their recurring nature is a constant reminder that life is more complex, and the cosmos more ineffable, than we could ever hope to imagine.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on "star trek," non-corporeal aliens tend to appear as lights or clouds or glowing mists of energy. " That entity had the ability to sort of intuitively communicate with Cochrane (Glenn Corbett), and could also heal diseases and sustain human life beyond its usual biological barriers. Others might immediately think of Zefram Cochrane's glowing, cloud-like "companion" in the episode "Metamorphosis. One might recall the smoke-like alien that made Kirk nervous in the episode "Obsession," one of the more underrated episodes of the show. A common theme of non-corporeal entities on "Star Trek" is that they are godlike and powerful, able to tap into the powers of the universe in ways we don't understand.

Diungkapkan bahwa the medusans may be one of the most popular non-corporeal entities on "star trek," but fans of "deep space nine" would surely want me to acknowledge the wormhole aliens, a. a. k. The Prophets. In that show's pilot episode, "Emissary," Benjamin Sisko (Avery Brooks) travels into a stable wormhole and encounters bodiless creatures who can only communicate with him by appearing as people from his memories.

Berdasarkan laporan, the wormhole aliens from "deep space nine" are so, well, alien, they don't understand concepts like linguistic communication or linear time. They don't see cause leading to effect, but rather a widespread series of events that happen all at once. Sisko has to do the impossible, and explain the human habit of seeing time as a straight line.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and, of course, there are many species of godlike beings on "star trek" who often take the form of humans, despite not having physical bodies. Those two beings tend to see corporeal humans as lesser species and amuse themselves by taunting and playing with them. Kevin took the form of a human, married, and witnessed his wife killed, leading him to, in a moment of ill-temper, commit instant galaxy-wide genocide of a single species. Less whimsical is Kevin Uxbridge (John Anderson), a member of a powerful energy species called the Douwd. He's the deadliest character in all of "Star Trek. Q (John de Lancie) from "Star Trek: The Next Generation" is one of these beings, as is Trelane (William Campbell) from the original series. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the list goes on. Q tormented the Calamarain, which exist as ionized gas. There are the Organians, the Lights of Zetar, and the godlike Metrons, the latter of whom oversaw the fight between Kirk (William Shatner) and the Gorn in the episode "Arena," and plenty of other examples. In most cases, non-corporeal entities are so far beyond human experience, it's difficult to communicate with them, much less come to some kind of diplomatic understanding.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but sometimes non-corporeal entities do become our friends. On "Star Trek: Prodigy," the character of Zero (Angus Imrie) is a Medusan who managed to construct a robot-like vehicle for themselves, allowing them to interact with us flesh-beings without exposing themselves. Sometimes the ineffability of the cosmos works in our favor.

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/rivals-season-2-part-2-aidan-turner-victoria-smurfit-emily-atack/

Berdasarkan laporan, greer riddell is a london-based film and television journalist writing about comedy, streaming and the evolving media industry in the uk and usa. She works at Collider, covering the latest in film, television and entertainment through interviews, features, reviews and industry coverage.

Sebagaimana diketahui, her recent brand collaborations include hbo, warner bros. , Netflix, Hulu, Sky, Disney+ and DC Studios. She has covered titles including Saturday Night Live UK, Rivals, Scrubs, Stuart Fails to Save the Universe, Ludwig, Supergirl and Stranger Things.

Her recent interviews include Florence Pugh, Mike Faist and Christopher Abbott for Netflix's East of Eden, Taika Waititi and Jenna Ortega for Klara and the Sun.

Berdasarkan laporan, editor's note: the following contains spoilers for rivals season 2, episodes 7-9. It's been a long wait since June to find out whether Tony Baddingham (David Tennant) and Maud O'Hara (Victoria Smurfit) will get their comeuppance after their affair led to Monica Baddingham (Claire Rushbrook) dying in a car accident during a storm. Rivals is never short of drama, and that's not all for the Baddinghams, as it was revealed earlier in the season that Sarah Stratton's (Emily Atack) baby is also Tony's illegitimate child.

Diungkapkan bahwa to explore these cliffhangers and more, collider joined aidan turner, smurfit, and atack to discuss the first three explosive episodes of rivals season 2, part 2. They break down Declan and Maud's extraordinary argument on Bonfire Night and reveal whether Declan will finally give in to the urges he's been repressing out of fierce loyalty to his wife. Atack shares why she enjoys playing Sarah at her most vulnerable and why the most confident characters are often not what they seem. The trio also reveal what goes on behind the scenes on the Rivals set and whether being part of a series that's so much fun to watch is equally enjoyable to film.

Sebagaimana diketahui, collider: well, i didn't think rivals could get more dramatic, but the last three episodes, they've really blown it out of the water. And I have to ask first: that big showdown between Maud and Declan. Have you recovered from that? In the kitchen?.

SMURFIT: I was just saying my hips are still sore!.

TURNER: [Laughter] I feel really bad about that.

TURNER: Well, I kept on hitting the dirt.

SMURFIT: It's only a hairy second, isn't it?.

Berdasarkan laporan, turner: i kept throwing you down quite hard. It’s one of those ones.

TURNER: It's a year ago now; it still hurts.

Diungkapkan bahwa smurfit: she does. Anyway, so yes, it was great. So, it was like all the emotions, all the justifications, all the failings, all the passion, all. It was weirdly fun to do because it was such a juicy, beautifully written scene. you know, it was just, oh, it was just juicy, wasn't it?.

SMURFIT: You don't get many of those in your career.

Sebagaimana diketahui, turner: you don't. I find when I work, it just all goes a bit weird, and there was a strange energy in the air, and I kind of went wild. Maybe it was a full moon or something, but I felt a bit crazed that night. It's also, not that this should really matter — but it kind of does for me — it was a night shoot, and there's something that happens at nighttime. Did you?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, smurfit: well, yeah. You kept feckin’ me in a fire!.

Is that something that you do as an actor to get yourself into that sort of big emotional state? Because you're really asked to go from zero to 11 in a really quick space of time.

Sebagaimana diketahui, turner: yeah. Sometimes I think we split the scene where he runs out, but you're in the moment from moment to moment. Yeah. I mean, you just kind of do it, but it's also like, you want to stay present. So you can't play what's ahead of you.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, smurfit: when you know where you're starting and the stuff that's behind you, you don't think about what's coming. You know where you're at, and then you put your foot on the gas, and you're playing with great actors, then it's all just sort of there.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there's a few moments, actually, in that where declan was stood in the trees and him obviously being incredibly angry there. There were times where it was quite similar to the visuals we got of Tony and him being really angry. So I wondered if that was a conscious decision, or you thought about, actually, is Declan going to get to that Tony level of anger throughout?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, turner: he did get really angry. I think he completely lost control.

Sebagaimana diketahui, turner: i was just saying earlier, i mean, which i sort of forgotten about, but i feel thankful there were other people around. I feel really scared when I think of what he would have done had no one else been there to stop him. It was a kind of blind anger he had.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i'm looking forward to seeing what happens when sarah's secret fully comes out because it's been teased. A few people know. But when Tony actually finds out that has gone around the whole village, that's going to be mad. That's going to be another confrontation, I think! But I wanted to ask you, what's something you enjoy the most? Is it playing somebody who's really confident or at their most exposed? Because there are a lot of scenes in this where you're having some quite emotional moments.

Diungkapkan bahwa atack: yeah, i was really grateful for that. I think she's learned to be a certain way. She has to be a certain way to survive in the world that she's in. And, yeah, women like Sarah are definitely that. And I think what it touches on is the obvious thing that so many outwardly confident people are often inside, kind of, battling something else, battling vulnerability. You know, a male-dominated world, the world of telly.

Berdasarkan laporan, i think that what's so great about the writing is characters like sarah, who would have been so unlikable in other tv shows, but there's something about this. There's something about Rivals where you really root for people that are making all these terrible mistakes and making all these mental decisions.

Diungkapkan bahwa i was really happy when i read the script that we got to expose that vulnerability underneath all the hair and the makeup and the confidence and sexiness. Because that's kind of true to life, really. Not me, just [laughs] confident people; they're often covering something.

The two stars of the Hulu series also break down their characters' toxic relationship.

Berdasarkan laporan, so now that declan has found out that maud and tony have been an item, he has obviously been very loyal to maud before. Does this mean he might have a change of heart? May he explore seeing if Cameron's still interested? Is he going to explore some of those urges?.

Diungkapkan bahwa turner: i don't know what urges he's going to explore, but i think it's going to be difficult for him to come to terms with this. I think it's been really hard on him, and that's going to continue. There's obviously so much love there, and they have this really strong connection, and there's been things in the past — different infidelities and affairs that they've managed to wade through, but this feels different this time. I don't know if he's going to be able to forgive. I think she hurt him in the most fundamental. So, I don't know how it's going to play out. Maybe he will. I don't know.

Is there a behind-the-scenes moment for you that really sums up what it's like to have been a part of that set? Because it looks really fun from where we're watching at home.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, smurfit: i think a lot of the memories, when we do. in a lot of the episodes, we have a set piece, as we call it, which is most of the cast all together at a Hunt Ball, at the polo, you know, all these different set pieces. And it's usually got an incredible story. Everyone's together, so they'll pull this group of people in, and the rest are held in the tent or in a room, and invariably what's happening is games of chess, games of cards, games of— what was that spy game that Brendan Patricks always brings?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, smurfit: codenames, where you're — it's basically like the traitors — all lying. And it's so fun to watch everybody dip into the game; they're called, they go off to work, and then just somebody else will take over the game that they're playing. And, and so there are all these tables full of different, different actors sitting together playing the games. And it's like a big, weird family, dysfunctional children, and absolutely no adults.

You just made me think, actually, that all of the characters in Rivals, they'd be too good at playing The Traitors because they'd all be good at lying, and no one would be able to identify them.

ATACK: It's kind of like they are playing The Traitors!.

Sebagaimana diketahui, turner: i don’t know if declan would be very good at lying. Maybe not him, but, yeah, everyone else, maybe!.

One part of his incredible legacy is voice acting; how could he not try his hand there when he had such a magnificent voice? Stewart's defining voice role is probably the eccentric CIA Deputy Director Avery Bullock on "American Dad. " Casting him against type there is the whole joke. Patrick Stewart, famous for playing dignified, fatherly authority figures like Captain Jean-Luc Picard and Professor Charles Xavier, is the one saying all of Bullock's ridiculous, profane, and unhinged lines, which become even funnier read in his baritone voice.

Berdasarkan laporan, the folks behind the biblical epic "the prince of egypt" also knew the weight stewart's voice carried. Patrick Stewart plays Pharaoh Seti, adoptive father of Moses and the man who ordered the massacre of Hebrew babies that made Moses' mother send him away. At Steven Spielberg's suggestion, DreamWorks Animation adapted the first stretch of the Book of Exodus, or how the prophet Moses (Val Kilmer) — raised as an Egyptian prince — discovered his true heritage and led his people out of bondage. Stewart/Seti has only a few scant scenes in the movie's first act, but he casts a shadow as wide as any pyramid over the rest of the film.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as with later dreamworks pictures, "the prince of egypt" employs celebrity voice casting: kilmer as moses, ralph fiennes as moses' brother/seti's son pharaoh rameses, etc. But here, it mostly works — mostly. Jeff Goldblum as Moses' brother Aaron is a distracting bit of casting where you hear the actor first, not the character. "Prince of Egypt" doesn't disguise Stewart's voice either (you probably couldn't with a voice of such power), but it complements his character to a chilling effect.

Diungkapkan bahwa in "the prince of egypt," seti first appears admonishing his two sons for being reckless in a chariot race. " When Moses asks his father to go easier on Rameses, Seti offers understanding (and pure dramatic irony): "Moses, you will never have to carry a burden like the crown I will pass to Rameses. He's especially harsh on his heir, Rameses, explaining that "one weak link can break the chain of a mighty dynasty. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, pretty typical patrick stewart, right? seti is stern but reasonable, some of the same qualities that made captain picard such a respected leader. His respect-commanding voice is even more effective as a disappointed father, too; would you want to hear "I'm disappointed in you" from that voice?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but then moses learns the truth about where he came from, and how. Seeing his son in despair, Seti is gentle but also doesn't deny he had a generation of Hebrew babies murdered as population control. The animation and Stewart's performance work in perfect sync. In Seti's whispered tone, he sounds genuinely pained. Even if his claim "sometimes, for the greater good, sacrifices must be made," rings hollow here, Seti's thousand yard stare tells us that maybe he does feel the weight of what he did and realizes he's damned for it.

Berdasarkan laporan, but then the kicker comes: he tries to "comfort" moses that the babies cast into the nile "were only slaves. " The dissonance of Seti loving his own family and also being a genocidal enslaver is potent, but sadly believable. Fittingly, this is also the last time we see him in the film, because the bond he shared with Moses has been severed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the prince of egypt" is one of the most gorgeously animated films ever made, and it's not only the animation that's beautifully crafted. The storytelling is sharp and mature. It sits at the very fine line of being simple enough for kids and complex enough for adults; Moses and Rameses being turned from beloved brothers to enemies by forces much bigger than themselves is painful to watch.

Berdasarkan laporan, right off, "the prince of egypt" is an unconventional title for the exodus story; after all, the whole story is about moses rejecting that life for his people by birth. (Compare it to the 1956 biblical epic titled "The Ten Commandments. ") But the movie paints Moses' deliverance of his people as bittersweet, since it cost him the brother he loved.

Diungkapkan bahwa though not nearly as controversial as nikos kazantzakis's book (and later martin scorsese's film) "the last temptation of christ," "the prince of egypt" similarly invents human drama from scripture. So, then, wouldn't he be afflicted by man's foibles and doubts? The Book of Exodus holds that Moses was raised as an Egyptian in the Pharaoh's own family. "Last Temptation" works from the tenet that Jesus was both fully divine but also fully human. Wouldn't Moses, then, feel pained about having to turn his back on the home where he was raised, even if he recognized the necessity of God's plan for him?.

Diungkapkan bahwa part of the tragedy is that this only flows one way. After Moses learns the truth, he can't look at the enslaved Hebrew workers without thinking their birthright is also his. Conversely, neither Seti nor Rameses clock that the son/brother they love would've been just another of those slaves. It's an excellent use of Patrick Stewart, twisting our relationship to his fatherly presence and providing an undercurrent of darkness to it.

Diungkapkan bahwa there's something of a paradox when it comes to making legitimately good crime action movies. On the one hand, most filmmakers want the action to be as accurate and based in reality as possible, whether it be robbing a bank, taking down a security truck, or whatnot. On the other hand, they don't necessarily wish to inspire criminals who would copycat a crime they happened to see in a movie, especially as that's an instance where all publicity doesn't necessarily equal good publicity. (Remember the brouhaha over a crime allegedly inspired by 1995's "Money Train," a case which only just reached a resolution a few years ago?).

Berdasarkan laporan, the irony of the new crime action film "how to rob a bank" is that it intentionally wishes to exist on the edge separating these two sides. wealth gap, decide to become bank robbers. The film, written by Mark Bianculli and directed by David Leitch, concerns a group of friends who, upon becoming radicalized by the various injustices of the current U. S. Their gimmick is hiding their crimes in plain sight, filming themselves in the act and detailing exactly how they did it for their YouTube channel (all while hiding their identities, naturally).

Berdasarkan laporan, thus, leitch and bianculli have to include a bunch of real-world tactics and hardware without going too far. e. To help accomplish this, they have their bandits (who've dubbed themselves the Wolf Pack) borrow a technique from the sequel to the bonafide action classic that is "Die Hard," i. 1990's "Die Hard 2. " And while the characters never mention the movie on-screen, the inclusion of a trick used by that film's villains works as both an Easter egg homage to that movie as well as a bit of real-world verisimilitude, as this particular tactic does sound like it could actually work.

Berdasarkan laporan, in "die hard 2," the terrorists holding washington dulles international airport hostage around christmas are former u. After Bruce Willis' John McClane their plans while getting a quip or two in, the airport brass call in a military counter-terrorism unit. Then, during the subsequent firefights between the counter-terrorism unit and the terrorists, each group makes a point of switching to clips for their machine guns labeled with blue instead of red stripes. S. Army soldiers who've been corrupted by a military drug lord. Eventually, McClane discovers this code means blue for blank rounds and red for live rounds, revealing that both units are working together.

Diungkapkan bahwa while the terrorists in "die hard 2" have devised a fairly elaborate scheme, the blank-vs-live rounds element seems fairly simple and self-explanatory. The Wolf Pack want to make their robberies feel threatening to the authorities they encounter and only elect to use live rounds to save their own skins. In other words, it has an authenticity about it, which is why its use in "How to Rob a Bank" feels smooth rather than belabored. As such, adopting the blue and red labeled gun clips makes for an easy to understand visual code, so much so that the characters in the film barely have to explain it to the audience.

Berdasarkan laporan, for those who know "die hard 2," this is a cute easter egg calling back to that film's intuitive code system. Who knows if anyone has used it (or will) in real life, but it helps "How to Rob a Bank" exist on that edge.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the wizarding world of harry potter, albus dumbledore is often referred to as one of the wisest and most powerful wizards in history. In the original Harry Potter film franchise (which is getting a new life, in a way, with the forthcoming HBO Harry Potter TV show), Harry Potter, as played by Daniel Radcliffe (who may not watch the HBO reboot series), leaves his humdrum life with his mean non-magical relatives behind and starts attending Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, run by Dumbledore (Richard Harris in the first two movies before the legendary actor passed away in 2002, at which point Michael Gambon took over). so, it's lucky for the titular boy wizard that Dumbledore just happens to be the headmaster of his magical academy. Berdasarkan laporan, it's a rare thing when two equally well-known artists collaborate behind the camera. This year alone, we've seen the news that Steven Soderbergh is helping out Matt Reeves with "The Batman Part II," while Quentin Tarantino has handed the "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" character of Cliff Booth over to David Fincher for the upcoming Netflix spin-off. An auteur director team-up doesn't happen often, but it's certainly not unheard of. Famously, Fincher took over the troubled "Alien 3" after it had been developed for years, and inherited a script structure from director Vincent Ward that he isn't thrilled with to this day.

Diungkapkan bahwa around the same time, the budding film auteur (who was then still primarily known as a music video director) was approached to make a video for the rock star meat loaf's 1993 single "i'd do anything for love (but i won't do that). (That's one version of the story, at least; more on that later. " However, Fincher's price tag caused Meat Loaf to look elsewhere for the video's director, turning to none other than an up-and-coming Michael Bay. " According to Craig Marks and Rob Tannenbaum's 2011 book "I Want My MTV: The Uncensored Story of the Music Video Revolution," Fincher and Meat Loaf's vision was pretty much what the finished video became, a Gothic riff on "Beauty and the Beast. ) Though the two didn't directly work together on it, the final video is, in its own weird way, a collaboration between the pair.

Berdasarkan laporan, although michael bay and david fincher technically worked together at the production company propaganda films, their relationship was definitely more complex than just coworkers or collaborators. As various colleagues and other luminaries who worked at or with Propaganda detail in "I Want My MTV," Fincher was already a star internally given his extensive work on numerous successful music videos, and this was something that the young Bay was all too aware of. Employees told Craig Marks and Rob Tannenbaum that Bay would follow Fincher around the Propaganda offices constantly, with some people already considering him a younger version of Fincher.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this comparison came to a head when meat loaf approached fincher with the gig for "i'd do anything for love. " According to Meat Loaf, the musician pitched Fincher with a "Beauty and the Beast" premise for the video, which Fincher allegedly loved. However, Fincher supposedly gave Meat Loaf a quote of $2. 3 million, which Loaf balked at. He continued:.

Diungkapkan bahwa "so he came back a few days later and gave me a budget of $1. ' And Fincher said, 'Well then, get Michael Bay. 7 million. ' That's the last time Michael Bay was the cheaper option. I said, 'David, we don't have that kind of money. ".

So, in Meat Loaf's version of the tale, the vision for the music video was the singer's idea, Fincher couldn't make the budget work, and the then-cheaper Bay got a hand-me-down project which he spun into a hit video.

Berdasarkan laporan, in meat loaf's version of what happened with the "i'd do anything for love (but i won't do that)" music video, the video was an idea had by the singer which changed hands from david fincher to michael bay. However, according to Propaganda Films producer Joni Sighvatsson, it was his idea to pass the torch from Fincher to Bay, and as such, the video ended up being the one and only collaboration between the two filmmakers. As he recalled:.

Diungkapkan bahwa "fincher was very expensive. He and the label were at an impasse over the Meat Loaf video, so I said, 'Why don't we just give this to Michael Bay?' Fincher gave it to Bay, we ended up spending $750,000, and it was a seminal video. That was the first and last time Fincher and Bay collaborated. Michael directed, and it was David's concept. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, it's very possible that sighvatsson is merely aggrandizing the story of the "i'd do anything for love" video, making it sound like it's the result of two now-famous auteurs rather than just one. It's the most perfect visual encapsulation of Meat Loaf's sound, all theatricality and opera. Or it's possible that he and Meat Loaf have hazy memories of what went down and how. It's got Bay's fingerprints all over it, of course, from a fetishization of hardware and sunsets to the way every woman is shot like a supermodel. All we really have to go on is the video itself, which remains one of the most visually rapturous short films of the 1990s. Yet the video's Gothic flavor and trappings feel more Fincheresque. However it happened, the video is a gift, and we should probably thank all three men for it.

#923. Grey's Anatomy's Downfall Can Be Traced Back To One Moment

Grey's Anatomy's Downfall Can Be Traced Back To One Moment

Diungkapkan bahwa "grey's anatomy" has been on the air since 2005, which is to say that it's experienced a handful of high highs and very low lows. Shonda Rhimes' medical drama, which premiered as a humble mid-season replacement and became one of the longest-running shows in the history of its medium, stars Ellen Pompeo as surgical intern turned award-winning general surgery attending and hospital owner Dr. Meredith Grey, who lives, loves, and learns alongside her colleagues and who has a knack for picking up cases that connect to her personal life in some way (as all of the doctors do, honestly).

Berdasarkan laporan, (i say it "stars" pompeo, but there's a technicality here; pompeo technically left "grey's anatomy" as a series regular in season 19 in 2022, but still provides voiceover and appears on the show often enough that she's still the main character for all intents and purposes. ).

Diungkapkan bahwa there are, if i'm being honest, many parts of "grey's anatomy" that one could identify as a major series downfall, like the time dr. The issue? Many of those lows are followed by highs (as Heigl's Izzie leaves the series, there's a hospital merger followed by a two-part finale in Season 6 that's a legitimate series highlight). Isobel "Izzie" Stevens (Katherine Heigl) has ghostly physical intimacy with her dead fiancé before figuring out it's a brain tumor, the time a plane crash kills most of the show's surgeons, or every time a wedding is interrupted by a dramatic, ridiculous problem. That's why I'm pointing to a true point of no return for "Grey's Anatomy," and I am truly sorry to say that, despite my respect for the show's commitment to "realism" during a terrifying time for the entire world, the 17th season of the medical drama, also known as the "COVID season," is its downfall.

Berdasarkan laporan, at face value, it makes total sense for a show like "grey's anatomy" to address the very real covid-19 pandemic head-on; because the characters also dressed in protective medical gear, there was an air of practicality to the whole thing to boot. Here's the problem: the way they addressed it was straight-up bonkers. Partway through Season 17, Meredith develops a pretty serious case of COVID-19, which sidelines her (and, to an extent, Ellen Pompeo) for the remainder of the season's run, giving her a truly bizarre storyline where she sees dead loved ones in dreams in a random seaside location that fans like me simply refer to as the "coma beach. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, instead, fans of the series couldn't escape the pandemic surrounding them, and to make things worse, the show's best quality — its genuinely funny and smart dialogue — fell by the wayside in the process. Meredith may have eventually recovered from her severe case of COVID-19 and left the coma beach behind after Season 17, but the show wasn't able to pull off the same feat. and as it continues, you can feel the slip in quality with each passing season.

Berdasarkan laporan, i know better than most people that "grey's anatomy" has its fair share of detractors; i've been watching this damn show since it premiered, and it's one of the longest relationships of my life without comparison. I'll be among the first to admit that a lot of it is heightened and silly — and I got the chance to interview a friend who's a real doctor for this very site, who confirmed that it's the least realistic televised medical drama by a country mile.

Sebagaimana diketahui, still, i'll go to the mat for a lot of seasons and episodes of "grey's anatomy. The chemistry between most of the original actors was undeniably great, its jokes often hit their mark beautifully, and remember that two-part Season 6 finale I mentioned? "Sanctuary" and "Death and All His Friends," which chronicles a devastating mass shooting within the walls of the central hospital, is one of my favorite TV episodes ever. " Shonda Rhimes, while she was still hands-on with the series, was a masterful dialogue writer and gave actors like Sandra Oh (who left the series after the Season 10 finale) unbelievably sharp monologues with regularity. and I'd stack it against plenty of prestige dramas any day.

Diungkapkan bahwa that's what makes the fall of "grey's anatomy" particularly painful for me. Instead of quippy dialogue that feels like a tennis match, characters over-explain everything in the preachiest way possible (like a female doctor explaining to a male counterpart that women get Brazilian butt lifts because society influences them into it). I'm committed to the proverbial bit by still watching it, but it's painful. "Grey's Anatomy" is a pale shadow of what it once was, and it all started in Season 17.

#928. 7 Best Things About the Original Xbox That Aren't Halo, Ranked

📅 15 Nov 2026

7 Best Things About the Original Xbox That Aren't Halo, Ranked

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/xbox-retrospective-best-things-besides-halo/

Sebagaimana diketahui, when microsoft entered the console market with its xbox brand, people outside the company didn’t necessarily have high hopes. Throughout the 1990s, the industry was dominated by Japanese hardware companies like Nintendo, Sega, and Sony. But Microsoft meant business, and its first console effort provided some excellent reasons to give the brand a chance.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the best reasons to own an xbox was undoubtedly halo: combat evolved, with a compelling first-person campaign and a multiplayer mode that kept people busy for dozens or even hundreds of hours. Bungie’s sci-fi epic shifted a lot of hardware units, but it wasn’t the only reason for players to be excited. Here are seven of the best things about the original Xbox that aren’t Halo.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the xbox came out during a difficult time for sega. The company had just ended an unfortunate string of hardware failures that concluded with the death of the Dreamcast, its final console. That platform had offered all sorts of great games, but they didn’t connect with wide audiences because everyone was too focused on the PlayStation 2, which offered a built-in DVD player that made it a particularly attractive prospect.

Berdasarkan laporan, microsoft offered sega a way to present its own vision for a console future without devoting all of its resources to challenging hardware. A string of terrific Sega titles hit the Xbox during its early years, and Microsoft promoted them aggressively, from Jet Set Radio Future to Sega GT 2002 and even more niche affairs like Gun Valkyrie. That support persisted throughout the console’s life, and also produced Panzer Dragoon Orta, one of the very finest games on the system.

Diungkapkan bahwa commercial tie-ins weren’t huge news by the time burger king released a series of three video games near the end of the xbox life-cycle. They had been around for some time, particularly during the Atari 2600 era. In 1983, Chase the Chuck Wagon even built a game around a dog chasing a wagon, which consumers obtained by sending in UPC labels clipped from bags of Purina dog food.

Sebagaimana diketahui, burger king brought that convention back with sneak king, pocketbike racer, and big bumpin’. To get a copy, players paid a small fee while placing an order for a value meal. At the time, Burger King advertised heavily in print and on TV with its creepy “king” character, who featured in each of the games. The games worked on both the original Xbox and the newer 360, a cross-generation wonder that people have largely forgotten.

Sebagaimana diketahui, players naturally associate microsoft with halo, which it published on behalf of bungie. Fable, from Lionhead Studios, kicked off another successful franchise that’s scheduled to return early in 2027 with a reboot from Playground Games. But the giant publisher also took chances on less conventional fare during the era.

Diungkapkan bahwa one such game was kung fu chaos, which offered a parody of ‘70s b-movie chaos. In a slapstick fighting brawler along the lines of Power Stone, players survived perilous environments and talked trash to their opponents until one fighter emerged the victor. The edgy humor doesn’t hold up well today, but plenty of players had fun with it at the time.

Berdasarkan laporan, other unusual releases from the time included phantom dust, a deck builder with 3d arena battles, and voodoo vince. The latter was a platformer featuring a voodoo doll roaming New Orleans. To harm enemies, he had to inflict damage on himself through dangerous maneuvers, like setting himself on fire. Players never knew quite what to expect from Microsoft Game Studios at the time, and it was wonderful.

Diungkapkan bahwa first released on nov. 15, 2001, the original Xbox missed the ‘90s by only a little bit. As it helped define the 2000s gaming scene, it did so with help from one powerful component: the hard drive.

Sebagaimana diketahui, players suddenly had a lot of space to store their game saves. They could install them directly to the device, no longer relying on separate memory cards. If they preferred, they could also rip audio CDs to the drive and then play their favorite titles accompanied by their favorite music. You haven’t lived until you’ve played Dead or Alive Xtreme Beach Volleyball while Creed, Nickelback, and Avril Lavigne croon in the background.

Berdasarkan laporan, unlike today, when a required install for a game like grand theft auto 6 can eat up roughly a third of your available space on a playstation 5, the original xbox supported large libraries without flinching. That made it an especially good time to be an Xbox fan.

Diungkapkan bahwa formerly known as tehkan, the game publisher that became tecmo (and later koei tecmo) published its first original console game on the famicom in 1986. Traditionally a Japanese publisher, the company nevertheless made a name for itself in North America, thanks in large part to the classic Ninja Gaiden series.

Berdasarkan laporan, unexpectedly, tecmo threw considerable support behind the xbox hardware, and with excellent results. Ninja Gaiden (later released in an expanded form as Ninja Gaiden Black) became one of the hardware’s biggest successes. Tecmo also brought over the excellent Dead or Alive fighting game series, which felt like the perfect match for Microsoft’s powerful system. The beautiful environments and the detailed fighters within them provided ample eye candy to remind players that console gaming had come a long way since the 8-bit figures they remembered stomping on turtles only a decade prior.

Graphics were still a huge differentiator, and Tecmo was arguably the era’s developer that did the most to prove the Xbox was a graphical powerhouse.

Diungkapkan bahwa a weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

Diungkapkan bahwa console gaming had a certain feel to it by the time the xbox arrived, and microsoft quickly pushed some boundaries. Today, many games release on PC alongside their console counterparts, but that wasn’t the case back in 2001, when Xbox began building bridges across some of the biggest gaps.

Diungkapkan bahwa on xbox, we got to see some games that surprised us, like the elder scrolls 3: morrowind, star wars: knights of the old republic, and even sid meier’s pirates. Microsoft also published versions of the original Fable across the two platforms, and the role-playing epic felt just right on both. And MechAssault made a big splash when Xbox Live launched, proving the power of the hardware to provide compelling online play experiences.

Berdasarkan laporan, the dreamcast deserves credit for making some early efforts in the same arena, but the xbox stuck the landing. In the process, it set Microsoft up to enjoy the even more successful generation that followed with the Xbox 360.

Berdasarkan laporan, by the time the xbox came around, the strong relationship between rare and nintendo had soured enough that the time was ripe for someone else to swoop in and acquire the most storied software developer in twycross, england. Microsoft saw the opportunity and went for it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, although it has failed to capitalize on the rare acquisition the way people once thought it might, microsoft did acquire some early gems in the years before sea of thieves. The latter served as one of the final Microsoft releases on its first console. Grabbed by the Ghoulies and Conker: Live & Reloaded both launched on the original Xbox. A remake of the surprisingly vulgar Nintendo 64 classic, it provided not only a visual overhaul of the single-player campaign, but multiplayer modes that kept players busy fragging each other for hours at a time.

Berdasarkan laporan, most of rare’s post-nintendo triumphs came during the xbox 360 era, but its earliest efforts on the original xbox are solid games that hold up reasonably well today. They didn’t exactly set the world on fire, but they’re fun to revisit even now. You can still acquire them on the Xbox Store today, and they’re well worth a look.

Diungkapkan bahwa disc-to-digital is either a genuine players-first initiative or a swipe at sony. Either way, I'll take it.

#937. Stardew Valley Meets Night in the Woods in One of 2026's Scariest New Games

📅 15 Nov 2026

Stardew Valley Meets Night in the Woods in One of 2026's Scariest New Games

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/village-in-the-shade-new-farm-sim-horror-game/

Diungkapkan bahwa i thought i knew what to expect from village in the shade after attending nis america's pre-launch preview event in september. But they're dark on a small-scale, personal level, and rarely do they have something poignant to say. Nippon Ichi Software's non-Disgaea games get pretty dark, as do the Labyrinth games and Yomawari. The villagers would be quirky but likeable, and things would probably get at least a little twisted, though nothing too terrible. Village in the Shade tossed all my expectations out the window within the first few hours and, since then, has quickly rocketed up my list of the year's best games.

Diungkapkan bahwa village in the shade starts with a child frolicking in the fields, running through dappled woods, skipping over rivers, and doing normal kid stuff. Not that the idea brought anyone joy. Then they fall down a hole and die, or so you'd think from the amount of blood on-screen, except they climb out and start walking again like nothing happened. The local carpenter and a hunter find the child, who happens to bear a striking resemblance to a kid who vanished years ago. Something did happen, though. They seem worried, actually, but Rin, the de facto mayor of Kagatsu Village, decides the child may be of use.

Diungkapkan bahwa rin initially seems like a tom nook caricature. She's fixated on profit and productivity, stuffs you in a ratty little hovel, charges you for it, and decides your value based on how much you do for the community. One life out of the village in exchange for another life in. But NIS had something much more interesting in mind, which became evident the next in-game day when Rin threw a baby goat down the village well as an offering. There's a bit of subtle commentary from her about min-maxing supposedly relaxing games to get the most out of them, and I thought this poke at established cozy staples would be the extent of Rin's personality. Balance must be maintained.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it likely comes as no surprise to hear this following a sentence that includes the words "threw a baby goat down the well," but kagatsu village is a weird place. Their families lived at the foot of this mountain for generations. A good quarter of the people who live there agree with that assessment. Even so, they don’t seem to have much of a choice but to stay and deal with it. Leaving would be tantamount to betrayal of everyone past and present, and who knows what might happen then?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rin and kagatsu village under her rule are the epitome of toxic communalism. It’s less great if you just want to help a friend out with no strings attached. She's sincere in her dogged determination to put the village first — frighteningly so at times — but either overlooks or just plain doesn't understand the harm of ignoring the individual. Part of Kagatsu's code is that every favor must be met with appropriate compensation, which is great for people with mercenary dispositions. As long as the collective is intact and moving forward, every sacrifice is permissible. You're also not supposed to pry into anyone's affairs or share their secrets, no matter how upset they are or whether they're gathering poison as part of a murder plot. And mandatory.

Berdasarkan laporan, the most common sacrifice is a monthly fee, like a tax, though to rin's intense frustration, people tend to get around it. Some perform a service. Those with nothing to give, or who flat-out refuse to give anything, are taken to the local clinic where the doctor draws a rather alarming amount of blood. There's the monthly offering, of course, along with a spate of serial killings 10 years in the past — around the time you disappeared from the village, in what's surely a totally normal coincidence. Others give food or necessary items. Blood figures quite prominently in Village in the Shade. On some nights, one of the bridges leading to the center of town is covered in blood.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i'm a coward and haven't ventured beyond the bridge on those nights, so i don't know why the blood is there yet. That, plus a general lack of defensive capabilities and places to hide, is enough to get the adrenaline going during evening wanderings. Untold horrors slither down the mountain and haunt the streets and alleys, and dealing with them is much more nerve-wracking than I originally thought. It was pretty tame. Village in the Shade uses a drumming sound like a heartbeat and a tremor effect on the screen when danger approaches, and they increase in intensity the closer you get to the source of it. The preview session showed the very first haunted incident, a linear segment where the ghost of an old man chases you through the village. Nighttime is dangerous in Kagatsu Village. The rest of the hauntings are not. Stealth and bloody death were not on my bingo card when I started this game, and the intensity of these moments — plus just how at odds they are with the sedate daytime routine — make them standouts.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the "weird rural place with a terrible past" and its critiques on collectivism aren't entirely uncommon in japanese media. Ryukishi07's Higurashi: When They Cry springs to mind as one of the stronger examples of it, and, more recently, there's The Summer Hikaru Died and even Nintendo's Emio — The Smiling Man. The concept is typically reserved for anime or visual novels, though, and I've yet to come across a good example of the storytelling style in more interactive media. Who'd have thought a farm-sim could make the perfect fit for it? Certainly not me.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but it does, and even the calm routine surprised me. Village in the Shade holds little back at the start and throws a lot of crop variety, processing machines, and progress at you. Most farming games in the last decade have done very little to shake up the daily chores, and even Stardew Valley followed a pattern familiar from old Harvest Moon games. I'd upgraded my tools once by the first summer, reached level 50 of the mine, and harvested enough spring crops to get them all to silver rank in quality.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it's not too easy, though, and nis didn't skimp on the farming just to facilitate storytelling. There were flower fields for producing honey, flowers for selling, and a smaller plot for gift flowers. Crop-producing trees had a section all to themselves. In that first summer, I divided my fields (plural, as I bought a second one with my springtime earnings) into planned segments. The furrowed vegetables — Village in the Shade lets you alternate between tillage and furrows to encourage faster growth for some species — had a section all to themselves, just because uniformity looked nice.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while i hadn't created rice paddies yet, that didn't stop me from spending thousands of yen on seedlings while the store had them in stock, and i created a special bed of edamame beans that i'd let ripen into autumn for a soybean harvest. Meanwhile, at the other end of the homestead plot sat my beehives, smelters, smithing station, mayonnaise maker, and pickling barrels. I had full access to cows, ducks, chicken, horses, and sheep despite being early in the game, too.

Berdasarkan laporan, and all of this is for the good of the village. Well, assuming there's enough people left to live there when the future arrives. Regardless of how things play out, I'm frankly astonished at just how well Village in the Shade tells its story and wraps it around familiar farm-sim routines. With more crops, more money, and more goods, you can fulfill more requests and improve Kagatsu, giving it a better chance at surviving into the future. As we head into the twilight of 2026, this one definitely deserves a spot on the lists of the year's best games.

Grave Seasons captures the terror of small-town living.

Netflix's Away takes the idea of a mission to the Red Planet and fleshes it out on a more personal level by following a crew of astronauts as they try to make history while managing their relationships and obligations at home. Berdasarkan laporan, created by andrew hinderaker, away premiered on netflix in september 2020. Although the series was canceled after its first season, its 10 episodes tell a largely self-contained story about the first crewed mission to Mars. The journey takes three years, and the people aboard have much to lose before they reach their destination, making for a different kind of space drama that draws as much interest from people watching from Earth as from the astronauts traveling through space.

Sebagaimana diketahui, swank stars as emma green, a nasa astronaut selected to command the atlas, a spacecraft carrying an international crew on humanity's first mission to mars. They come from different backgrounds and have varying levels of experience, but they share the significant responsibility of getting to Mars alive.

Diungkapkan bahwa emma's appointment as commander is hardly straightforward, as some crew members question her leadership after an early emergency aboard the atlas, leaving her to earn their confidence while managing the demands of an increasingly dangerous expedition. They also face the challenge of keeping everyone alive for three years in a confined spacecraft. Equipment malfunctions, medical emergencies, and problems with the ship's essential systems put the mission at risk, forcing the astronauts to rely on one another even when their personal differences get in the way.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of the mission's most compelling aspects is its international nature. Every astronaut goes through a unique set of experiences that influence their relationships throughout the mission. Misha is a seasoned space traveler, with a lot of turbulence in his personal life as the price of his success. Kwesi is a newcomer to astronautics, with knowledge of botany and some faith beliefs that influence how he sees the mission.

Diungkapkan bahwa although this book has a central theme of the technological obstacles of space travel, much of the content focuses on events on earth. Matt is an ex-astronaut who was unable to join the expedition due to his medical problems and suffered a stroke shortly after Emma's departure. As a result, the family faces issues beyond the distance between Earth and Mars. Recovery includes both the difficult rehabilitation process for Matt while Lex is doing everything in her power to deal with the experiences of being a mother without her mother and caring for her father. Here, Matt Logan (Josh Charles), Emma's husband, and their daughter, Alexis “Lex” Logan (Talitha Bateman), must learn to cope without Emma. All Emma can do is accept that, unfortunately, she cannot simply abandon the mission every time something goes wrong at home.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, christopher nolan's interstellar explores the emotional consequences of space exploration through a father and daughter separated by an extraordinary journey. Away approaches a similar idea from a different family dynamic, with a mother attempting to reconcile her professional ambitions with her responsibilities as a parent. The separation is difficult for everyone involved, and the series gives those feelings considerable room to develop.

Diungkapkan bahwa of course, viewers looking for the relentless action of the martian should adjust their expectations. Away has its share of emergencies, including a damaged solar panel and a failing water reclamation system, but it often prioritizes the crew's emotional lives over the mechanics of survival. That's a deliberate choice, although it occasionally comes at the expense of the show's pacing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one thing prospective viewers should know before settling in for all 10 episodes is that away will not return for season 2; netflix canceled the series in october 2020, just weeks after its premiere. The decision was reportedly tied to production costs, with individual episodes costing about $6 million, despite the show's early streaming success.

Diungkapkan bahwa the good news is that the first season does give a certain amount of closure. The Atlas arrives at Mars, and the crew manages to pull through with the main mission goals. Although some characters have unresolved issues and contradictions that could be developed in the second season, they still get enough closure related to the mission itself.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for anyone who is interested in a show about astronauts who spend as much time thinking about their loved ones as performing operations in outer space, away is unsurprisingly worth watching. The show may struggle with pacing and its emotional core, and some of the emotional backstory may feel too sweet. Nevertheless, Swank and the other actors give the series a personality you can't help but appreciate.

Jamie remains a fan-favorite for a reason.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, many factors have helped make george r. The eight-season adaptation brought Martin’s vast, stunning world and complex central characters to life. Weiss. Jaime Lannister, played by Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, was one such character. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire one of the most beloved fantasy series of all time, and one big reason is HBO’s adaptation of the dark fantasy epic by showrunners David Benioff and D. R. B. And like many others in Game of Thrones, he had poetic one-liners that captured his nature and helped define his place in the story over the years.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, unlike ned stark, whose blunt and severe demeanor left little room for elaborate remarks, jaime lannister seemed to have an arsenal of memorable quotes and cutting one-liners. His words reflected both his standing as Tywin Lannister’s beloved son and as Lord Commander of the Kingsguard, as well as the complicated reputation he carried throughout Westeros. To many, Jaime was a man without honor, and his sharp remarks often seemed to echo the way others judged him.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with so many banger quotes from jaime, it’s tough to pick the best one. Still, we think we’ve narrowed it down to a line that captures a key part of Jaime’s character and a central fantasy theme.

Sebagaimana diketahui, of all the meaningful lines jaime delivers over game of thrones’ eight seasons, one perfectly highlights a key theme that often serves as a source of strength in stories, regardless of genre: love. Martin, however, twists that theme in a way that helps ensure Jaime goes down as one of fantasy’s most memorable characters.

In the show's first episode, “Winter is Coming,” Jaime delivers his best line to his sister, Cersei, shortly after Bran Stark, the youngest son of Ned Stark of House Stark, catches them locked in an incestuous romantic embrace in one of Winterfell's towers.

Turning to Cersei, Jaime gives a self-assured smirk and says:.

Moments later, Jaime pushes Bran out the open window — triggering a chain of events that leads to eight seasons of warfare, seedy politicking, and epic fantasy unlike anything ever seen before.

Diungkapkan bahwa love is a powerful emotion that drives stories across every genre and format. It is love that causes Jack to sacrifice himself for Rose in Titanic, and it is love that protects Harry from dying from Voldemort’s killing curse in Harry Potter.

Berdasarkan laporan, game of thrones may be a dark fantasy tale in which nobody is truly safe, but that does not mean its characters are one-dimensional. Both D&D and Martin have made it clear that even the most loathsome among them can feel love and form deep attachments.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, those feelings do not necessarily make them kinder or less dangerous. On the contrary, in some cases they will commit monstrous acts for the people they love. That is clearest with Jaime, who is capable of killing a boy if it means his secret relationship with Cersei isn’t exposed to the rest of Westeros.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, jaime committing heinous acts for the love of his sister proves just how obsessive and toxic that love can be. It’s only when Jaime realizes his sister cares more about power than about being with him that he eventually wises up.

Sebagaimana diketahui, unfortunately, jaime’s toxic bond with cersei has been a foundational part of him since childhood. Even when Jaime eventually leaves Cersei’s influence and forms a romantic relationship with Brienne of Tarth, sleeping with her after the Battle of Winterfell, it’s not enough. When Jaime hears of Cersei’s precarious situation in King’s Landing in the final season, he abandons Brienne and the Starks to rush back to the capital to try to save Cersei from her own folly.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ultimately, this final act of love for his sister leads to jaime’s downfall. Even as the Red Keep begins to crumble, Jaime refuses to leave Cersei’s side. They came into the world together, and so it only makes sense that they leave it together too.

Berdasarkan laporan, as aemond targaryen explained to jon snow in a game of thrones: “we are only human, and the gods have fashioned us for love. That is our great glory, and our great tragedy. ”.

#959. 7 Decades Later, the Most Satisfying Movie of All Time Is Free on YouTube

📅 15 Nov 2026

7 Decades Later, the Most Satisfying Movie of All Time Is Free on YouTube

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/12-angry-men-free-youtube/

It’s widely considered to be one of the greatest films ever made.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sometimes, all i’m looking for in a movie is a really great performance. I don’t need grand adventure or killer special effects or stakes so impossibly big that I can’t relate to them. I just want to be moved by an actor (and a script) with as few frills and distractions as possible. Currently, for free (with ads) on YouTube, there is a movie that contains no less than 12 of those kinds of great performances, and it's one of the most satisfying films ever made.

Sebagaimana diketahui, 12 angry men begins at the very end of a trial, just as the jury is about to go deliberate. The judge reminds the jury of their duty, and that the sentence for this person, if convicted, will be death. This is a murder case where a son is being accused of stabbing his father to death. Silently, the young man who barely looks to be out of high school looks at the jury and a couple of members look back. Then the jury goes off into the jury room.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the men pile in and take a few minutes to get settled, but once they do, the foreman suggests they take a vote to see where everyone stands. Of the 12-man jury, 11 of the men believe the man is guilty, while the 12th man is unsure. From there, the discussion unfolds about whether to convict or not.

That’s literally it, and that’s all you need.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to bring home my point about no frills, 95 percent of this black-and-white movie from 1957 takes place in the jury room (just the very beginning and the very end don’t). The movie is just 12 guys in a room talking and making their points, arguing, and revealing their prejudices. The characters don’t even have names, they’re just called “Juror 1,” “Juror 2,” etc. And while Henry Fonda, who plays the dissenting Juror 8, is the star of the movie with the most compelling performance, every single one of those characters is given something interesting to do and is a fully fleshed-out character in their own right.

Juror 1 is played by Martin Balsam, the foreman and the steady hand who leads the discussion, but even he finds himself shaken by the arguments that break out in the room.

Diungkapkan bahwa juror 2 is john fiedler, a character actor who may be best remembered as the voice of piglet. He’s an easygoing, seemingly weak man, but he learns to stand up for himself in the room, especially after he’s insulted or it’s revealed that bigotry is part of the reason why some of the men who agree with him want to convict.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, lee j. Cobb is Juror 3, a loudmouth jerk determined to convict. He’s easy to root against because of how obnoxious he is, but he becomes more and more sympathetic once you figure out the source of his anger had more to do with his own estranged son than it does with the accused.

Sebagaimana diketahui, juror 4 is played by e. Marshall. G. He’s a cold, analytical man who presents the best, most logical case for conviction.

Diungkapkan bahwa the odd couple’s jack klugman has one of the most sympathetic character arcs as juror 5. Like the young man whose life is in their hands, Klugman is a “slum kid” and he objects to the innuendos about the accused based on his social standing.

Juror 6, played by Edward Binns, is an understated blue-collar guy who is easy for the viewer to identify with.

Diungkapkan bahwa jack warden is the kind of character actor who makes you go, “oh, i know that guy,” even if you’re not sure from what. He was in The Great Muppet Caper as Kermit and Fozzie’s boss at the newspaper and in Dirty Work as Artie Lange’s dad. As Juror 7, he often steals the show by cracking jokes and making it very clear that he’s got tickets to a Yankee game after this and he really doesn’t want to miss it.

Diungkapkan bahwa then there’s the star of the film, henry fonda as juror 8. He states his points and, one by one, more people come to his side by bringing up their own points and even convincing themselves. He’s a principled, thoughtful man who originally dissents not because he’s sure of the innocence of the accused, but because he’s just not sure. His performance is moving and the arguments he makes are compelling, but the movie isn’t just him convincing everybody. He thinks, because this is a death penalty case, that they should take the time to discuss everything — a man’s life is at least worth that. It’s the unique kind of performance that is both commanding and, in many ways, quite subtle.

Juror 9 is Joseph Sweeney, an old man who is easy to overlook, but he makes some of the most profound observations about the trial.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, juror 10, played by ed begley, is a bigoted business owner who is determined to convict simply because of the defendant's unspecified ethnicity. (A key point to the case is that it took place in a New York City slum and the accused murderer is darker-skinned than everyone on the jury, which is incredibly relevant to how things proceed in the jury room. ).

Juror 11 is George Voskovec, a European watchmaker who also finds himself a target of some bigotry in the room.

Finally, Juror 12 is Robert Webber, an ad man who doesn't really care about the proceedings, but eventually rises to the occasion.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, written by reginald rose, 12 angry men was directed by master filmmaker sidney lumet, famous for films like dog day afternoon, serpico, network, and many others. 12 Angry Men was his directorial debut and he shows tremendous wisdom in just letting the actors do their thing. Relatively early in the movie, it becomes clear that the trajectory of the film is that each man changes their minds, one at a time. But the interesting part is the why of each man.

Sebagaimana diketahui, most compelling of all is to figure out when you, the viewer, switch sides. Going into the jury room, the majority is convinced of the man’s guilt because the case they just witnessed was convincing. The evidence appears to point in favor of conviction, and it's laid out, at first, to make sure the viewer is also on the side of conviction. But one by one, the men change their minds and the experience of watching the film is that you, at some point, change your mind, too.

#965. 25 Funniest 'Peanuts' Comics from the 1960s That Prove Charles M. Schulz Is Unbeatable

📅 15 Nov 2026

25 Funniest 'Peanuts' Comics from the 1960s That Prove Charles M. Schulz Is Unbeatable

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/funniest-peanuts-comics-1960s/

And maybe Charles Schulz’s funniest-ever story.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the year 1964 was an election year in america. Kennedy, Democratic President Lyndon Johnson was running for reelection on a platform of civil rights and combating poverty. His opponent was Republican Senator Barry Goldwater, who ran on a conservative platform of smaller government. After assuming office in late November 1963 following the assassination of President John F. Johnson ended up winning in a landslide with 61 percent of the popular vote and 44 out of 50 states voting for him.

As is the case with every presidential election year, the race was the number one news story, and it invaded many other aspects of American life, up to and including the immensely popular comic strip Peanuts, albeit in a very Peanuts-appropriate way.

Sebagaimana diketahui, beginning on oct. Linus even reaches 92 percent support in the polls at one point, but on Oct. Linus runs a pretty savvy campaign, conducting rousing speeches about the same nonsense real politicians do, talking about “moral decline” and other amorphous platitudes. 5, 1964, Charles Schulz launched a month-long story about Linus running for school president. His sister Lucy convinces him to run and acts as his campaign manager, while Charlie Brown becomes his running mate. 21, the campaign takes a shocking turn that changes everything.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the story is probably schulz’s funniest-ever long-running story. There are a lot of amusing political points that Schulz makes about our system, some of which still feel pretty prescient. The whole build-up to the big shift is a brilliant slow burn, while still being quite funny along the way. While most Peanuts comics work just fine out of context, this 25-day arc is best enjoyed in its entirety, to get the full effect (or at least some of the same effect) newspaper readers experienced back in 1964.

Perhaps Linus’ face in panel number three should have prepared people for where this story would go.

It’s pretty sad that teachers' salaries are still such an issue more than 60 years later.

Linus is officially nominated here by Schroeder, who can’t seem to skip an opportunity to bore people about Beethoven.

Berdasarkan laporan, linus’ acceptance speech puts up a serious red flag when he says he may do away with elections. This is one of those things that feels especially relevant in today’s political climate. I would not have taken Linus for a fascist.

Diungkapkan bahwa after his nomination and acceptance speech, linus brings in his vice presidential candidate, charlie brown. I think I agree with Lucy here when she says “Good Grief!” to the choice. I mean, just look at the Christmas special (which aired a year after this). Linus is an excellent, inspiring public speaker, while Charlie Brown can’t even direct that goofy little play or pick out a decent tree. He’s not meant for leadership.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i, for one, think linus should have nominated snoopy for vice president. Sure, it’s a gimmick, but there have been several times in US history where America would have been better off with a dog as VP (just look up a guy named Aaron Burr).

“The press is against me!” also feels like it could have run today with equal relevance.

Berdasarkan laporan, you may have noticed that this series skipped oct. 11. That’s because the Sunday strips had to be standalone, as many people only got Sunday papers. Also, because they were in color and had wider distribution, Sunday strips had to be completed much farther ahead than the daily strips.

This is just bad journalism on Violet’s part.

Berdasarkan laporan, linus’ propensity for religious fervor is so incredibly funny. What’s even funnier is how effective it is.

All of these ideas are super-solid and should happen in real life.

#966. 7 Prime Video Action Shows With No Bad Seasons, Ranked

7 Prime Video Action Shows With No Bad Seasons, Ranked

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, prime video has a fantastic slate of originals. And many of them fall into the action genre. In fact, some of its newest shows have counted among the most talked about this year. From secret spies to law enforcement, military men and women, superheroes and super not-so-heroes, ghouls, and villains, the list is extensive, the shows filled with memorable characters.

Sebagaimana diketahui, some shows waver and dip, losing their luster eventually and overstaying their welcome. But the best action shows on Prime Video don't have a single bad season among the bunch. Sure, two of them have only streamed one season so far. But these singular seasons were so incredibly entertaining, you won't be disappointed by watching them.

Berdasarkan laporan, not since thelma & louise have we had such a fun, female-centric buddy action adventure comedy like ride or die. Hannah Waddingham is a downright badass as elite assassin Judith Burton. She has hidden her identity from her best friend Deborah "Debbie" Claybourne (Octavia Spencer) since they became friends years prior. But current circumstances mean Debbie is in for a wild ride she never saw coming, and is going to be introduced to a side of her friend she didn't know existed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the series, one of the best prime video shows in 2026 so far, is so fun throughout its eight episodes. Sadly, Ride or Die was cancelled after its first season. The fact that two female actors lead the story is refreshing. It's as much a story of female friendship and dealing with childhood trauma as it is an action-packed show. But there are also fantastic fight sequences with engaging choreography, and intense physical and emotional moments. But it's a fantastic weekend binge-watch with the gal pals or partner that provides a satisfying ending.

Berdasarkan laporan, one of those enduring prime video shows that no one talks about, the legend of vox machina has streamed four seasons already and will be coming back for a fifth and final season. The adult animated fantasy series based on the first Dungeons & Dragons campaign called Critical Role, follows a seven-member team embarking on a mission to avenge the murder of their town's rulers. The story develops from there in subsequent seasons as the characters grow and the battles evolve.

Berdasarkan laporan, initially, the series was funded through a kickstarter campaign, yet it has since become one of prime video's most enduring originals. In her Season 4 review, Collider's Victoria Luxford says the show remains just as strong, a "funny, thrilling, and surprisingly deep fantasy series that balances fan service with a story that won't leave newcomers alienated. " Once you have powered through The Legend of Vox Machina, check out its spin-off/sequel series The Mighty Nein.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the most polarizing shows of this decade, the boys was set up to satirize the current political and societal landscape, and ended up becoming like a mirror of the times. Some of these powers are typical, like superhuman strength, speed, laser eyes, and invisibility. But others are more gruesome, vulgar, even offensive. The story in the satirical superhero series, a Prime Video show with no bad seasons, centers around an alternate world whereby humans live among those with superhuman abilities. And what these "Supes" do is nothing close to heroic: they're focused on feeding their egos and the pocketbook of the company that manages them, not actually helping others.

Diungkapkan bahwa the boys is subversive, politically commentative, and extremely violent. But some will appreciate the deep meaning masked behind blood, gore, and a record number of male appendages and expletives. If you dig in to the root of the show, it's actually one of the smartest shows on television. It isn't a show that everyone will like. Watch the entire five-season run and follow it up with the companion series Gen V.

Berdasarkan laporan, i might be in the minority, but i actually like neagley better than reacher. But she's also just as rebellious and against the rules as her friend Reacher is. And with a Season 2 renewal, it will likely get even better. The character of Frances Neagley (Maria Sten), who is first introduced in Reacher, is much more layered than Reacher fans realized. He knows she will have his back and will always be two steps ahead, able to anticipate what he might need. She shows up on that show as a trusted confidante, someone Jack Reacher (Alan Ritchson) knows he can count on to get the job done, no matter how challenging. Both shows are fantastic, but Neagley came out of the gate strong with its first season. This is emphasized in Neagley where Frances is clearly valued at the private investigation firm where she works. The ensemble nature of the show introduces conflicting personalities that come together to form sort of a ragtag team.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the story in season 1 follows frances' investigation into the death of an old friend, which leads her to a dangerous cult and strange experiments. It has all the elements you'd expect from a good action crime show, including intense hunts, lots of engaging fight scenes, and emotional backstories that draw you into the characters themselves, not just the plot.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, having only just recently binged all of reacher, the show's flow is still fresh in my mind. The later seasons are arguably better than the first two, but there still isn't a bad season among the bunch. Season 1 sets up Ritchson as the first actor to truly embody the character as he is in the Lee Child books. The stakes rise higher in Season 2, and the personal connection to the cases grows and becomes more intimate with each passing season.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the action and intensity is amped up in later seasons, too, with some of the most intriguing villains. If you love action shows, Reacher is among the best, with a protagonist who towers over his prey, doesn't flinch when he has to kill a bad guy, yet has the softest heart and strongest moral code. The fact that the action crime drama has so much source material to work from with Child having written 31 novels about the character to date, there's no shortage of exciting stories from which to draw. With at least two more seasons already confirmed, it's a good time to binge-watch the show and catch up on all the literal action.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mark grayson (steven yeun) just wants to be a regular teenager, but he doesn't have that chance. He's the son of the most powerful superhero on Earth, Omni-Man (J. K. That means honing his skills now that he's coming of age and his latent powers are starting to show up. Simmons), so he has a duty to serve. That's the set-up for the story in Invincible, an adult animated superhero series from Robert Kirkman that has become a huge pop culture phenomenon.

Diungkapkan bahwa even though it's animated, invincible is very violent, gruesome, and graphic, so this isn't necessarily a show to watch with young kids. But the show is completely bingeable and addictive, adding depth to an otherwise thin story of good guys versus bad. The stories are also quite mature. Earning widespread acclaim, Invincible has already been renewed for two more seasons, continuing the story as Mark grapples with a shocking truth about his dad and fighting an evil group looking to conquer Earth.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the action doesn't start immediately in fallout, but when it does, it happens in a big way. It begins with a betrayal in an underground bunker and expands to include the Earth above where there's nothing but conflict. Based on the video game franchise of the same name, Fallout follows Lucy (Ella Purnell) and her journey to find her kidnapped father, leaving the safety of her underground home for the first time. And the Prime Video show hooks you in the first five minutes. She comes across interesting and dangerous people, including The Ghoul (Walton Goggins), who has an interesting backstory and who is on a mission that eventually overlaps with Lucy's.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, you'll see everything from radroaches (giant, mutated cockroaches) attacking humans to robots, men in robotic armor, mutated creatures, undead ghouls, and a lot of eccentric personalities as people do whatever they can to survive in this post-apocalyptic world. The show wonderfully introduces new groups and characters each season while the journeys of Lucy and The Ghoul make progress and eventually come together. With only two seasons so far and a third on the way, considering there are five main video game stories and six spin-offs or mobile titles, there's lots more story to tell. If you like seeing unique fight scenes that you won't see in any other show, Fallout won't disappoint.

Diungkapkan bahwa wordle is a daily word-guessing game that tasks players with solving a five-word puzzle using letter position clues.
